                        June      22,       39.
1.

ARREST OF C.D.C. 279 BY ARMED MEMBERS
OF TIH SUH CHUNG (鐵血軍).
======================================

For the purpose of verifying an address given by
a suspect in a larceny case brought to the Bubbling Well
Station by C.P.O. 1365 at 6.15 a.m. June 22, 1939.
C.D.C. 279 was despatched by D.S. 252 Weeks to Lane 1421,
House 5, Yu Yuen Road.

The C.D.C. proceeded by station car and alighted
at the entrance to the alleyway. He was looking for
the number of the alleyway standing on the Yu Yuen Road
footpath when two male Chinese, who were standing at the
entrance to the alleyway suddenly threatened him with
mauser pistols. The detective thinking they were
highway robbers offered them money. The suspected
robbers pulled the detective into the alleyway and there
searched him and upon finding that he was armed accused
him of being a traitor. At this juncture the two
suspects were re-enforced by about 20 other armed men.
The C.D.C. was subjected to interrogation and then
marched away to a Chinese style house in the Zau Ka Yi
village situated between Edinburgh and Great Western
Roads.

At 8.05 a.m. June 22, Inspector Yao Kyia Kwei
received a telephone message from Lee Shih Chung (李石崇)
living at Lane 95, House 10 Edinburgh Road, C.C.L.
pages.zh:
副总监办公室
“B”分区

“B”区
杂项编号 335/39.         静安寺
                        1939年6月22日
1.

中国侦探警员（C.D.C.）279号被铁血军武装成员逮捕。
======================================

为核实一名盗窃案嫌疑人在1939年6月22日上午6时15分由中央巡捕房（C.P.O.）1365号带至静安寺捕房时所供出的地址，
副巡长（D.S.）252号威克斯（Weeks）派遣中国侦探警员（C.D.C.）279号前往愚园路1421弄5号。

该侦探警员乘坐警车前往，并在弄堂入口处下车。当他站在愚园路人行道上寻找弄堂门牌号码时，两名站在弄堂入口处的中国男子突然用毛瑟手枪威胁他。该侦探以为他们是拦路抢劫的匪徒，便向他们交出钱财。这两名疑似劫匪将该侦探拖入弄堂内并进行搜身，在发现其携带武器后，指控他为汉奸。此时，另有约20名武装男子前来增援这两名嫌疑人。该中国侦探警员受到审问，随后被押往位于爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）与大西路（Great Western Road）之间的曹家义村（Zau Ka Yi village）的一处中式房屋。

1939年6月22日上午8时05分，姚基贵（Yao Kyia Kwei）巡官接到居住在爱丁堡路95弄10号的李石崇（Lee Shih Chung）打来的电话留言，李石崇系中央捕房线人（C.C.L.）。

pages.en:
Misc.No.335/39.
1/2.

informing the Inspector that a detective attached to
Bubbling Well Station had been arrested by a gang of men
and he would effect the release of the detective as a
mistake had been made,
In consequence of this message D.I. Tabrum, Inspr.
Yao Kyin Kwei and D.S. Weeks promptly proceeded to Lane
95, House 10 Edinburgh Road.
Upon arrival at the lane leading to this house,
the Police party noticed several armed men standing in
the alleyway. Evidently the Police party were expected
as the iron door leading to the compound of the house
was promptly opened to admit them.
Upon entering the compound, the Police were confron-
ted by about 30 men all armed with mauser pistols. The
gate-keeper was armed with a mauser fitted with an
automatic stock.
The Police party were escorted to a large room on
the ground-floor. They were received in a very friendly
manner by Lee Shih Chung who introduced the 10 or 12
men present, some of whom were armed. Included in these
introduced were Sung Tsocng Mei (沈忠美), Zee Wen Ocn
(徐文安), a Mr. Chu and one named Lee Yih Fei (李飛).
The last named, according to information of Bubbling
Well detectives was shot by Inspector Dudley and D.S.I.
Tilton when participating in an Armed Robbery at No.5
pages.zh:
杂项第335/39号。
1/2.

通知督察称，一名隶属于静安寺捕房的侦探已被一伙人逮捕，他将安排释放该侦探，因为此前发生了误会，

鉴于此消息，副督察塔布伦（Tabrum）、姚金贵督察（Yao Kyin Kwei）和警佐威克斯（Weeks）迅速前往爱丁堡路95弄10号。

当抵达通往该房屋的弄堂时，警方人员注意到巷内有数名持枪男子站立。显然警方人员的到来已在预期之中，因为通往该房屋院落的铁门随即打开，让他们进入。

进入院落之后，警方遭遇了约30名全部配备毛瑟手枪的男子。看门人配备有一支装有自动枪托的毛瑟手枪。

警方人员被护送至一楼的一间大房间。李世忠（Lee Shih Chung）以非常友好的态度接待了他们，并介绍了在场的十余人，其中部分人携带武器。在被介绍的人员中包括沈忠美（Sung Tsocng Mei）、徐文安（Zee Wen Ocn）、一位朱先生以及一名叫李飞（Lee Yih Fei）的人。据静安寺捕房侦探提供的情报，最后提到的这名李飞曾在参与第5号的一处武装抢劫案时，被达德利（Dudley）督察和蒂尔顿（Tilton）副督察开枪击中

pages.en:
Misc.No.335/39.
1/3.

Fah Wah Sing Tsung off Rockhill Avenue, Misc.No.207/39
(BW) and later removed to Lane 95, House 10 Edinburgh
Road in Lee Shih Chung's M/car. During the discussion
Lee Tih Fei openly admitted being shot three times
and showed the Police the scars on his body resulting
from the bullet wounds he received. He was shot twice
in the back and once in the buttocks.

Lee Shih Chung who was previously unknown to any
of the visiting Police is a man of small stature, aged
about 35/6. He claims to be the owner of a steamship
line and also the owner of a Native Bank on Kiukiang
Road. He is a loquacious talker and desires to give
the impression that he is a man of great power. In
response to many questions concerning himself and the
numerous armed men surrounding him, he stated in
principle, that he had was a man of such power that he
was not subject either to the rule of the Japanese
or members of the Shanghai City Government. He had
under him between 700 or 800 men, most of whom, he
stated had been recruited from the villages in the
Western Area of Shanghai. This organization, he
called the Tih Suh Chung (Iron Colour Corps) (鐵血軍
50 of whom act as bodyguards to himself.
pages.zh:
杂项卷宗第335/39号。
1/3.

法华生（Fah Wah Sing，音译）从罗克希尔路（Rockhill Avenue）被带离，涉及杂项卷宗第207/39号（BW），随后由李士忠（Lee Shih Chung）的汽车送往爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）95弄10号。在谈话期间，李铁飞（Lee Tih Fei，音译）公开承认曾中弹三次，并向警方展示了枪伤留下的疤痕。他背部中了两枪，臀部中了一枪。

李士忠此前不为任何到访警员所知，身材矮小，年龄约35至36岁。他声称自己是一家轮船公司的所有者，同时也是九江路上一家华资银行的所有者。他健谈，并试图给人留下其拥有巨大权势的印象。在回答许多关于他本人及其周围众多武装人员的问题时，他原则上表示，他的权势之大，使其既不受日本人统治，也不受上海市政府成员的管辖。他手下有七八百人，据称大多是从上海西部地区（Western Area）的村庄招募而来。他将此组织称为“铁血军”（Tih Suh Chung，即 Iron Colour Corps），其中50人担任他的保镖。

pages.en:
Misco. No. 335/39.
1/4.

Questioned as to the expenses for the upkeep of
this organization, Lee stated they are at present
poorly supported but when they need funds he provides
them.

The object of this organization, Lee stated, is
to eliminate members of pro-Chinese assassination
groups. Lee even went so far as to say that C.D.C. 279 would have been executed if it had not have been for the
fact that he was able to establish his identity by virtue
of the fact that he had a S.M.P. Warrant Card and S.M.P.
pistol and was later proved to be a member of the S.M.P.

Lee proposed that his organization be accorded
friendly treatment by detectives at Bubbling Well
Station with whom he expressed a desire to co-operate
for the specific purpose of exterminating members of
pro-Chinese assassination groups. He further stated
that as Police at Bubbling Well Station were responsible
for law and order in territory under the jurisdiction
of the S.M.C. in the Western Area that he be afforded
all possible protection.

Lee concluded the discussion which had lasted more
than one hour by stating that within a month or two
from now Mr. Wang Ching Wei would probably come to
Shanghai and there would be peace and quietness in the
Western Area of Shanghai.
pages.zh:
杂项卷宗第335/39号。
1/4.

当被问及维持该组织的费用时，李表示目前资金支持不足，但当他们需要资金时，他会提供。

李称，该组织的目的是消灭亲华暗杀团体的成员。李甚至进一步表示，如果不是因为他凭借持有工部局警务处（S.M.P.）委任证和工部局警务处手枪而得以确立身份，且后来被证实为工部局警务处成员的话，刑事侦缉处编号279的警员（C.D.C. 279）本已被处决。

李提议，静安寺捕房（Bubbling Well Station）的侦探应对其组织给予友好对待，他表示希望与该捕房合作，专门旨在消灭亲华暗杀团体的成员。他进一步表示，由于静安寺捕房的警察负责维持工部局（S.M.C.）在上海西部地区管辖范围内的法律与秩序，因此他应获得一切可能的保护。

李在持续了一个多小时的谈话结束时表示，在一两个月内，汪精卫先生可能会来到上海，上海西部地区将会恢复和平与安宁。

pages.en:
Misc.No. 335/39.
1/8.

During the discussion Sergeant Major Shida
entered the room, he was greeted in a friendly manner
by all. He left after a few minutes, not knowing the
reason for presence of the S.M.P. Lee stated as he was
not obliged to tell Sergeant Major Shida, whom he would
not inform of the incident.

Some of the men the Police saw and were introduced
to at Lee's residence were students between 20 and 25
years of age. Others were of the robber and loafer type.

The C.D.C. was handed over to D.I. Tabrum together
with his pistol and Warrant Card at about 10.15a.m.
With the exception of being scared the detective had
not been injured in anyway.

After returning to the Station, Inspector
Yamaguchi approached D.I. Tabrum and asked if there had
been any trouble at Lane 95, House 10 Edinburgh Road.
He explained that Sergeant Major Shida had just phoned
for information and stated that to approach this
particular house was very dangerous and, that he had
received instructions from a high authority to cause
the arrest of all unauthorized persons found in the
vicinity thereof.

Inspector Yamaguchi was told that Police went on
a friendly visit at the request of Lee Shih Chung.

D. I. Tabrum
Det. Inspector.
pages.zh:
杂项卷宗第335/39号。
1/8.

在谈话期间，志田（Shida，音译）巡佐进入房间，所有人都友好地向他致意。几分钟后他离开，并不知晓工部局警务处人员在场的原因。李表示，他没有义务告诉志田巡佐，因此不会将此事告知他。

警方在李的住所见到并被介绍认识的人员中，有一些是20至25岁的学生。其他人则属于强盗和游手好闲之徒的类型。

上午10点15分左右，刑事侦缉处编号279的警员（C.D.C.）连同其手枪和委任证被移交给侦探督察塔布鲁姆（D.I. Tabrum）。除受到惊吓外，该侦探未受任何伤害。

回到捕房后，山口（Yamaguchi，音译）督察走近侦探督察塔布鲁姆，询问爱丁堡路95弄10号是否发生了麻烦。他解释说，志田巡佐刚刚打电话来询问情况，并称接近这所特定的房子非常危险，且他已收到上级指示，要逮捕在该区域附近发现的所有未经授权的人员。

山口督察被告知，警方是应李士忠的请求进行友好访问的。

塔布鲁姆
侦探督察

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / OCT 25 / 1939 / DETECTIVE CORPS / SPECIAL BRANCH）

A number of the members of the Special
Service Corps of Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern
and National Salvation Army attached to the branch
office at 1081 Jessfield Road, O.O.L., who escaped
from the premises by way of the back door following
a number of their colleagues firing on a Municipal
Police party in front of the house on the early
morning of October 22, returned to the office on
October 23, 1939. Eleven of the members who
participated in shooting at the police and who were
subsequently taken into custody by the Japanese
Gendarmes and escorted to the Western District
Japanese Military Police Headquarters, 94 Jessfield
Road, were released and are now accommodated at
No.1, Yung Sz Faung (永思坊), Kong Kya Jao, off
Jessfield Road, O.O.L., another branch office of
the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang
Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army.

C. Crawford
D. I.

D.C. (Special Branch).

FILE

The four workers who were arrested by
members of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern
and National Salvation Army attached to the Branch
Office situated at No. 12 Yung Loh Tsung, Jessfield
Road, O.C.L., on October 7 from the Dao Hwa Silk
Factory, No. 37, South Zao Ka Za Village, off
Brenan Road, O.O.L., and the Tuh Dah Silk Factory,
No. 87 in the same village, were released after the
management of the two factories had each paid a

（印：COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 23 SEP. 1939）

Under the auspices of the Zao Ka Doo Merchants
Street Union, a dinner party was held in house 1081
Jessfield Road, O.C.L., at 7.30 p.m. September 19,
in honour of the members of the Special Service Corps
of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang and Anti-Comintern and
National Salvation Army attached to the branch office
at the above address. A total of some 40 business
men residing in Zao Ka Doo, including Ao Pah Dong
(夏伯棠), a committee member of the Zao Ka Doo
Merchants Street Union, and Hwang Tse Woo (黄致和),
ex-Commander of the now defunct Zao Ka Doo Merchants
Volunteer Corps, and some 50 members of the foresaid
Special Service Corps were present.

Ao Pah Dong, presided, and delivered a brief
speech expressing gratitude on behalf of the hosts
to the members of the corps for their good work in
the maintenance of peace and order. After the arrival
of the corps in Zao Ka Doo, Ao alleged, conditions in
the area had gradually returned to normalcy and
residents and merchants had been able to lead a more
peaceful and tranquil life. In conclusion, he stated
that the merchants and residents, as a token of their
gratitude, were arranging to present a seasonal gift
to the corps about the middle of the 8th Moon
(September 27).

Hwang Tse Woo, ex-Commander of the now defunct
Zao Ka Doo Merchants Volunteer Corps, then took the

Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-

days.

the restoration of the Merchants Volunteer Corps with
a two-fold aim:-

members of the corps are protectors of the merchants

1. 使曹家渡商人相信，该队成员是商人的保护者，不应因其多为前科犯而受到蔑视和恐惧。

Comintern and National Salvation Army.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Macadie

It is reported that a number of the members of
the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang
Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army, 76 Jessfield
Road, have been assigned to carry out observation duty
along Jessfield Road with the object of (1) ascertaining
the exact strength of the S.S.C. detailed for duty in
that thoroughfare (2) watching their movements; any
searches and arrests in Jessfield Road near the Head-
quarters of the Corps (76 Jessfield Road) are to be
reported immediately to the Headquarters. These
members are to be disguised as hawkers and labourers
while carrying out observation in the street.

In the afternoon of September 10, the shop
mistress and two assistants of Hwang Yuen Tai Cigarette
Shop (黄元泰) situated in Ho Loo Jao, off Jessfield
Road, were arrested by members of the Corps on suspicion
of having copied down the licence numbers of motor cars
entering and leaving House 76 Jessfield Road, which is
opposite to and some 10 yards south of the shop. The
three persons are being detained at 76 Jessfield Road,
pending investigations.

R. W. Macadie
D. S. I.

Made by....................and....................Forwarded by....................D.I. Crawford

On the morning of September 1, 1939, three
members of the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo
Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army
called at the Kan Kung (幹公) Primary School, 121
Brenan Road, O.O.L. (within perimeter) and demanded
that the school evacuate and hand over the premises to
the Corps for the accommodation of its members. This
school, which has a total of some 1,000 students,
refused to comply with the demand on the grounds that
the evacuation would cause the students to suspend their
studies at least for the present semester as the school
is not in a position to find other accommodation in such
a short period.

After negotiations with the Corps by Wu Tsung
Yuen (吳宗瑗), principal of the school, it was agreed
that the hall and the recreation ground instead of the
whole premises be taken over only.

On September 3, a number of workers employed by
the Corps visited the school and commenced taking
measurements for the construction on the recreation
ground of huts which, it is reported, will provide
accommodation for some 1,000 members of the Corps.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 15 SEPT. 1939）

E
It is reported from a reliable source that at
6 p.m. August 27, a dinner party took place on the
premises of the Special Service Corps of the Chung
Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Com'intern and National Salvation
Army at 76 Jessfield Road, O.O.L., under the auspices
of Ting Muh Tsung (丁默村) and Li Shih Chung
(李士), Director and Assistant Director of the
Corps when some 30 Japanese and Chinese journalists
attended. During the proceedings, Ting Muh Tsung
addressed the attendance stating that Wang Ching-wei
had gallantly taken upon himself the responsibility
of devising ways and means to settle the Sino-Japanese
hostilities by peaceful means mainly through a wish
to relieve the Chinese people of the sufferings which
they had endured as a result of the war. In view of
the tense situation now prevailing in Europe, Ting
continued, there appeared an urgent necessity for
Wang to speed up the object of forming a new regime
in China, which would be administered in accordance
with the peace principles. In conclusion, Ting
solicited the assistance of the attendance in connec-
tion with the peace campaign and asserted that the
assistance of journalists was always of first impor-
tance in the realization of a political movement.
The names of the journalists present and the
papers which they represented cannot be ascertained
as Ting Muh Tsung and Li Shih Chung personally arranged
the dinner party.

R.W. Gale.

由于晚宴由丁默村和李士(音译)亲自安排，无法查明出席记者的姓名及其所代表的报社。

Subject Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern
and National Salvation Army.
Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

Tenants of three of the twenty houses in the
Hwa Tsung alleyway, Jessfield Road, who failed to
remove on August 24, as instructed by the Special
Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern
and National Salvation Army at 76 Jessfield Road, were
ejected on the morning of August 25, 1939, by three
Chinese members of the corps who were each armed with
a Mauser pistol.

It is reported from a reliable source that some
2,000 men consisting chiefly of ex-guerrilla members
who hitherto operated in the suburbs of Shanghai have
been bought over by the corps and after reorganization,
will be despatched to the Western District of Shanghai.
The first batch of these men, numbering some 500, it
is reported, are due to arrive towards the end of
September and the houses in the Hwa Tsung alleyway
on reconditioning will be made into billets for those
people.

The members of the Special Service Corps of the
Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National
Salvation Army have given the people in the Western
District to know that garrison duties in the entire
Western District and its suburbs at present undertaken
by the Japanese Authorities will be handed over to
them in the near future.

C. Crawford
D. I.

A.C. (Special Branch).

FRENCH POLICE INTELLIGENCE REPORT

Shanghai, August 25, 1939.

A pro-Wang Ching-wei organ.

Hwa Tsung Alley, Lane No.455, Jessfield Road, is
adjacent to Lane No.453 on the same road (S.M.C. No.76) in
which lives Li Shih-cheng, Chief of the "Chinese Kuomintang
Headquarters of the Special Service for the Suppression of
Communism and National Salvation" (a pro-Wang Ching-wei organ).

As a measure of precaution, Li Shih-cheng has
requested the Western District Section of the Japanese
Gendarmerie to drive away the residents in Hwa Tsung Alleyway.
Yesterday policemen of the City Government Police Bureau
proceeded to the alleyway and warned tenants to remove within
one week. In the afternoon, a number of tenants had already
vacated their premises.

Pawnshops raise interest on pledges.

The Pawnbrokers Guild, 250 Burkill Road, has decided
to raise, as from September 1, the rate of interest on loans
from 1.8% to 2%.

1. Chow Fu Hai is a native of Hunan, age 42.
He received education in the Imperial University of Tokio. Returning to China he became a professor in the Kwangtung University at Canton and Wuhan University at Wuchang. He was subsequently appointed secretary to Headquarters of the Commander-in-Chief of the Nationalist Army, Chief Secretary to the Central Military and Political Academy, elected member of the Central Executive Committee since 1931, appointed member to the Kiangsu Provincial Government in 1935-1936, concurrently as Commissioner of Education of the Government. He has a large circle of friends amongst the educationalists, especially in this province.

In January 1939 he joined Waung Ching Wei in the peace movement. His surrender to the pro-Japanese cause was a surprise to Chungking officials as he had always received favourable treatment from Chiang Kai-shek. He came to Shanghai long before the arrival of Waung Ching Wei and undertook all preparations and organizations for peace talks. He is at present in charge of the Propaganda Department and is considered the most senior man amongst Waung's followers.

2. Ting Meh Pong is probably Ting Muh Chun (丁默村), a native of Wusih, age about 40. He was not known to the Police until 1933 when he came to Shanghai assisting the Nanking Political agent in the campaign against communists in Shanghai. He was then

It is reported from a reliable source that
members of the Special Service Corps of the Chung
Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation
Army have been instructed to procure and store as
much food stuff as possible as a precautionary measure
against a possible blockade of Shanghai by the Japanese
authorities in the near future. According to a
number of senior members of the Corps, a blockade is
bound to be effected sooner or later in order to compel
the Chinese living in the foreign settlements to leave
there. By doing so the Japanese will ultimately
starve the foreign interests in China.

At 4.30 p.m. August 23, Hsia Tsao (夏超),
Kuo Tsung Woo (郭忠和) and two other members of
the No.4 Execution Group of the Special Service Corps
of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National
Salvation Army, No.1 Zung Woo Li (人和里), Kong Kya
Jac, off Jessfield Road, O.C.L., called at the "Black
& White Dry-cleaning and Dyeing Shop", 666 Yu Yuen Road,
O.C.L., and took away the proprietor Hu Zoong Peng
(胡崇本), aged 39, a native of Ningpo. The four
members were armed with pistols when they visited the
shop.

cleaning and Dyeing Shop", 666 Yu Yuen Road, was

POLICE FORCE
REGISTRY
No. B. D. 9236 (8)39
21 AUG 1939
Translation of letter to Mr. Franklin,
Chairman of Council, from Tseu Yan-pei
(海佛周) and Ting Meh-pong (邦默丁).
Dated 17th August, 1939.
Address: No. 76, Jessfield Road.

Newspapers, etc,: Police attitude objected to.
The Chung'ing Government, under the forcible control
of Communists and semi-Communists, is now pursuing a perverse
policy tending to drive the Chinese people towards an
inextricable doom. All Chinese are deeply indignant about this.
To save our country, our Party and our people from the
present crisis, Mr. Wang Ching-wei, Vice-Chairman of the
Kuomintang, has resolutely opposed Communism and advocated
peace. With the exception of Communists, all quarters have
expressed profound sympathy with the stand taken by Mr. Wang;
this fact, we trust, is also well-known to the Council Chairman.
The Council's Police Department, however, have adopted
an unjust, non-neutral, unfriendly and discriminating attitude
towards us, and have unreasonably oppressed us as if we were
their enemies. The following particulars may be pointed out
as proofs:
1. The S.M. Police have not only failed to prevent Chinese
language newspapers in the International Settlement from
opposing Mr. Wang Ching-wei and his views, and from frequently
publishing reports which are without any foundation, but have
afforded those papers careful protection with large parties of
heavily armed Detectives and Constables. This has caused
these newspapers to be more aggressive in the tone of their
editorials and to publish more untruthful news. This is the
first point.
2. Because the Police have not arrested all terrorists, but
have allowed them to take shelter in the Settlement, their
activities have recently much increased. The Police therefore
are guilty of negligence. This is the second point.

警察部队
登记处
编号 B. D. 9236 (8)39
1939年8月21日
周海佛（Tseu Yan-pei）和丁邦默（Ting Meh-pong）
致工部局董事会主席富兰克林先生信函的译文。
日期：1939年8月17日。
地址：极司菲尔路76号。

报纸等：对警方态度表示反对。
重庆政府在共产党和半共产党人的武力控
制下，目前正推行一种违背常理的政策，
倾向于将中国人民推向无法解脱的厄运。
所有中国人对此深感愤慨。为了拯救我们
的国家、我们的党和我们的人民脱离当前
危机，国民党副总裁汪精卫先生坚决反对
共产主义并倡导和平。除共产党人外，各
界人士均对汪先生所持立场表示深切同情；
我们相信，这一事实也为董事会主席所熟知。
然而，工部局警务处对我们采取了不公正、
非中立、不友好且带有歧视性的态度，并
不合理地压迫我们，仿佛我们是他们的敌
人。以下细节可作为证明：
1. 上海公共租界警务处不仅未能阻止国际
租界内的中文报纸反对汪精卫先生及其观点，
并频繁刊登毫无根据的报道，反而派遣大批
全副武装的侦探和巡捕对这些报纸予以严密
保护。这导致这些报纸在社论语气上更加激
进，并刊登更多不实新闻。这是第一点。
2. 由于警方并未逮捕所有恐怖分子，而是允
许他们在租界内藏身，他们的活动近期大幅
增加。因此，警方犯有疏忽之罪。这是第二点。

pages.en:
3. Under the direction of Mr. Robertson of the S.M. Police,
eight Chinese, working in three shifts, have been ordered to
pick up telephone messages to and from No. 76 Jessfield Road
throughout the day and night. This is the third point.
4. During the last half month armed police and cars mounted
with guns have been sent to keep a careful watch in the
neighbourhood of No. 76 Jessfield Road. Persons connected
with us have been subjected to searches. This is the fourth
point.
The above particulars are sufficient proofs that the S.M.
Police are unjust towards us and are not neutral. We know, however,
that the Chairman and his honorable country have always been
strictly impartial in their attitude and have a deep aversion
towards Communists. Will the Chairman please give careful attention
to the above points.
We beg to submit the following proposals for the Council's
consideration:
1. All armed detectives and policemen detailed to protect
various newspaper offices should be withdrawn, and the offices should
be warned not to attack in future the views advocated by Mr. Wang.
2. If the police officers are not promptly withdrawn, then
the newspaper offices must cease to attack the views and written
articles of Mr. Wang; if the newspapers refuse to comply, the
Council must withdraw police protection.
3. The Police Department should be instructed to effectively
suppress the activities of terrorists in the Settlement and to
refuse them shelter. As soon as any report is received from us,
the Police should do its utmost to have the persons concerned
apprehended so that terrorism may be completely eradicated. When
a terrorist is arrested, and there is sufficient evidence to prove
him to be such, he should be handed over to us to be dealt with.
If there is no evidence against him, a further investigation should
be conducted jointly by the Police and ourselves, and an arrangement
should be made as how to deal with the man; he should not be
pages.zh:
3. 在上海公共租界警务处罗伯逊先生
（Mr. Robertson）的指挥下，八名华人分
三班倒，被命令日夜监听进出极司菲尔路
76号的电话信息。这是第三点。
4. 在过去半个月里，武装警察和装有枪支
的车辆被派往极司菲尔路76号附近严密监
视。与我们有关的人员遭到搜查。这是第四点。
上述细节足以证明上海公共租界警务处对
我们不公且不中立。然而，我们知道主席
及其尊贵的国家始终秉持严格公正的态度，
并对共产党人深恶痛绝。恳请主席对上述
各点予以密切关注。
我们谨提出以下建议供工部局考虑：
1. 应撤走派驻各报社保护的所有武装侦探
和警察，并警告各报社今后不得攻击汪先生
所倡导的观点。
2. 如果警察不及时撤走，那么各报社必须
停止攻击汪先生的观点和文章；如果报纸拒
绝遵守，工部局必须撤回警察保护。
3. 应指令警务处有效镇压租界内恐怖分子
的活动，并拒绝为其提供庇护。一旦收到我
们的任何报告，警方应尽最大努力逮捕相关
人员，以便彻底根除恐怖主义。当恐怖分子
被捕，且有充分证据证明其为恐怖分子时，
应将其移交给我们要进行处理。如果没有针
对他的证据，应由警方和我们共同进行进一
步调查，并就如何处理此人做出安排；未经

pages.en:
-3-

released without our consent.

4. The Police to be instructed not to send men in future
to pick up telephone messages to and from house No. 76,
Jessfield Road, so that we may not be deprived of the freedom
of speech.

5. Armed police officers posted near premises No. 76,
Jessfield Road, should be withdrawn and persons having connexions
with us should not be searched.

The above mentioned proposals are very reasonable and
lawful. We hope that they will receive the Council's careful
consideration and will be duly adopted. Should our proposals
be adopted, we guarantee that hereafter no action will be taken
by us in the Settlement. If our proposals are rejected and
the Police officers are still to be used as tools for other
people, we shall not be responsible for the occurrence of
untoward incidents which may undermine the peace and good
order of the Settlement.

(Signed) Tseu Vah-hei
Ting Meh-pong

(Note: Received for translation late p.m. 18th August, 1939)

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL TRANSLATION OFFICE）
pages.zh:
-3-

我们同意，不得释放。

4. 应指令警方今后不再派人监听极司菲尔
路76号住宅的电话往来，以免我们被剥夺
言论自由。

5. 应撤走部署在极司菲尔路76号 premises 
附近的武装警察，且不得搜查与我们有关联
的人员。

上述建议非常合理且合法。我们希望它们能
得到工部局的仔细考虑并被适时采纳。如果
我们的建议被采纳，我们保证此后不在租界
内采取任何行动。如果我们的建议被拒绝，
且警察仍被用作他人的工具，我们将不对可
能破坏租界和平与良好秩序的不幸事件的发
生承担责任。

（签名）周海佛（Tseu Vah-hei）
丁邦默（Ting Meh-pong）

Ching Wei Armed Gang to remove.
Made by. and Forwarded by. D. I. Crawford

Vide Sp.Br.
report dated
17/8/39.

The tenants of some 200 houses in Hwa Tsung
Alleyway, Jessfield Road, situated immediately north
of the office of the Special Service Corps of the Chung
Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation
Army, 76 Jessfield Road, were instructed by the corps
to vacate their premises at the beginning of August.
The occupants of the premises concerned ignored this
order and on August 20, a notice was posted at the
entrance of the alleyway warning the tenants to remove
before August 25, failing which, the notice asserted,
they would be ejected by force.

This block of houses (Hwa Tsung Alleyway) is the
property of one Koo Ping Sung (顧炳生), residing at
453, Jessfield Road, O.O.L.. Early in August he was
approached by representatives of the Corps who demanded
that the premises concerned be leased to them. Under
fear that a refusal of the demand would entail trouble
from the Corps, Koo, it is said, agreed to lease the
houses to the organization on condition that the latter
would accept the responsibility of persuading or compell-
ing the tenants to vacate.

Date August 18, 1939.
Subject. Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and
National Salvation Army - sub-office at 1081 Jessfield Road, C.C.I.
Made by: and Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

It is reported that Kuomintang party flags and
a portrait of the late Dr. Sun Yat Sen, founder of the
Kuomintang, are being exhibited inside the sub-office
of the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang
Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army situated at
No. 1081 Jessfield Road, C.C.I. with the object of
convincing the members and the public that the corps
is a "Kuomintang" organization and not a traitorous
body.

During the past few days, members of this sub-
office, some of whom are armed with pistols, were
patrolling the Jessfield Area. A number of alleged
thieves, and persons involved in brawls and other petty
crimes were taken into custody and detained in the office
but they were invariably released after a certain amount
of money was paid. These members were not interfered
in their operations by the Western District Police
Bureau but instead appear to be there with the connivance
of the bureau.

It is reported that members of this sub-office
have also visited factories, gambling and "hwo-wei"
lottery dens in the Zac Ka Soo area with the object of
obtaining remuneration from them.

C. Crawford

据报道，位于极司菲尔路西段1081号的
中国国民党反共救国军特别服务队分局内

在过去几天里，该分局的一些成员（其中

放。西区警察局并未干涉这些成员的行动，

据报道，该分局的成员还走访了曹家渡

Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army.
Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

From a usually reliable source, it has been learned that the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army has removed its headquarters from 76 Jessfield Road to 31, Lane 1136, Yu Yuen Road. House 76 is now a sub-office of the organization while House 31, Lane 1136, the new premises of the headquarters, it will be recalled, was selected as the local residence of Wang Ching Wei, the ex-Deputy Executive of the Kuomintang.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER 17 AUG 1939）

Residents of some 20 houses in the Hwa Tsung (華邨) alleyway, Jessfield Road, to the immediate north of 76 Jessfield Road, have been instructed by members of the corps to vacate the premises on the grounds that these houses overlook House 76 Jessfield Road and are therefore a danger to the secret activities of the organization.

It is reported that the Corps is making diligent efforts to absorb guerilla units in the suburbs of Shanghai and is contemplating the extension of the movement gradually to places along the S.N.R. and S.H.N.R. Numerous persons hitherto having connections with the guerillas have been bought over by the corps and have been despatched to the interior to persuade other guerilla units to surrender to Wang Ching Wei's cause for peace. Those guerillas who agree to pledge their allegiance to Wang Ching Wei's move will be allowed to remain

Commissioner of Police

from their position in spite of the fact that some
reorganization of these units will have to be carried
out. It is said that Wang Ching Wei and his followers
are making efforts to enlist the service of a
Kuomintang army commander, who is not in active
service at present and is also in disgrace with the
National Government, to undertake the reorganization
of the guerilla units who surrender and create an
army for a new regime which is to be inaugurated
under the direction of Wang Ching Wei and the
Japanese Military Command. In this connection
followers of Wang are said to have approached
General Chen Chi Tang (陳濟棠), the former
warlord of Kwangtung, General Chen Ming Chu
(陳銘樞), a leading figure in the Fukien Revolt
in 1932 and General Tsai Ting Kai (蔡廷鍇),
ex-Commander of the 19th Route Army, but they have
met with no success.

FILE

In the afternoon of August 11, 1939, some 10
committee members of the Zao Ka Doo Merchants' Street
Union held a meeting in House 2, Sing Kong Li (新康里),
Connaught Road, O.O.L., the home of Ao Pah Dong (敖伯堂),
and discussed the occupation of the premises of the
union at 1081 Jessfield Road, O.O.L., by members of
the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang
Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army." The
following resolutions were passed:-
1. That Kitaoka, Japanese Advisor of the "Shanghai
City Government" in Jessfield Area, be requested
to instruct the members of the corps to remove
from the premises.
2. That should Kitaoka fail to intervene in the
matter, the union suspend functioning pending
solution of the dispute.
3. That the union cease to render any further assistance
to the Bureau of Finance in connection with the
collection of business tax in the outside roads
area in the Western District.
In connection with the last resolution, it will
be recalled that the Zao Ka Doo Merchants' Street Union,
acting upon instructions of the Bureau of Finance,
persuaded industrial and business concerns in the
Western District, O.O.L., to pay the business tax
to the organ and distributed copies of a revised table
of rates of the tax to various industrial and business
concerns.

1939年8月11日下午，兆丰路商人街联合会的约10名委员在西区康纳路新康里2号敖伯堂家中举行会议，讨论了中国国民党反共救国军特别服务队成员占用西区极司菲尔路1081号该联合会会所一事。会议通过了以下决议：
1. 请求极司菲尔区“上海市政府”的日本顾问北冈（Kitaoka）指令该队成员撤离该场所。
2. 若北冈未能介入此事，联合会在争议解决之前暂停运作。
3. 联合会停止就西区越界筑路地区的营业税征收事宜向财政局提供任何进一步协助。
关于最后一项决议，需指出的是，兆丰路商人街联合会此前根据财政局的指示，劝说西区越界筑路地区的工商企业向该机构缴纳营业税，并向各工商企业分发了修订后的税率表副本。

the pro-Wang Ching Wei Armed Gang in Western District.
Made by. and Forwarded by. D.I. Crawford

Enquiries have ascertained that Woo Sz Pau
(吴士宝), alias Woo Yung Fu (吴云甫), Vice-
Commander in charge of the four execution groups of
the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang
Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army, 76 Jess-
field Road, O.O.L., is a native of Tungchow (通州),
aged about 37. He was formerly employed a chauffeur
by the Fee Lung Garage (now defunct). In 1930, he
became a disciple of Kao Shing Pao (高鑫宝),
notorious loafer in the French Concession and the
present proprietor of the Lido Garden, 306 Medhurst
Road, and since that time has led the life of a loafer.
He is known as a man in favour of strong and drastic
measures against opponents and, being so, is respected
by the underworld fraternity frequenting the vicinity
of the Great World Amusement Resort, corner of Boule-
vard de Montigny and Avenue Edward VII. His home
is situated at No.7 Dong Foh Li, Rue Ratard.

In August, 1938, Woo Sz Pau became a follower of
Wong Tuh Ling (王德林), Chief of the Western District
Police Bureau, 92 Jessfield Road, O.O.L., and through
the recommendation of the latter, joined in March,
1939 the pro-Wang Ching Wei organization now known as
the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang
Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army.

Chung (李士群), assistant director of the Corps,

Some 25 members of the Special Service Corps of
the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National
Salvation Army were seen being taken into custody by
the Italian Marines on the morning of August 3 from
the Zao Ka Doo Merchants Street Union, 1081 Jessfield
Road, O.C.I.. The Italian marines left a small section
of men to guard the premises after the incident but
withdrew same at about 2 p.m. the same day.
Following the withdrawal of the Italian marines,
armed guards were again posted by the Corps outside
the premises and some of the families of the members
of the Corps began to move in.
From one of the armed guards it was learned that
the Italian Marines had agreed to release his colleagues
the same evening after representations had been made
by the Japanese Military Authorities.
On the morning of August 4, Zee Wen Oen (徐文安),
Chief of Staff of the Corps, who was seen among those
taken away by the Italian Marines on August 3, appeared
at No.1081 Jessfield Road. According to him all the
members of the corps arrested by the Italian marines
had been released, hence the report on the release of
the members submitted on the morning of August 4.
It is reported, however, that at about 12 noon,
a small section of Italian marines called at No.1081
Jessfield Road and, after placing Zee Wen Oen and an

At about 10.30 a.m. August 3, some 100 Italian
marines arrived at the Zao Ka Doo Merchants' Union,
1081 Jessfield Road, O.C.L., and threw a cordon
around the premises. They later succeeded in dis-
arming some 25 members of the "Special Service Corps
of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and
National Salvation Army" who had forcibly occupied
the premises the same morning at about 8 a.m..
The disarmed men together with their weapons, consist-
ing of mauser pistols, hand-grenades and swords, were
removed to the Headquarters of the Italian Marines
situated at No.62 Robison Road.
and
After negotiations between the Japanese/Italian
forces, the latter released the arrested men in the
evening of August 3 together with the seized firearms
on the grounds, it is said, that these people are
members of a subsidiary organ of the "Shanghai City
Government."
On being released, these members returned
immediately to the premises of the Zao Ka Doo Merchants
Street Union, 1081 Jessfield Road, O.C.L.. Some of
the family members of these members have also taken
up residence on the union premises and the armed
guards have appeared again outside the premises.

8月3日上午10时30分左右，约100名意大利海军陆战队员抵达位于极司菲尔路 (Jessfield Road) 1081号、越界筑路区 (O.C.L.) 的曹家渡商界联合会，并在该处周围设立警戒线。随后，他们成功解除了约25名“中国国民党反共救国军特别服务队”成员的武装，这些人于当天上午8时左右强行占领了该处所。被解除武装的人员及其武器（包括毛瑟手枪、手榴弹和刀剑）被移送至位于罗别根路 (Robison Road) 62号的意大利海军陆战队总部。
据称，经过日/意军队之间的谈判，后者于8月3日晚释放了被捕人员以及被扣押的枪支，理由是这些人是“上海市政府”下属机构的成员。
获释后，这些成员立即返回位于极司菲尔路 (Jessfield Road) 1081号、越界筑路区 (O.C.L.) 的曹家渡商界联合会会所。部分成员的家属也已入住该联合会会所，武装警卫再次出现在会所外。

Made by. Forwarded by. D.I. Crawford

At about 8 a.m. August 3, 1939, some 20 members
of the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomin-
tang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army,
armed with Mauser pistols, hand-grenades and swords
and headed by Sung Tsung Mei (孙宗梅), Secretary
of the Corps, arrived at the Zao Ka Doo Merchants
Street Union, 1081 Jessfield Road, O.O.L., in three
private motor cars and took over the premises of the
Union by force. Those 20 members were later joined
by thirty of their colleagues who arrived at the
union premises on foot.
Immediately after taking over the premises,
the members of the corps issued an order instructing
the union to move out within three days and meantime
have posted armed guards at the entrance of the house.
These rowdies are either dressed in foreign style
clothing or in short jacket and pants.
It will be recalled that these members were
originally accommodated in House 6, Zeu Ching Li,
inside Lane 95, Edinburgh Road, C.O.L.. On July
28, 1939, they demanded through two representatives
that the Zao Ka Doo Merchants Street Union premises
be given to them for their use but were refused after
negotiation had taken place between Kitaoka, Japanese
Advisor of the "Shanghai City Government" in Jessfield
Area, and /the Assistant Director of the Corps. In
consequence they removed from House 6, Zeu Ching Li,
Lane 95, Edinburgh Road, to No.76 Jessfield Road,

1939年8月3日上午8时左右，约20名中国国民党反共救国军特别服务队成员，携带毛瑟手枪、手榴弹和刀剑，由该队秘书孙宗梅 (Sung Tsung Mei) 率领，乘坐三辆私人汽车抵达位于极司菲尔路 (Jessfield Road) 1081号、越界筑路区 (O.O.L.) 的曹家渡商界联合会，并强行接管了该联合会会所。随后，另有三十名同事步行到达联合会会所，与这20人会合。

I am now temporarily living at House Nos. 5,6,7 and 8, Zai Ching Lee off Tae Ka Pang, Bubbling Well District.

On 27th November 1938 I was released from the Gaol. I was charged with Pocket-picking from Pootoo Road Station. After release from the Gaol I lived in a small boat moored at the Markham Road Bridge for a period of half a month. Later I went to live in a house at Hungjao Road near Avenue Haig. Since then I removed to House 10 Waung Ka Loong off Great Western Road.

About June I joined this "Tang" (group). On 31/12/1938, through the introduction of Tsi Siam Nyi Tae (戚小=子) I joined the "Patriotic Youth Iron Blood Group for the Riddance of Traitors" and received $20.00 per month. The chief of the Group is one Miss Chang, who has a brother named Chang Hoong Sung (張鴻声). The first job I did was on the 1st day of February when I participated in the shooting of one Kung Zen Pao (耿寿宝) at Zea Ka Doo. After this case I went to an alleyway named Tien Ziang Lee off Rue Pere Frot where the ex-President of the Nantao District Court was shot. His name was unknown to me. Then another murder by stabbing of a Chinese detective attached to the Japanese Military Police. This was about in the month of March. In Room 29 of Wu Ling Lodging House, situated at Rue Wants, French Concession I was arrested by French Police on suspicion of being concerned in a pocket-picking case. After being detained there for 12 days I was released owing to lack of evidence. About 2 days before my release, the four persons named (1) Wong Yung Tsai

1938年11月27日，我从监狱获释。我被指控在普陀路站扒窃。出狱后，我在停泊于马克姆路 (Markham Road) 桥边的一艘小船上住了半个月。后来，我搬到海格路 (Avenue Haig) 附近虹桥路的一所房子里居住。此后，我搬到大西路 (Great Western Road) 旁王家弄10号。

大约在六月，我加入了这个“堂”（团体）。1938年12月31日，通过戚小子 (Tsi Siam Nyi Tae) 的介绍，我加入了“爱国青年铁血除奸团”，每月领取20美元。该团首领是一位张小姐，她有一个哥哥叫张鸿声 (Chang Hoong Sung)。我做的第一件案子是在2月1日，当时我参与了在曹家渡枪杀耿寿宝 (Kung Zen Pao) 的行动。此案之后，我去了法租界神父路 (Rue Pere Frot) 旁的天祥里 (Tien Ziang Lee) 的一条弄堂，前南市区法院院长在那里被枪杀。他的名字我不知道。接着又发生了一起刺杀一名隶属于日本宪兵队的中国侦探的案件。这大约是在三月。在法租界万恩路 (Rue Wants) 的五岭旅馆29号房间，我因涉嫌参与一起扒窃案被法国警察逮捕。在被拘留12天后，因证据不足我被释放。在我获释前约两天，上述旅馆中与我一同被警察逮捕的四个人，即(1) 王永洲 (Wong Yung Tsai)

This group was then dispersed on account of there being

Wong Yung Fah, Soong Yung Foo (朱文富), Zung Sau Ching
(陳少青), Tah Koh Liang (戴國樑) and myself were arrested

Mauser pistols. They were under the charge of "Woo Koong
Kwei" (Mr. Woo) and "Lee Koong Kwei" (Mr. Lee). We were
eventually taken to the Japanese Military Police and after
being detained for about one month we were released on
security of Sung Tsoong Mei. (This man was the member of the
"Patriotic Group for the Riddence of Traitors", who was
previously arrested by the Japanese).

We later met together at House No.6, Zai Ching Lee, Tse
Ka Peng, which place was used as the "Sing Sing Club". Cha
Dah Pao (邱大寶), guard of the gambling den was present at
the time. It was learned that a group had been established
by them. Sung Tsoong Mei and Cheng Koh Tsung made a call
on Woo Sa Pao at House 6, Lane 299, Rue Ratard and asked for

end of May. We, 5 in all, then went to live at House 6, Zai

about 30 persons altogether. We were not allowed to go out
freely. We have to report Chang Koh Tsung, when desired to
go out on private business. Chang would then give us a pass.
No work has been done prior to the day of 22/7/39. On
the afternoon of the latter date, Chang Koh Tsung gave a
lecture, saying that the other guards of Mr. Woo's under
"Yang" had carried out some good work which had disrupted the
business of a newspaper office situated at Ningpo Road on
a previous occasion. They visited the latter place in
m/cars and m/cycles. Chang Koh Tsung then told us to take
a note of their good result. He further stated that something
had to be done that night so no one would be permitted to
go out.
After partaking of supper, Chang Koh Tsung called the
roll and gave each one a Mauser pistol with four magazines
containing 40 rounds of ammunition and one hand-grenade.
In all he had issued to us 12 Mauser pistols and 24 hand-
grenades. Chang Koh Tsung was in possession of a .25
calibre pistol. We, 15 in number left in four Ford Hire
Service hire cars in company with the 3 other men sent by
Mr. Woo to take us. We proceeded from Edinburgh Road to Lane

(王永江), (2) Wong Yung Fah (王云芳), (3) Ming Zai Ziang
(明瑞祥) and (4) Dong Yah Kwang (唐学广) who had been
arrested by Police together with myself at the above mentioned
lodging house were released first by the French Police.
We all then visited Fah Wha Village where we met Sung
Tsoong Mei (沈宗美). He was a member of the "Patriotic
Group for the Riddance of Traitors". About 2 or 3 days later
he was taken into custody by the Japanese Military Police.
This group was then dispersed on account of there being
no leader.
At about 10a.m. on 7/5/39, on leaving the Jessfield Park,
Wong Yung Fah, Soong Vung Foo (宋文富), Zung Sau Ching
(陈少青), Tsh Koh Liang (朱国梁) and myself were arrested
by a gang of about 20 persons, all of whom were armed with
Mauser pistols. They were under the charge of "Woo Koong
Kwei" (Mr. Woo) and "Lee Koong Kwei" (Mr. Lee). We were
eventually taken to the Japanese Military Police and after
being detained for about one month we were released on
security of Sung Tsoong Mei. (This man was the member of the
"Patriotic Group for the Riddance of Traitors", who was
previously arrested by the Japanese).
We later met together at House No.6, Zai Ching Lee, Tse
Ka Sang, which place was used as the "Sing Sing Club". Chu
Dah Pao (邱大宝), guard of the gambling den was present at
the time. It was learned that a group had been established
by them. Sung Tsoong Mei and Chang Koh Tsung made a call
on Woo Sz Pao at House 6, Lane 299, Rue Ratard and asked for

随后我们都去了法华村，在那里遇到了沈宗美（Sung Tsoong Mei）。他是“爱国锄奸团”的成员。大约两三天后，他被日本宪兵队逮捕。由于没有领导人，该团体随后解散。

the release of our five men. We were released about the
end of May. We, 5 in all, then went to live at House 6, Zai
Ching Lee Alleyway off Edinburgh Road. Sung Tsoong Mei and
Chang Koh Tsung obtained money from Mr. Woo for purchasing
furnitures etc. We were given the name as "Self Defence
Group" to Mr. Woo, and received $30.00 per month. There were
about 30 persons altogether. We were not allowed to go out
freely. We have to report Chang Koh Tsung, when desired to
go out on private business. Chang would then give us a pass.

No work has been done prior to the day of 22/7/39. On
the afternoon of the latter date, Chang Koh Tsung gave a
lecture, saying that the other guards of Mr. Woo's under
"Yang" had carried out some good work which had disrupted the
business of a newspaper office situated at Ningpo Road on
a previous occasion. They visited the latter place in
m/cars and m/cycles. Chang Koh Tsung then told us to take
a note of their good result. He further stated that something
had to be done that night so no one would be permitted to
go out.

After partaking of supper, Chang Koh Tsung called the
roll and gave each one a Mauser pistol with four magazines
containing 40 rounds of ammunition and one hand-grenade.
In all he had issued to us 12 Mauser pistols and 24 hand-
grenades. Chang Koh Tsung was in possession of a .25
calibre pistol. We, 15 in number left in four Ford Hire
Service hire cars in company with the 3 other men sent by
Mr. Woo to take us. We proceeded from Edinburgh Road to Lane

在1939年7月22日之前未执行任何任务。当天下午，张国忠发表讲话，称吴先生手下“杨”系的其他保镖此前曾出色地完成了一项任务，扰乱了位于宁波路的一家报社的业务。他们当时乘坐汽车和摩托车前往该地。张国忠随后告诉我们要记下他们的良好成果。他还表示当晚必须采取行动，因此任何人不得外出。

晚饭后，张国忠点名，并给每人发放一支毛瑟手枪、四个装有40发子弹的弹夹和一枚手榴弹。他总共向我们发放了12支毛瑟手枪和24枚手榴弹。张国忠本人持有一支.25口径手枪。我们共15人，连同吴先生派来带领我们的另外3人，分乘四辆福特出租服务公司的租赁汽车出发。我们从爱丁堡路前往弄堂

a way out and requested him to take me out of the house.
He promised to do so and then took me out of the main
entrance of the house. I then found that I was still in the
Zang Keng Lee alleyway. On seeing C.P.Cs standing outside
the above alleyway I immediately ran back to the Yung Chong
Tai Shipping Hong, and again climbed over the wall to the
west drying stage on the other side. As no one was on the
drying stage I then climbed the water pipes on the wall
into the alleyway but owing to the breaking of the water
pipes I fell to the ground and my face was bleeding. I then
stood up and ran into a tailor shop in the Zang Keng Lee
alleyway. As I could not cross the tailor shop so I took

On the 31-12-1938 through the introduction of Tsi Siau
Nyi Ts" I joined the "Patriotic Youth Iron Blood Group for
the Riddance of Traitors" as a member under the charge of a
Miss Chang.
At the end of March this year (1939) owing to our leader
Sung Tsong Hai being arrested by the Japanese Military
Police in the Eastern area, we were compelled to disperse
the group. I then loitered in the vicinity of the Western
Area.
At about 10 a.m. on 7-5-39 I, in company with my friends,
namely, Wong Yung Fah (王永发), Soong Veng Foo (宋文富),
Lung Sau Ching (龙守清), Ta Koh Liang (大国梁), visited the
Jessfield Park for the purpose of recreation. On leaving the
entrance of Jessfield Park on Brenan Road we were surrounded
by a number of men, all of whom were armed, for searching.
Nothing incriminating was found on our persons, but we were
all handcuffed and taken into a waiting car, licence number
unknown, to a HOUSE NO. 94, JESSFIELD ROAD, the premises of
the JAPANESE MILITARY POLICE. We were then taken into the
Interrogation Room and questioned by a Japanese Officer
through a Chinese Interpreter, in the presence of a dark fat
Chinese. The Interpreter stated that we were formerly members
of a group for the riddance of traitors and making
disturbances, for which reason we were arrested. The
Interpreter then asked us if we were the members of the
group in question. We answered in the negative. We were
detained there for a period of 3 weeks after beating up by

于1939年8月5日在中央捕房录取，由罗公硕（Loh Kung Soh）传译。

1938年12月31日，经徐小尼（Tsi Siau Nyi Ts"）介绍，我加入“爱国青年铁血锄奸团”，隶属于张小姐麾下。

今年（1939年）3月底，因我们的首领宋宗海（Sung Tsong Hai）被日本宪兵在东区逮捕，我们被迫解散该团体。此后我在西区附近游荡。

1939年5月7日上午10时许，我与友人王永发（Wong Yung Fah）、宋文富（Soong Veng Foo）、龙守清（Lung Sau Ching）、大国梁（Ta Koh Liang）一同前往兆丰公园游玩。当我们从布伦南路（Brenan Road）的兆丰公园出口离开时，被一群持械男子包围搜身。在我们身上未发现任何罪证，但我们均被戴上手铐，押入一辆车牌号码不明的等候汽车，送往极司菲尔路94号，即日本宪兵队驻地。随后我们被带入审讯室，由一名中国翻译在场，并在一名肤色黝黑、体型肥胖的中国人在场的情况下，接受一名日本军官的讯问。翻译称，我们曾是锄奸及制造骚乱团体的成员，因此被捕。翻译接着问我们是否是该团体的成员。我们予以否认。我们在遭受殴打后被拘禁于此达三周之久

the Japanese Officer.
On or about the 26-6-39 we were removed from the Detention
Room for further questioning. We saw the fat and dark
complexion Chinese was also present in the Interrogation Room.
At that time the Interpreter pointed out the fat and dark
complexion Chinese and stated that we were luckily released
on recommendation of the man indicated, who was wearing a
pair of dark spectacles. After our release we should obey
the instruction of this man, failing which we would be arrested
again and subjected to the death sentence by shooting.
After this the Japanese officer instructed two Military Police
officers to escort us and we followed the fat Chinese. On
leaving the room, the fat Chinese told us that he was not a
traitor and asked us not to make mistake about it. He stated
he was pro-Wang Ching Wei's party, and further stated that
to sacrifice for the "Patriotic Youth Iron Blood Group for the
Riddance of Traitors" meant nothing, as we had been detained
in the Military Police Headquarters for about 3 weeks no one
from the said group had come to assist us. He stated the men
under his control namely Tsang Koh Tsung (張國正) and Sung
Tsoong Mei (沈宗美) helped us by requesting him to be our
guarantor. He asked us to work with him in a proper manner.
We then all entered the HOUSE NO.76 JESFIELD ROAD, where
we met the two men mentioned above. Under such difficult
conditions we had a chance to meet together so we talked
with tears. The men Tsang and Sung said "don't you worry"
and also pointed at the fat and dark Chinese as being the

大约在1939年6月26日，我们被从拘留室带出接受进一步讯问。我们看到那名体态肥胖、肤色黝黑的中国人也出现在审讯室内。当时，翻译指着那名体态肥胖、肤色黝黑的中国人说，我们之所以幸运获释，是得益于所指之人的推荐，此人戴着一副深色眼镜。获释后，我们必须听从该人的指令，否则将再次被捕，并被判处枪决。
随后，日本军官指示两名宪兵军官护送我们，我们便跟随那名肥胖的中国人。离开房间时，那名肥胖的中国人告诉我们，他并非汉奸，请我们不要误解。他表示自己支持汪精卫派系，并进一步指出，为“锄奸团爱国青年铁血组”牺牲毫无意义，因为我们在宪兵司令部被拘禁了约三周，该组织未有一人前来协助我们。他说，受其管辖的人员，即张国正（Tsang Koh Tsung）和沈宗美（Sung Tsoong Mei），通过请求他担任我们的保人而帮助了我们。他要求我们正当地为他工作。

On or about the 10th day of July as I had some important
matter to attend to and wished to go out, but my request
was not granted. It made me so angry as I lost my freedom
after receiving a pay of $30.00 per month. This was overheard
by the supervisor named Chen Dah Pau who made a report of
same to the Headquarters. I was then taken to the Captain
Woo who decided to shoot me. I then begged to say that
enquiries regarding my conduct could be referred to the chief
of my section Tsang Koh Tsung. After further requests were
made I was eventually released. Under such influences I
was compelled to obey their instructions, if not death by
shooting must be my end. Our two sections are situated in
Houses Nos.5,6,7 and 8 ZEU CHING LEE. Iron beds are supplied
to the members in upstairs rooms and ground floor consisting
of reception room, mess room and Chinese Boxing room. Our
Headquarters is situated at No.76 JESSFIELD ROAD, the main-
entrance is guarded by many persons. The entrance guards
are in possession of six Mauser pistols. The next entrance
guards are in possession of four Mauser pistols and the 3rd
entrance guards are armed with six Mauser pistols and two
machine guns. Chief Captain Lee and Captain Woo were working
on the premises situated at No.35 EDINBURGH ROAD. The 1st
Section, sub branch consists of about 20 members. The man
in-charge is one named "Yang" (full name unknown). There is

It was stated that the man wearing grey coloured long gown
was formerly employed by the newspapers office in question.
The chief TSANG KOH TSUNG then said to us that the 3 men
sent by Headquarters had arrived and we should obey their
instructions. After discussion, at about 8 p.m. TSANG KOH
TSUNG called four hire cars from the Ford Hire Service and
same were parked at the mouth of the Eden Tsang alleyway off
Edinburgh Road. Owing to the haste I could only
remember that No.8 was sitting beside the list of the three
men. We proceeded to Lane 15 off Kiangse Road from Edinburgh
Road, via Great Western Road, Avenue Foch, Weihaivei Road,
Race Course Road, Mohawk Road, Lungmen Road, Avenue Edward VII.
On arrival at Kiangse Road people in the three of the cars
alighted with the exception of one CHU PAH LING (No.2 according
to the list) who was watching the three cars. I then followed
the man who dressed in grey coloured long gown into Lane 158,
Lang Keng Lee, off Avenue Edward VII. On turning from the
staircase on the 1st floor of the "China Evening News" premises
I heard the report of shooting from the outside of the
entrance.
At the time of my arrest the chit with the telephone Nos.
thereon was found by the Police.
A photograph shown to me by detectives of persons wanted,
I recognised the man LEE YIH FEE is TSANG KOH TSUNG, and others
are GI NYOEH PING, CHU PAH LING, LI JU HOONG SUNG and the
instigator WOO SZE PAU.
This is my true statement.
Note: A further statement made by the accused contain details regarding
the attack on the "Chinese American Daily News."
Signed.

据说那个穿灰色长衫的人以前受雇于那家报社。随后曾国忠头目对我们说，总部派来的三个人已经到了，我们应该听从他们的指挥。经商议，晚上8点左右，曾国忠从福特租车行（Ford Hire Service）叫了四辆出租车，停在爱丁堡路伊甸园曾弄（Eden Tsang alleyway，音译）口。由于匆忙，我只记得名单上的第8号坐在三个人的旁边。我们从爱丁堡路出发，经大西路（Great Western Road）、福煦路（Avenue Foch）、威海卫路（Weihaivei Road）、跑马厅路（Race Course Road）、莫霍克路（Mohawk Road，音译，疑为慕尔鸣路或其他路名误植）、龙门路（Lungmen Road）、爱德华七世路（Avenue Edward VII），前往江西路（Kiangse Road）15弄。到达江西路后，除朱伯龄（CHU PAH LING，音译，名单上的第2号）负责看守这三辆车外，其他车上的人都下了车。随后我跟随那个穿灰色长衫的人进入爱德华七世路朗耕里（Lang Keng Lee，音译）158弄。在《中国晚报》（China Evening News） premises 一楼楼梯转弯处，我听到入口处外面传来枪声。
在我被捕时，警察发现了一张写有电话号码的便条。
侦探向我展示了一张通缉犯照片，我认出李义飞（LEE YIH FEE，音译）就是曾国忠（TSANG KOH TSUNG），其他人分别是季耀平（GI NYOEH PING，音译）、朱伯龄（CHU PAH LING）、李菊红（LI JU HOONG，音译）、宋（SUNG，音译）以及主谋吴师保（WOO SZE PAU，音译）。
这是我的真实陈述。
注：被告的另一份陈述包含了关于袭击《中美日报》（Chinese American Daily News）的细节。
签名。

Subject Zao Ka Doo Merchants' Street Union, 1081 Jessfield Road
- visited by executives of the "Special Service Corps of
the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National
Salvation Army"
Made by D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by C. Crawford

At 9 a.m., on July 28, 1939, Sung Chung Mei
(孫志潔) and Wong Yung Ching, sectional chiefs
of the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo
Kuomintang Anti-Cmintern and National Salvation Army,
with headquarters at No.6, Lane 95, Zuen Ching Li,
Edinburgh Road, called at the office of the Zao Ka
Doo Merchants' Street Union, 1081 Jessfield Road.
They informed Zung Sien (陳選), Secretary of the
Union, who received them that as the house on Edinburgh
Road, in which their Iron and Blood Corps is situated
was inadequate, they were directed by their superiors
to request the use of the office of the Union. When
informed that the premises of the Union was private
property, the visitors appeared to be offended and
departed in a haughty manner saying that they would
move in with or without the consent of the Union.
Following the above visit, an urgent meeting
was called at which Ao Pah-daung (夏伯棠) presided
and the following resolutions were discussed and
passed :-
(1) That Kitaoka (北岡), Director of the Shanghai
City Government in the Western District, be
petitioned to instruct those people that the use
of the private property of the Union should not
be allowed.
(2) That Mang Kuo-bei (孟國培), nicknamed "Siau
Koo Pai" (小骨牌), proprietor of the Ding
Sung Tai (鼎順泰) Cigarette and Exchange
Shop, 1089 Jessfield Road, who is reputed to be
connected with the Special Service Corps on
Edinburgh Road, be requested to call on the
executive of the Corps to explain the views
of the Union.

- 遭“中国国民党反共救国军特别服务队”执行官员访问
由特别调查员廖仲坚（Liao Chung Chien，音译）撰写，呈报 C. Crawford

1939年7月28日上午9时，中国国民党反共救国军特别服务队的分部负责人宋志洁（Sung Chung Mei，原文拼音与中文名对应存疑，暂按音译及括号内汉字）和王永清（Wong Yung Ching，音译），其总部设在爱丁堡路兆庆里（Zuen Ching Li，音译）95弄6号，造访了兆丰路1081号曹家渡商人街联合会办公室。他们告知接待他们的联合会秘书陈选（Zung Sien，原文拼音与中文名对应存疑，暂按音译及括号内汉字），由于他们铁血团所在的愛丁堡路房屋不够用，上级指示他们请求使用联合会的办公室。当被告知联合会会所为私有财产时，来访者似乎感到被冒犯，傲慢地离去，并称无论联合会是否同意，他们都要搬进去。
在上述访问之后，召开了一次紧急会议，由夏伯棠（Ao Pah-daung，音译）主持，讨论并通过了以下决议：
(1) 请愿上海市政府西区主任北岡（Kitaoka），指示这些人不得使用联合会的私有财产。
(2) 请求孟国培（Mang Kuo-bei，音译），绰号“小骨牌”（Siau Koo Pai），系兆丰路1089号鼎顺泰烟兑店店主，据称与爱丁堡路的特别服务队有关联，去拜访该队执行官，解释联合会的立场。

The branch office of the Special Service Corps
of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and
National Salvation Army at House 6, Zeu Ching Li,
inside Lane 95, Edinburgh Road, O.O.L., has been
abolished; the members, some 70 in number, hitherto
accommodated therein have removed to the Headquarters
of the corps at No.76 Jessfield Road, O.O.L..
The abolition of the office, it is said, is due
to the fact that it has not been managed to the
satisfaction of the Japanese Military Authorities.
The latter consider that the members have not kept
their activities secret enough when carrying out
their work with the result that the Settlement autho-
rities have been able to gain a complete knowledge
of the organization and its workings.
After they had removed to House 76 Jessfield Road,
these members were instructed to hand over their fire-
arms to the corps for safe-keeping which was carried
out. The majority of these members brought their
own firearms when joining the organization, the guns
being their personal property. They were also warned
that in future they would be punished if seen carrying
pistols without permission from the corps headquarters.
It will be recalled that on the morning of July 28,
1939, Sung Chung Mei (孙忠谋) and Wong Yung Ching
(王荣庆), two executive staff members of the Special
Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern

中国国民党反共救国军特别服务队位于越界筑路区 (O.O.L.) 爱丁堡路95弄内邹庆里6号的办事处已被撤销；此前安置于此的约70名成员已迁至该队在越界筑路区极司菲尔路76号的总部。
据称，办事处的撤销是因为其管理未能令日本军方当局满意。后者认为，成员在执行任务时保密工作做得不够，导致租界当局得以全面掌握该组织及其运作情况。
这些成员迁至极司菲尔路76号后，奉命将枪支上交该队保管，此事已执行。大多数成员在加入该组织时自带枪支，这些枪支属于其个人财产。他们还受到警告，今后若未经该队总部许可而被发现携带手枪，将受到惩处。
兹回顾，1939年7月28日上午，中国国民党反共救国军特别服务队的两名执行人员孙忠谋 (Sung Chung Mei) 和王荣庆 (Wong Yung Ching)，

and National Salvation Army, called at the Zao Ka
Doo Merchants' Street Union, 1081 Jessfield Road,
O.O.L., and made a demand for the use of the premises
of the union on the grounds that their office situated
in Edinburgh Road was inadequate. However, through
the intervention of Kitaoka, Director of the Shanghai
City Government in the Western District, the corps
has abandoned the idea of taking over the union premises.
    Regarding the person Wong Yung Ching, one of the
two executives of the corps who called at the Zao Ka
Doo Merchants Street Union on July 28, it has been
ascertained that his real name is Wong Yung Fah (王永法),
alias Wong Ah Nyi (王阿二). He is an ex-member
of the notorious armed gang known as the "Chinese
Youths Anti-Japanese and Traitors-Extermination Iron
and Blood Corps" which formerly operated in the Western
District, O.O.L., and was arrested by the French Police
on 2/4/39. He was later loaned to the Municipal
Police for enquiries as it was believed that he had
been concerned in the assassination of Tseu Chi Tang,
(池堂), Chief of the Joss Paper Tax Bureau, Sinza
Road, on 7/2/39 and in a number of other armed outrages
in the Western District but no evidence on these charges
could be found and he was handed back to the French
Police and released on 14/4/39.

于越界筑路区极司菲尔路1081号的肇嘉浜商民联合会进行交涉，以他们在爱丁堡路的办事处空间不足为由，要求使用该联合会的场所。然而，经过上海市政府西区主任北冈 (Kitaoka) 的干预，该队放弃了接管联合会场所的想法。
关于7月28日前往肇嘉浜商民联合会的该队两名执行人员之一的王荣庆，经查实，其真名为王永法 (Wong Yung Fah)，化名王阿二 (Wong Ah Nyi)。他曾是臭名昭著的武装帮派“中华青年抗日锄奸铁血团”的前成员，该团伙此前在越界筑路区西区活动，他于1939年4月2日被法国警察逮捕。后来他被借调给工部局警务处接受讯问，因为人们相信他参与了1939年2月7日新闸路纸税局局长池堂 (Tseu Chi Tang) 的暗杀案以及越界筑路区西区的其他多起武装暴行，但由于无法找到指控这些罪行的证据，他于1939年4月14日被移交给法国警察并获释。

REPORT

Subject. Further to:- Investigations made into the activities of thirteen
members of the "Special Service Corps" of the "Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-
Comintern & National Salvation Army", arrested by British Military.

Made by D. I. Glover Forwarded by Supt. Bennett

Sir,

The following is a brief resume of the cases in
which the arrested persons have been identified or
implicated :-

(1) 3rd, 6th & 10th accused

Murder & Attempted Murder (Cent. F.I.R. 2155/39)

This case concerns the armed attack made by
members of the above organisation at about 8.30 p.m.
22-7-39, on the premises of the "Chinese-American Daily
News", No. 160 Avenue Edward VII, which resulted in the
death of Mr. A.F. "Tug" Wilson (American) and thirteen
other casualties.

The 6th accused, who admits participation and
implicates the 3rd and 10th accused, was on the 7th March
1940 identified by an employee of the above newspaper.

Three of the pistols seized by British Military,
i.e. "Mauser" Pistols 892708, 1749, and "Astra" Pistol
No. 6396, on examination by the Arms Identification
Section, were found to have been used in this crime.

(2) 12th accused

Attempted Armed Robbery (Chengtu Rd. F.I.R.730/39)

At about 10.30 p.m. 23-5-39, a number of armed
men attempted to commit an armed robbery at House No. 69,
Lane No. 506, Taku Road, but on an alarm being raised,
decamped after firing one shot to intimidate the inmates.

The 12th accused was identified on the 7th March
1940 by a female servant employed at the above address.

报告

主题：续前：对英军逮捕的“中国国民党反共救国军”“特别服务队”十三名成员活动的调查结果。

制作人：格洛弗督察 (D. I. Glover) 呈报人：贝内特巡官 (Supt. Bennett)

先生，

以下是已确认或牵连被捕人员的案件简要摘要：-

(1) 第3、第6及第10被告

谋杀及谋杀未遂（中央 FIR 2155/39）

本案涉及上述组织成员于1939年7月22日晚8点30分左右对位于爱德华七世大道160号的《中美日报》社址进行的武装袭击，导致美国人A.F. “塔格”·威尔逊 (A.F. "Tug" Wilson) 先生死亡，另有十三人受伤。

第6被告承认参与并牵连第3和第10被告，于1940年3月7日被上述报社的一名员工指认。

经武器鉴定科检查，英军缴获的三把手枪，即“毛瑟”手枪892708号、1749号和“阿斯特拉”手枪6396号，被发现曾用于此犯罪。

(2) 第12被告

武装抢劫未遂（成都路 FIR 730/39）

1939年5月23日晚10点30分左右，数名持械男子企图在大沽路506弄69号实施武装抢劫，但在有人发出警报后，开枪一声恐吓屋内人员后逃窜。

第12被告于1940年3月7日被上述地址的一名女佣指认。

February 28, 40.

Arrest of members of the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo
Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army by British Military.

At about 9.30 a.m. February 27, two of the
members of the Section of the Special Service
Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern
and National Salvation Army, situated in House
17, Sung Ka Zah, West Tsu An Pang which is
accessible from Edinburgh Road and Yu Yuen Road,
were observed carrying Mauser pistols in a small
lane (Crescent Avenue) off Yu Yuen Road by a
patrol of the East Surreys. They and eleven of
their colleagues who were on the premises of
their office were subsequently taken into custody
by the British Military patrol and four Mausers
and four small pistols were seized.

The following is a list of the names of
the persons arrested :-

clerk of the section and an

Subject. Investigations made into the activities of thirteen members of the
"Special Service Corps" of the "Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern
& National Salvation Army", arrested by British Military.

Made by. H.I. Glover Forwarded by Supt. Bennett

Sir,

At about 9.30 a.m. February 27th 1940, a patrol
of the 2nd Bn: East Surrey Regiment observed two armed male
Chinese loitering in Crescent Avenue off Yu Yuen Road.
Following the arrest of these two men, a raid was carried
out on House No. 17, Jung Ka Lah (鄭家宅), West Tsu An
Bang (西諸安浜), off Yu Yuen Road, where eleven further
arrests were made and seven more pistols seized. All
thirteen men and the seized pistols were detained by
British Military.

At the request of the British authorities,
D.J. Macadie of the Special Branch, S.M.P., questioned
the arrested men, with the result that it was ascertained
that they were members of the 3rd Section of the 2nd Coy.
"Special Service Corps" of the "Chung Kuo Kuomintang
Anti-Comintern & National Salvation Army". Following is
a list of the names and particulars of the arrested
persons :-

制作人：H.I. Glover 转呈人：Bennett 警司

先生，

1940年2月27日上午9时30分左右，东萨里团第二营的一支巡逻队在愚园路旁的新月路（Crescent Avenue）观察到两名携带武器的中国男子徘徊。在逮捕这两人后，警方对位于愚园路旁西诸安浜郑家宅17号的住所进行了突击搜查，又逮捕了十一人，并缴获七支手枪。所有十三名男子及缴获的手枪均由英军扣留。

应英国当局要求，上海公共租界工部局警务处政治部的 D.J. Macadie 对被捕人员进行了讯问，结果查明他们系“中国国民党反共救国军”“特别服务队”第二连第三分队的成员。被捕人员名单及详情如下：

(1) LING YEE MING (秦奕民)，24岁，青岛。

(9) Y NG TAENG S.N (楊俊山)，25岁，安徽。
(10) AN SIEU SAN (安秀山)，34岁，天津。

During the morning of the 1st March 1940, the
und rsigned and D.I. Crighton, acting on instructions
received, took over from the British Military the thirteen
arrested men for interrogation.
On these persons being fingerprinted it was
found that the undermentioned men had been previously
convicted :-
9th. Yang Tseng San (楊俊山) - "Illegal Detention" -
6 months imprisonment, suspended
for two years, 19-6-39 (B'W. 688/39).
13th. Sung Tseng Hai (宋正海) - "Highway Robbery" -
8 years imprisonment, 30-11-27
(H. E2036). Sentence reduced under
Government Amnesty - Released on
remission of sentence 4-3-33.
One other man, namely the 10th accused, An Sieu
San, had been charged with "Assault", on the 15-6-39, but
was found "Not Guilty" on being arraigned before the 1st
S.M.D.C. (B'Well 96174).
On being individually questioned, the thirteen
men admitted that they were members of the organisation
in question, under the immediate command of Major Lao
Bang Zung, who receives his instructions from the sub-
office of the Special Service Corps situated at No. 35
Edinburgh Road.
The were aware of the fact that these orders
usually emanated from either Woo Sz Pao (胡書保) or Li
Sz Chuen (李士全), Commanders of this organisation, with
Headquarters located at No. 76 Jessfield Road.

1940年3月1日上午，签署人及督察克里顿 (D.I. Crighton)
根据收到的指示，从英军手中接管了十三名被捕男子
以进行审讯。
在对这些人员进行指纹采集后，发现下述人员曾有
前科：
第九名：杨俊山 (Yang Tseng San) - “非法拘禁” -
判处六个月监禁，缓刑
两年，1939年6月19日（百老汇路 688/39）。
第十三名：宋正海 (Sung Tseng Hai) - “拦路抢劫” -
判处八年监禁，1927年11月30日
(H. E2036)。刑期因政府赦免而减刑 -
于1933年3月4日获释。
另有一人，即第十名被告安秀山 (An Sieu San)，曾于1939年6月15日被控
“袭击罪”，但在第一上海地方法院 (1st S.M.D.C.) 受审时被裁定
“无罪”（百老汇路 96174）。
经单独讯问，这十三名男子承认他们是该组织的成员，
该组织直接受劳邦忠 (Lao Bang Zung) 少校指挥，后者
接受位于爱丁堡路 35号的特别服务队分队的指令。
他们知晓这些命令通常发自该组织的指挥官
胡书保 (Woo Sz Pao) 或李士全 (Li Sz Chuen)，其
总部位于极司菲尔路 76号。

曾庆娥 (Tsang Kyung Ngoh) 为参与1939年7月22日
晚上约8点30分袭击其办公室的人员之一。
        关于此案，应记得在当日，大批手持手枪和手榴弹的
男子袭击了该场所，导致十四人死亡或受伤，其中包括
A. F. Wilson 先生（美国人），他因伤重不治身亡。
        用于此犯罪的三支手枪，即毛瑟手枪编号 892708、1749
和阿斯特拉手枪编号 6396，是在第六名被告被捕时由
英军扣押的。

attack he had been instructed by a compositor named Ling
Kwei Sing (李桂生) to purchase a packet of cigarettes
for him. On the 2nd floor landing he met three men who

The 6th accused, on being questioned, admitted

question he was attached to No. 35 Edinburgh Road, and on
receiving instructions from Tsang Koh Tsung (張國珍)
alias Li Bang Foo (李飛), he accompanied the 3rd and
10th accused and four others in a Ford Hire car to the
scene of the crime, where they took part in the attack.
Later he became frightened, discarded his pistol and made
good his escape.
The 3rd and 10th accused, on being questioned,
denied participation in this crime.
Sung Ngoh Fee (宋玉飛), Chu Pei Ming (朱白林)
and Chang Suh Tsung (張如增), arrested by Police parties
from Central and Louza following this shooting affray,
were confronted with the thirteen arrested men, but no
identifications were made.
Two other men, Shah Ming Faung (夏銘堂) alias
Siau Ningpo (小甯波) and Ts Ching Pang (支金邦), who
were arrested by Central Station in connection with
Central Misc. 103/40, also believed to be members of
gang operating in the Western district under Li Sz Chuen,
were also confronted with the arrested men, but likewise
without result.
None of the C.P.C.'s involved were able to
identify any of the persons paraded before them.

第六名被告在接受讯问时，承认参与了此犯罪。在当日，

在此次枪战后，由中央分局和老闸分局警员逮捕的
宋玉飞 (Sung Ngoh Fee)、朱白林 (Chu Pei Ming) 和张如增 (Chang Suh Tsung)，

(2) Chengtu Rd. F.I.R. 730/39
A young girl named Lung Lee Foo ( □□□ ),
aged 14 years, native of Kiangsu, employed as a maid
servant at House No. 69, Lane No. 506 Taku Road,
identified the 12th accused Licu Vee Sing as one of the
men who took part in an "Attempted Armed Robbery" which
took place at the above address at about 10.30 p.m. on
the 23-5-39.
She stated that at the time and date in
question, in response to a knock at the front door, she
requested to know who was calling. She was answered by
a man who stated that he wanted to speak to her master,
a Mr. Lung. On opening the door she was confronted by
five armed men, two of whom guarded her, whilst the
remaining three went upstairs. Owing to an alarm being
raised by Mrs. Lung and her son from upstairs, the robbers
after firing a shot decamped.
The 12th accused, on being questioned, denied
participation in this crime.
(3) Gordon Rd. F.I.R. 17/40
C.P.C.'s 1960, 2336, 1256 and 2517, attached
to Gordon Road Station, identified the 11th accused Ngah
Ts Bing as the man who fired on them at about 8.15 p.m.
2-1-40, when they attempted to search four men in Hire
Car No. 18289, which was proceeding from North to South
on Kiochow Road.
The 11th accused, however, on being questioned,
denied participation in this crime.

As the result of continuous interrogation
statements were finally obtained from the 10th accused
An Sieu on concerning three further cases, particulars
of which are given hereunder :-
After giving a brief resume of his life up to
the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities, he relates
how he enlisted in a patrol unit under the Commander-in-
Chief of the 3rd War Zone of the Chinese Nationalist
Army. Following the retreat on Nanking this particular
corps to which he was attached was reorganised and named
the "Rear Defence Orderly Staff" of the "Military Affairs
Committee". He remained with this unit until ordered to
Changsha, when owing to ill health he was granted sick
leave to proceed to Shanghai. Returning to this city in
May 1938 he took up residence at No. 1005 Brenan Road,
which he operated as a macaroni shop. On the 2nd August
1939, he became acquainted with Zau Bang Zung, Captain
of the 3rd Section of the 2nd Squad, Special Service
Section of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern &
National Salvation Army. On expressing a wish to join
this organisation he was taken to No. 35 Edinburgh Road,
where he was enlisted as a member of the Corps at a salary
of $45.00 including a subsistence allowance. On the 1st
September 1939, by order of one Yang Jih (楊傑),
Commander of the 2nd Squad, he was transferred to the 3rd
Section under the command of Zau Bang Zung, who had
established offices at No. 17 Sung Ka Zah (孫家宅),
Yu Yuen Road. At this address he was issued with an
imitation Browning auto: pistol No. 2715 and six rounds

At about 7 p.m. on the 15-9-39, Zau Bang Sung
instructed the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 11th and himself (10th

proceed to the intersection of Jensfield and Connaught
Roads and there rob three Chinese Constables, of the
Shanghai Municipal Police, of their service pistols.
They were further instructed that should these men
resist they were to be shot.
On arrival at the place indicated they held up
three C.P.C.'s of the Shanghai Municipal Police outside
the "Sing Kong Li" (新康里) alleyway. At this point
in his statement the 10th accused admits that he is not
clear as to how many pistols were stolen as they were
removed by the 4th and 11th accused. One of the C.P.C.'s
ran away, and according to the 10th accused, was fired
upon by the persons not in custody, Chah Lih Kwang and
Tseu Tih Fu. However, as the three C.P.C.'s, who were
victimised, state that they were not fired upon, it is
just possible that the accused has become confused with
Gordon Rd. F.I.R. 254/30, in which he does not admit
participation. In the latter case, C.P.C.'s 1054 and
1098 were held up at the intersection of Hart and
Connaught Roads at about 6.23 p.m. January 26th, 1940,
by a gang of men who succeeded in robbing the first
mentioned C.P.C. of his service pistol. C.P.C. 1098,

At 7 p.m. they proceeded to the place indicated,
where the 11th and 12th accused relieved the two Indian
Policemen of their revolvers, whilst the remainder kept
the victims covered. They then returned to No. 17 Sung
Kah Lah, where the revolvers were handed to Lau Bang Hung.
Only the 6th and 10th accused admit participation
in this case, the remainder denying complicity.
S.M.P.'s 103 and 402, the two Indian Constables
concerned attended identification parades on the 7th
March 1940, but failed to identify any of the accused
paraded before them.
The 6th accused, on being further questioned,
made a rambling verbal statement concerning the attack
made by gunmen upon two constables of the S.M.P., which
took place at about 6.45 p.m. 20-10-39 at the
intersection of Yu Yuen and Edinburgh Roads, and
resulted in the death of the late C.P.C. 3378 and the
wounding of S.P.C. 459 (B'Well 2604/39).
As this man appears at times to be mentally
unbalanced, no reliance can be placed upon his garbled
version of same.
S.P.C. 459, now attached to Yangtsepoo, attended
an identification parade at Chengtu Road Station during
the morning of the 27th March 1940, but failed to
identify any of the men paraded before him.
There is no doubt whatsoever in the minds of
the investigating officers that the cases in which these
men have been identified or have implicated themselves,
constitute but a tithe of the cases which they have
actually committed.

将左轮手枪交给刘帮洪（Lau Bang Hung，音译）。
只有第六和第十被告承认参与此案，其余人均否认共谋。
涉案的两名印籍巡捕，即上海公共租界工部局巡捕103号和402号，
于1940年3月7日参加了列队辨认，但未能从受检被告中认出任何人。
第六被告在接受进一步讯问时，就枪手袭击两名上海公共租界工部局巡捕一事，
做了一份语无伦次的口头陈述，该袭击发生于1939年10月20日下午6时45分左右，
地点在愚园路与爱丁堡路交叉口，导致已故华籍巡捕3378号死亡，
以及上海公共租界工部局巡捕459号受伤（倍开尔路案件记录 2604/39）。
由于此人有时似乎精神失衡，对他这一混乱的版本不能采信。
现隶属杨树浦（Yangtsepoo）分队的上海公共租界工部局巡捕459号，
于1940年3月27日上午在成都路（Chengtu Road）警署参加了一次列队辨认，
但未能从受检人员中认出任何人。
调查官员心中毫无疑问，这些人被指认或自认涉及的案件，
仅占他们实际作案案件的十分之一。

pages.en:

They appear to be under the impression that
they have nothing to fear from the Shanghai Municipal
Police, and that they will eventually be released by
pressure being brought to bear upon the S.M.C. by the
Japanese authorities. Efforts have been made to
disillusion them on this score, but owing to the
difficulty of getting witnesses and complainants to
attend identification parades, there is very little
likelihood of them being implicated in any further cases.
Efforts are however being made to get other complainants
and witnesses to attend identification parades, the
results of which will be made the subject of a further
diary.
（批：Officer D.C.B (S.I)）
D. I.
