他们似乎认为无需害怕上海公共租界工部局警务处，
并且相信日本当局会对工部局（S.M.C.）施加压力，最终使他们获释。
警方已努力打破他们的这种幻想，但由于难以让证人和投诉人
出席列队辨认，他们牵涉进更多案件的可能性微乎其微。
不过，警方正努力让其他投诉人和证人出席列队辨认，
结果将在后续的日志中另行报告。
（批注：警官 D.C.B (S.I)）
D. I.

pages.en:
10th. accused

An Sieu San (安秀山), aged 34 years,
married, residing at 1005 Brenan Road,
Chingchow Hsien, Hopei          D.S.I. Zia Vai Faung
                                translated
C.1, C.B.H.Q.      13.3.40      xxxxxxxx   Clerk Tsaung

I am a member of the 3rd Section, 2nd Squad of Wang
Ching Wei's Defence Corps.
        I was born at Tsang Tsong (張庄) Village to the
east of Chinchow Hsien, Hopei Province. At the age of 9 I
was admitted to a primary school in the village, where I
pursued my studies until I was 16 years old. I then assisted
my parents in farming. At the age of 22 I came to Shanghai
and lived at the home of my cousin An Sieu Foong (安秀峯),
who was a policeman attached to the Public Safety Bureau in
Nantao. After remaining there for about a week, I was taken
by my cousin to sit for an examination at the Public Safety
Bureau, which I passed and was subsequently appointed as a
policeman attached to the Public Safety Bureau Headquarters
at a monthly salary of $12.00. I was thus employed for
about 3 years, after which I obtained a position as Police
Constable No.695 of the French Police. I was then 25 years
old and my first assignment was to go on duty at Ave. Petain
Police Station and later I was transferred to Ave. Joffre
Station. After completing about two years' service, I applied
for leave to return to my native country due to the death of
my father. I was delayed 4 days when coming back to Shanghai
as the boat on which I sailed encountered a typhoon at sea.
As a result of this, I was immediately dismissed from the
French Police. I remained unemployed for about a month, after
which I joined the Anti-piracy Guard of the China Merchants
Steam Navigation Co. and was despatched for duty aboard the
S.S. "Hai Lee". My pay for this job was $16.00 per mensem.
pages.zh:
第十被告

安秀山（An Sieu San），34岁，
已婚，居住于贝当路1005号，
河北静海县          副督察长 谢伟芳（Zia Vai Faung，音译）
                                翻译
C.1, C.B.H.Q.      1940年3月13日      xxxxxxxx   书记员 庄（Tsaung，音译）

我是汪精卫保卫团第二分队第三区的成员。
我出生于河北省静海县以东的张庄（Tsang Tsong）村。9岁时，
我进入村子里的一所小学读书，一直读到16岁。之后我协助父母务农。
22岁时，我来到上海，住在我的表哥安秀峰（An Sieu Foong）家中，
他是南市公共安全局的一名警察。在那里待了大约一周后，
表哥带我去公共安全局参加考试，我通过了考试，
随后被任命为公共安全局总部的警察，月薪12.00元。
我以此身份工作了大约3年，之后我在法租界警务处获得了一份工作，
警号为695。当时我25岁，我的第一个任务是在贝当路（Ave. Petain）警署执勤，
后来我被调至霞飞路（Ave. Joffre）警署。服役约两年后，
因父亲去世，我请假回国。回上海时，我所乘的船在海上遭遇台风，
延误了4天。因此，我立即被法租界警务处开除。
我失业了大约一个月，之后加入了招商局轮船公司的防海盗护卫队，
并被派往“海利”号（S.S. "Hai Lee"）轮船上执勤。这份工作的月薪为16.00元。

pages.en:
(2)

I ceased to work there after the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in 1937. I then enlisted in the Patrol Unit under
the Commander-in-chief of the 3rd War Zone of the Nationalist
Army. Following our retreat to Nanking the troops were re-
organised to be known as the Rear Defence Orderly Staff of the
Military Affairs Committee. After our troops moved further
into Changsha, I suddenly commenced to spit blood and was
therefore granted sick leave to return to Shanghai. It was
then during the month of May 1938. I took up residence at No.
1005 Brenan Road, where I operated a "machine made" macaroni
business. On the 2-8-39, Zau Bang Zung (趙程), Captain
of the 3rd Section of Wang Ching Wei's Defence Corps, took me
to No.35 Edinburgh Road, where I was introduced to join as a
member of the Corps at a monthly pay of $45.00 including food
allowance. On the 1-9-39, by order of Commander Yang Jih (楊傑)
of the 2nd Squad, I was transferred to the 3rd Section under
the leadership of Captain Zau Bang Zung, with offices at No.
17 Sung Ka Zah, off Crescent Avenue. The personnel of our staff
are as follows:-

One Captain : Zau Bang Zung (趙鵬程)
Two Section : Zung Zih Tsu(2nd accused)
Chiefs (郭 碧 芝)
Lieu Dien Hwa(not arrested)
(劉 殿 華)

Eleven Executive Members.

One Clerk : Zing Yee Ming (1st accused)
(秦 義 民)
One Coolie : Sung Tsung Hai (13th accused)
(孫 正 海)

Three Cooks (Not arrested).

I was issued with a pistol No.2715 and 6 rounds of
ammunition.
pages.zh:
(2)

1937年中日敌对行动爆发后，我不再在那里工作。随后我加入了国民党军队第三战区司令官麾下的巡逻队。我军撤退至南京后，部队进行了重组，改称为军事委员会后方防卫参谋处。当我军进一步向长沙转移时，我突然开始咯血，因此获准病假返回上海。那是1938年5月间。我住进布伦南路（Brenan Road）1005号，经营一家“机制”通心粉生意。1939年8月2日，汪精卫保卫团第三连连长赵程（Zau Bang Zung）带我到爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）35号，介绍我加入该团，月薪45.00元，含伙食津贴。1939年9月1日，根据第二分队队长杨杰（Yang Jih）的命令，我被调至赵邦程（Zau Bang Zung）连长领导下的第三连，办公地点位于新月路（Crescent Avenue）旁的孙家宅（Sung Ka Zah）17号。我处人员如下：-

连长一名：赵鹏程（Zau Bang Zung）
排长两名：宗子祖（Zung Zih Tsu）（第二被告）
郭碧芝（Kuo Pi-chih）
刘殿华（Lieu Dien Hwa）（未逮捕）

执行队员十一名。

书记员一名：秦义民（Zing Yee Ming）（第一被告）
苦力一名：孙正海（Sung Tsung Hai）（第十三被告）

厨师三名（未逮捕）。

我配发了一支编号为2715的手枪及6发子弹。

pages.en:
(3)

At about 7 p.m. one day during September 1939
(15.9.39) Captain Zau gave orders at our office that we should
go out on a special errand and after assigning Zung Zah Ts (2nd
accused), Ying Shih Tsoo (4th accused), Tsang Kyung Nyoh (6th
accused), Ngah Ts Bing (11th accused), Chah Zih Kwang (not
arrested), Tseu Tih Fu (not arrested) and myself to the job,
stated that we could follow Section Chief Aung, who was cognizer
of the nature of our work. Armed with my pistol, I left with
the six others, who were all armed with Mauser pistols. We
proceeded on foot along Yu Yuen Road, and turned east to
Edinburgh Road, north of Kinnear Road, east of Jessfield Road,
and north to Connaught Road, where we stopped at the mouth of
Sing Kong Li alleyway. Before reaching the place Zung Zah Ts
told us that he was instructed by Captain Zau to take us to the
intersection of Jessfield and Connaught Roads with the object
of robbing Chinese policemen of their pistols. Presently we
saw three Chinese Policemen standing together at the entrance
to Sing Kong Li alleyway, whereupon we went forward and whilst
Chah Zih Kwang and Tseu Tih Foo pointed their Mauser pistols
at the policemen, Ying Shih Tsoo and Ngah Ts Bing took away
the pistols from two of them by cutting off the string attached
to the pistols with a 3 inch knife which they both carried. The
remaining policeman, however, succeeded in making good his
escape, and when doing so was fired upon by Chah Zih Kwang and
Tseu Tih Fu but was fortunately not hit. We soon returned to
17 Sung Ka Zah, Crescent Avenue, where Ying Shih Tsoo and Ngah
Ts Bing gave the two stolen pistols to Zung Zah Ts, who in turn
pages.zh:
(3)

1939年9月某日（9月15日）晚上7点左右，赵连长在我们办公室下令，让我们出去执行一项特殊任务，并将宗子祖（Zung Zah Ts）（第二被告）、应世佐（Ying Shih Tsoo）（第四被告）、张金玉（Tsang Kyung Nyoh）（第六被告）、叶达兵（Ngah Ts Bing）（第十一被告）、查子光（Chah Zih Kwang）（未逮捕）、周迪福（Tseu Tih Fu）（未逮捕）以及我指派给这项任务，并说我们可以跟随熟悉我们工作性质的Aung排长。我带上手枪，与其他六人一同出发，他们都配备了毛瑟手枪。我们沿愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）步行，向东转入金尼尔路（Kinnear Road）以北、极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）以东的爱丁堡路，再向北行至康纳特路（Connaught Road），在星港里（Sing Kong Li）弄堂口停下。在到达该地之前，宗子祖告诉我们，他是受赵连长指示，带我们去极司菲尔路与康纳特路的交叉口，目的是抢劫中国警察的手枪。不久，我们看到三名中国警察站在星港里弄堂入口处，于是我们走上前去，当查子光和周迪福用毛瑟手枪指着警察时，应世佐和叶达兵用他们各自携带的一把3英寸长的刀割断系在手枪上的绳带，从其中两人手中夺走了手枪。然而，剩下的一名警察成功逃脱，在他逃跑时，查子光和周迪福向他开枪，但幸运的是未击中。我们很快回到新月路孙家宅17号，应世佐和叶达兵将两支被盗手枪交给宗子祖，宗子祖随即

pages.en:
(4)

handed same to Captain Zau. I do not know when the latter
forwarded these pistols to No.35 Edinburgh Road. At about
9 a.m. the following day (16.9.39) Captain Zau warned us not
to mention anything to others about this robbery.

Signed:- An Sieu San
pages.zh:
(4)

将其转交给赵连长。我不知道后者何时将这些手枪送往爱丁堡路35号。次日（1939年9月16日）上午9点左右，赵连长警告我们不要向他人提及此次抢劫之事。

签名：- 安秀山（An Sieu San）

pages.en:
10th Accused.

further
/
AN SI SU SAN

// D.S.I. via Van Maung
translated Hsu S. F.
C.B.H.Q. 13.3.40

At 7.30 p.m. on the 16.9.39, acting on the instructions
of our captain, one named Zau Bang Tung (趙鵬程), I
together with the 4th accused Ying Shih Tsoo, 5th accused
Hoh Tsoong Un, 6th accused Tsang Kyung Ngoh, 8th accused
Zung Yoh Sung and 9th accused Yang Tseng San, proceeded
to attack S.M.Police constables on duty at the intersection
of Bremen and Edinburgh Roads. The 5th accused, 8th accused
and I were each armed with a pistol, while the 6th, 4th
and 9th accused armed with three Hauser pistols. Before
starting out we were instructed by Captain Zau to open fire
at the S.M.Police officers, should the latters offer any
resistance.

On arrival at the mentioned place we observed two
S.M.Police officers standing on the north-west corner of
the road. We then (six persons) rushed on and held up
the two policemen at the point of our pistols. The 4th
and 6th accused immediately produced a 3" long knife, cut
off the lanyards of the policemen's pistols and removed
them away from the person of the S.M.P. constables.

We then managed to escape freely and returned to
our headquarters at No. 17, where Ying Shih Tsoo and Tsang
Kyung Ngoh handed over the stolen pistols to Captain Zau,
who at that time instructed us not to disclose any information
regarding this case.

At 10 a.m. on the 17.9.39 Captain Zau took these
two pistols to No. 35 Edinburgh Road, where he handed same
over to Captain Yang Chi (楊傑) of the 2nd Detachment.

Signed:
pages.zh:
第十被告。

补充
/
安秀山（AN SI SU SAN）

// 通过 Van Maung 转交特别调查科
译者 徐 S. F.
中央捕房总部 1940年3月13日

1939年9月16日晚上7点30分，遵照我们连长赵鹏程（Zau Bang Tung）的指示，我与第四被告应世佐（Ying Shih Tsoo）、第五被告何宗安（Hoh Tsoong Un）、第六被告张金玉（Tsang Kyung Ngoh）、第八被告宗耀松（Zung Yoh Sung）和第九被告杨增三（Yang Tseng San）一起，前往袭击在不来梅路（Bremen Road）和爱丁堡路交叉口执勤的工部局警察。第五被告、第八被告和我各持一支手枪，而第六、第四和第九被告则持有三支豪瑟（Hauser）手枪。出发前，赵连长指示我们，如果工部局警官进行任何抵抗，就向他们开火。

到达上述地点后，我们观察到两名工部局警官站在路口的西北角。于是我们（六人）冲上前去，用手枪指着两名警察将他们控制住。第四和第六被告立即拿出一把3英寸长的刀，割断警察手枪的挂绳，并从工部局巡警身上取走手枪。

随后我们顺利逃脱，返回位于17号的总部，应世佐和张金玉将 stolen 手枪交给赵连长，他当时指示我们不得泄露关于此案的任何信息。

1939年9月17日上午10点，赵连长将这两支手枪带到爱丁堡路35号，在那里将它们移交给第二分队队长杨杰（Yang Chi）。

签名：

pages.en:
An Shiu San(安秀山)
C.B.H.Q.           13.3.40           x D. S. I. Zia
                                    translated clerk Kuh
                                    XXXXXXX

At about 6 p.m. on the 20th September 1939, our
Captain Zau Bang Zung(趙邦雄) told the 2nd accused Zung
Zee Ts, the 4th accused Ying Shou Tso, the 6th accused Tsang
Kying Nylon, the 11th accused Yie Ta Bing, the 12th accused
Lieu Vee Sing, and me that recently the house of Wang Ching
Wei in Yu Yuen Road near the house 1031 was guarded by two
Indian policemen to watch our movements, and instructed us
to rob them of their pistols the instructions having been
received from the superior.

At 7 p.m. on the 20-9-39, we all donned plain cloths
and proceeded to the place mentioned and after intimidating
the two policemen (Sikhs) the 11th and the 12th accused
relieved them of their pistols.

We then proceeded to No. 17 Sung Kah Zah(孫家宅)
and handed the pistols to Captain Zau.

This is the 3rd time that we robbed pistols.
This is my true statement.
pages.zh:
安秀山（An Shiu San）
中央捕房总部           1940年3月13日           x 特别调查科 Zia
                                    翻译员 Kuh
                                    XXXXXXX

1939年9月20日下午6点左右，我们的连长赵邦雄（Zau Bang Zung）告诉第二被告宗子祖（Zung Zee Ts）、第四被告应寿佐（Ying Shou Tso）、第六被告张金玉（Tsang Kying Nylon）、第十一被告叶达兵（Yie Ta Bing）、第十二被告刘维新（Lieu Vee Sing）和我，最近汪精卫在愚园路靠近1031号的住宅由两名印度警察守卫，以监视我们的行动，并指示我们抢走他们的手枪，该指示来自上级。

1939年9月20日晚上7点，我们都换上便衣，前往上述地点，在恐吓了两名警察（锡克教徒）后，第十一和第十二被告缴了他们的手枪。

随后我们前往孙家宅（Sung Kah Zah）17号，将手枪交给赵连长。

这是我们第三次抢劫手枪。
这是我的真实陈述。

pages.en:
Zung Lee Foo(陈兰富)
Li Yang Shien                      XX D.S.I.Wu
C.B.H.Q. C.l.      12.3.40         translated   clerk Kuh
                                     XXXXX

My name is Zung Lee Foo, age 14, native of Li Yang,
maid servant of Zung Zeu Ts, House 69, Lane 506, Taku Road
where I reside.

At about 10.30 p.m. on the 23-5-1939 when my mistress
was in the upstairs room I heard a knocking at the front door.
As I questioned who it was the person who was outside replied
that he wanted to see Mr. Zung (my master). As soon as I
opened the door five men all armed with pistols entered the
premises, two of whom intimidated me while the others proceeded
upstairs. Just as they got on half way of the staircase I
noticed that some one upstairs had switched off the light
and at the same time I heard my mistress shouting"arrest
thief". At that time my young master Zung Taoong Kyi(陈仲祺)
rushed down from the flight of stairs when the robbers
turned and made good their escape through the front door.
As my young master gave chase/one of the robbers fired a shot
toward the ground.

At about 2.30 p.m. on the 7-3-40, I called at the
Chengtu Road Station where I identified the 12th accused
Lieu Vee Sing(刘维新) as one of the five robbers who had
attempted to carry out a robbery in my master's family.

Signed: Zung Lee Foo.
pages.zh:
陈兰富（Zung Lee Foo）
李阳先（Li Yang Shien）                      XX 特别调查科 Wu
中央捕房总部 刑事侦缉处      1940年3月12日         翻译员   书记员 Kuh
                                     XXXXX

我叫陈兰富，14岁，籍贯李阳，是大沽路（Taku Road）506弄69号宗子祖家的女佣，我就住在那里。

1939年5月23日晚上10点30分左右，当我的女主人在楼上房间时，我听到前门有敲门声。当我询问是谁时，外面的人回答说他想见宗先生（我的主人）。我刚一开门，五名都带着手枪的男子进入屋内，其中两人恐吓我，其他人则上楼。就在他们走到楼梯半中间时，我注意到楼上有人关了灯，同时听到我的女主人大喊“抓贼”。当时我的小主人陈仲祺（Zung Taoong Kyi）从楼梯上冲下来，劫匪转身从前门逃之夭夭。当我的小主人追赶时，其中一名劫匪向地面开了一枪。

1940年3月7日下午2点30分左右，我到成都路警察局，指认第十二被告刘维新（Lieu Vee Sing）是企图在我主人家实施抢劫的五名劫匪之一。

签名：陈兰富（Zung Lee Foo）。

pages.en:
Zah Veng Tung (石文通)
Paoshan, Kiangsu.                 D.S.I. Wu Chen Mo
                                   translated
C.l, C. .B.H.Q.      19.3.40       xxxxxx    Clerk Hsia

My name is Zah Veng Tung, aged 17, native of
Paoshan, Kiangsu. I have been in the employ of the type-
setting office, Chinese-American Daily News, 160 Avenue
Edward VII, as apprentice for one and half years.
At about 8.30 p.m. on the 22.7.39 (28th. year
of the Republic of China), I was told to purchase a packet
of cigarettes by one named Zing Kwei Ling (秦桂林), a
compositor of the Chinese-American Daily News. Later, I
met a person wearing a black jacket and two others on the
staircase landing of the 2nd. floor. Owing to the office
door being closed, they fired with pistols which they were
carrying, at the staircase landing, I immediately ran down
to the ground floor, where I heard several more shots fired.
At the same time I also heard the police whistles, and
noticed three desperadoes running towards the office of the
Ta Mei Pao.
At 2.30 p.m. on the 7th. March 1940 (29th. year
of the Republic of China), I was summoned to the Chengtu
Road Police Station by a detective from the C.B.H.Q. (C.l)
where I identified one named Tsang Kyung Nyoh (張金玉) (6th
accused) as one of the desperadoes.
This is a true statement.

刑事侦缉处, 中央捕房总部      1940年3月19日       xxxxxx    书记员 Hsia

我叫石文通，17岁，籍贯江苏宝山。我在爱德华七世路（Avenue Edward VII）160号《中美日报》排版室当学徒已有一年半。
1939年7月22日（民国二十八年）晚上8点30分左右，《中美日报》排字工人秦桂林（Zing Kwei Ling）叫我去买一包香烟。后来，我在二楼楼梯平台上遇到一个穿黑夹克的人和另外两个人。由于办公室门关着，他们用随身携带的手枪向楼梯平台射击，我立刻跑到底层，在那里又听到几声枪响。同时我还听到了警哨声，并注意到三名歹徒朝《大美报》办公室方向跑去。
1940年3月7日（民国二十九年）下午2点30分，我被中央捕房总部（刑事侦缉处）的一名侦探传唤至成都路警察局，在那里我指认张金玉（Tsang Kyung Nyoh）（第六被告）是歹徒之一。
此为真实陈述。

21.3.40 ---------- Hsu Sa P.

At 8.15 p.m. on the 2.1.40 I was on duty with a
search party, consisting of C.P.C.s 1256, 2336, 2517 and
elf, led by F.P.S. 175, and on reaching the intersection
aochow and Sinza Roads, we observed a silver taxicab,
oceeding south to north on Kiaochow Road, F.P.S. 175,
i/c of the search party then went on and halted the car
with a view to searching the occupants.

No sooner had C.P.C. 1256 opened the front side
door of the car than a passenger, sitting by the side of the
driver, jumped out of the taxicab, seemingly to be under
influence of drink. This man after walking backward a few
steps ran towards north and at the same moment produced
a pistol. C.P.C. 1256 on seeing this opened fire at him,
who immediately fled into Lane No. 273 off Kiaochow Road,
and exchanged shots with C.P.C. 1850.

As we gave chase this gunman entered a certain house
in the above numbered lane and made good his escape.

On March 7, 1940 I was summoned to attend an
indentification parade held at the Chengtu Road Police
Station where I identified the 11th accused as being the
person who had opened fire during the shooting affray on
2.1.40.

Signed:

1940年3月21日 ---------- 徐 Sa P.

1940年1月2日晚上8点15分，我正在与一支搜查队一起执勤，该队由华捕1256号、2336号、2517号和我本人组成，由外捕175号带领，当我们到达胶州路（Kiaochow Road）和新闸路（Sinza Roads）交叉口时，我们看到一辆银色出租车，在胶州路上由南向北行驶。搜查队负责人外捕175号随即上前拦停该车，以便搜查车内人员。

华捕1256号刚打开车前侧门，坐在司机旁边的一名乘客就跳下出租车，看似处于醉酒状态。此人向后倒退几步后向北跑去，与此同时掏出一支手枪。华捕1256号见状向他开枪，他立即逃入胶州路旁273弄，并与华捕1850号互射。

当我们追捕时，这名枪手进入了上述弄堂内的某所房屋并成功逃脱。

1940年3月7日，我被传唤参加在成都路警察局举行的列队辨认，我指认第十一被告就是1940年1月2日枪战事件中开枪的人。

This office formerly had a Branch Office at No.6 Wonglu
Road, end of North Szechuen Road, it did liaison work and its
business was to vise passports. As the location is somewhat
out of the way, the officers employed have found it difficult
to contact the public on official business since the recent
reduction in transportation facilities. In view of this we have
had to remove to new premises at No.725 Avenue Haig, which we
occupied on the 25th instant; the telephone number is 73795.

Apart from informing other parties concerned, we beg the

Pro-Wang Ching Wei Re-organization
of Lodging House Union.
--------------------------------------------

Sir,

At 11.20 p.m. 22-11-41, Zee Vung Tsau (徐文旦),
Chairman of the Lodging House Union and proprietor
of the Hoong Foh (洪福) Lodging House, 89 Wuhu Road,
reported that about 10.p.m. same date, he was visited
by 2 Japanese and 2 Chinese who requested him to join
the pro-Wang Ching Wei Lodging House Union and to hand
over the funds of the old union totalling approximately
$40,000.00.

Owing to the late hour Zee Vung Tsau requested
the men to return on 23-11-41. At 2.p.m. 23-11-41,
3 Japanese and 2 Chinese of the Pro-Wang Ching Wei
party again visited 89 Wuhu Road where Zee Vung Tsau
and 10 other lodging house owners were requested to
join the new party. C.D.C.129 attended and as there
was no force or threats no police action was required.

It would appear that the Japanese stated that they
had secured the names of the following lodging house
managers and after showing their cards stated they
were selected as members of the new Committee:

(1) Tseu Foh Ming (周福敏).
Kyung Zung (隆城) Lodging House.

(2) Kau Yung Ching (高立清).
Tsoong Woo (中和) Lodging House.

(3) Tsar Ts Ching (邹子清).
Mying Ping (迎賓) Lodging House.

(4) Tseu Pau Nyau (周伯).
Secretary.

The chairman was not elected but they stated
one would be appointed at the next meeting, date of
which was not settled.

Muir and C.D.C. 319 revealed that on 14-11-41, the brother-in-law of Wong Kwei Ding named Chiang Loh Kung (蔣六根), residing 39 Chun Ching Lee off Sinza Road, attended 62 Ching Ts Too Miau, Connaught Road, on behalf of Wong Kwei Ding to interview Zee Ping (徐斌) and was informed that Zee Ping, though being attached to 62 Ching Ts Too Miau, his present section was unknown.

It was further revealed that Wong Kwei Ding's wife has wished to divorce him, which he, Wong Kwei Ding, refuses to comply with and since his wife left him, he has retained most of her belongings.

Chiang Loh Kung further stated that he had requested the assistance of one known to him as Doo Kwei Doo (大塊頭), also a member of 62 Ching Ts Too Miau organisation, to approach this Zee Ping and inform him that Wong Kwei Ding was a "poor man."

Since 13-11-41, no further interference, or visits by Zee Ping have been made to 554/95 Hart Road and as he Zee Ping, could not be located by the complainant's brother-in-law Chiang Loh Kung, the actual motive behind the visit on 13-11-41 is unknown, it is however presumed that the complainant's wife has close relations with Zee Ping or some of his associates, or has given him false information regarding the financial position of the complainant.

J. Smith
Sen. Det. i/c.
D.D.C. "B" Div.

Misc 393/41.
(2) 戈登路
1941年11月22日。
亲汪精卫武装人员的活动。

D.S. 161 Muir，负责人。

先生，
经 D.S. Muir 和中央巡捕319号进一步调查查明，1941年11月14日，王贵亭（Wong Kwei Ding）的妹夫蒋六根（Chiang Loh Kung），住新闸路春庆里（Chun Ching Lee）39号，代表王贵亭前往康纳脱路（Connaught Road）金司德庙（Ching Ts Too Miau）62号会见徐斌（Zee Ping），并被告知徐斌虽隶属金司德庙62号，但其目前所属部门不明。

还查明，王贵亭的妻子希望与他离婚，但王贵亭拒绝同意，且自妻子离家后，他扣留了她的大部分财物。

蒋六根进一步陈述，他曾请求一位熟人大块头（Doo Kwei Doo，音译）协助接近徐斌，此人也是金司德庙62号组织的成员，告知徐斌王贵亭是个“穷人”。

自1941年11月13日以来，徐斌未再干扰或造访哈特路（Hart Road）554/95号，由于投诉人的妹夫蒋六根无法找到徐斌，1941年11月13日造访的真实动机不明，但推测投诉人的妻子与徐斌或其某些同伙关系密切，或就投诉人的财务状况向徐斌提供了虚假信息。

J. Smith
高级侦探长。

Gordon Road MUNICIPAL
November 13th, 41.

Activities of Pro-Wang Ching ei armed personnel.

D. J. Muir. Officer i/c. (Signature)

Sir,
at 6.30p.m. on 13/11/41, one mr Kwei Ding
(王貴亭), 44, shanghai, n/r. No. garden coolie
residing 554/95 Hart Road came to the station and
reported that at 4.30p.m. 13/11/41, three male Chinese,
one armed with a small pistol entered his home during
his absence together with his wife one mr Deh Ts
(王唐氏), age 34, native of shanghai who has been
living apart from him for a period of 6 months.

According to the complainant these men and the
female removed several articles of clothing belonging
to the female from boxes then sealed these boxes with
strips of paper bearing the female's name.

In addition to this one of the men left a note
reading: "Lee Ping, 4th section sergeant, special works
corps, 62 Ching Ts Too Miau" (徐斌特工隊第四班長金司德廟62號)
and after warning the complainant's daughter that the
seals were not to be removed and that the complainant
was to call at the above address, the party left after
being in the house for about 10 minutes.

Seals and note forwarded for perusal and
information.

(Signature)
D.S. 161.

J. Smith
Sen. Det. i/c.
D.D.C. "B" Div.

先生，
1941年11月13日下午6时30分，王贵亭（mr Kwei Ding），44岁，上海籍，现居哈特路（Hart Road）554/95号，职业为花园苦力，来到警局报案称，1941年11月13日下午4时30分，在他不在家时，三名中国男子进入其住所，其中一人持有一支小手枪，与其妻王唐氏（mr Deh Ts，原文如此，应为Mrs. Wang Tang-shi），34岁，上海籍，已与他分居6个月，在一起。

封条和纸条已呈送审阅及备案。

and 2nd suspect together met a prostitute, the 1st

refused as she smelt drink. The 1st suspect
resenting this insisted, thus resulting in the
prostitute using foul language as is usual. At this

五名中国男子与妓女拉客引发的纠纷。
其中一名男子持有武器。

五名嫌疑人：
(1) 秦在奎（Zing Zai Kwei）23岁，镇江人，隶属康纳脱路62号第六小队。
(2) 赵海帆（Lau Hai Vai）30岁，北京人，隶属康纳脱路62号第六小队。（持有武器）。
(3) 李少祺（Lee Sao Chi）25岁，扬州人，男职员，天津路435号。
(4) 李棠才（Lee Tsong Zai）49岁，扬州人，男电梯员，广西路406号。
(5) 张阿庆（Tsang Ah Ching）49岁，扬州人，男苦力，广西路425号。

于1941年11月1日凌晨1时被中央巡捕654号（C.P.C.654）在贵州路附近的宁波路逮捕。

中央巡捕看到上述人员在一起争吵，并在上述道路巡逻后将他们带至本局。

到达警局后，观察到第一和第二被告处于醉酒状态。另发现第二被告持有一支 .32 口径自动手枪，圣艾蒂安（St. Etienne）制造，制造商编号59，工部局警务处编号 Y.833，以及一个弹夹和七发子弹，持枪许可证号为 S.N.C.Lic.No.3772。该枪支将于1941年11月1日上午送交枪械鉴定科。

事发经过似乎是，第一和第二嫌疑人共同遇到一名妓女，第一名嫌疑人试图包她过夜，但她因闻到酒味而拒绝。第一名嫌疑人对此感到不满并坚持要求，导致妓女像往常一样使用污言秽语。此时

Louza Police Misc.680/41. 6/10/41.

Re a pistol shot fired in Room 413 of the Great Eastern Hotel, Wing On Co. Ltd. Building, Nanking Road.

Enquiries by D.S.I. Wong Ching Sheng and D.S.I. Bretherton.

At 11 a.m. the 5/10/41, the manager of the aforementioned Hotel, reported to this Station that at about 11 p.m. the 4/10/41 one of seven male Chinese, all alleged to have been armed, fired his pistol once on the verandah of Room 413. The bullet had penetrated two wooden dividing doors on the verandah and had spent itself. From a cursory examination, it was apparent that the bullet had been prised out and taken away, presumably by the person who had fired it or by his colleagues.

The Room No. 413 had been rented on the 16/9/41 by one who signed himself Ding Yu Cheng (丁有成). Daily seven or more male Chinese, dressed in foreign style, Shanghai dialect, frequented the room and mostly played Mah-jong and the like. The room boy No. 1, Yuan Nan (袁南) had taken no untoward notice of the fact that these persons were armed because they had possession of pistol licences, at least the impression given him was to the effect that they had.

At 9 a.m. the 5/10/41, the persons in question had booked out taking what belongings they had with them. A perusal of all telephone calls made

关于南京路永安公司大楼大东旅馆413房间发生枪击事件。

由副督察长黄景生（Wong Ching Sheng，音译）和副督察长布雷瑟顿（Bretherton）调查。

41年10月5日上午11时，上述旅馆经理向本捕房报告称，41年10月4日晚11时许，七名中国男子中的一人（据称均持有武器）在413房间的阳台上开了一枪。子弹穿透了阳台上的两扇木制隔门后耗尽动能。经粗略检查，明显看出子弹已被撬出并带走，推测是由开枪者或其同伙所为。

413房间系由一名自称为丁有成者于41年9月16日租用。每日有七名或更多身着西式服装、讲上海话的中国男子出入该房间，大多进行打麻将等活动。1号侍者袁南（Yuan Nan，音译）并未对这些人的持械行为产生警觉，因为他们持有手枪执照，至少给他的印象是他们持有执照。

41年10月5日上午9时，相关人员结账离开，带走了随身物品。目前正在查阅他们拨打的所有电话记录，

TRANSLATION

In connection with your circular in favour of the
Peace Movement, it appears that your association is in
support of the Leader and is closely interested in the
national affairs. Such attitude on your part is deemed
highly beneficial to the Party and to the State. The
Chungking Government, however, has not yet awakened from
its dream and is making a desperate struggle by resorting
to mean threats in an endeavour to muzzle the press and
frustrate the Peace Movement. It is believed that your
association already understands these intrigues and therefore
no change is likely in your attitude.

Nevertheless, we send you this letter in view
of the possibility that unruly elements will take the
opportunity of chances furthering undesirable activities,
and that certain persons may be tricked owing to misconception.
If your attitude proves inconsistent trouble may follow, and
not only you will be despised by the public, but will be
severely punished as it is the duty of this Corps to prevent
any one from openly conducting activities against the Peace
Movement. Do not say that no previous warning was given.

(Chopped) : Special Service Corps of
the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-
Comintern & National
Salvation Army.
pages.zh:
译文

鉴于贵会发布支持和平运动的通告，看来贵会支持领袖，并密切关注国家事务。贵会的这种态度被认为对党国大有裨益。然而，重庆政府尚未从梦中醒来，正通过卑劣的威胁手段进行绝望的挣扎，企图钳制舆论并挫败和平运动。相信贵会已了解这些阴谋，因此态度不太可能改变。

尽管如此，考虑到不法之徒可能趁机进一步从事不良活动，以及某些人可能因误解而受骗，我们特此致函。如果贵会的态度表现出不一致，麻烦随之而来，不仅会被公众鄙视，还将受到严厉惩罚，因为本队有责任防止任何人公开进行反对和平运动的活动。勿谓言之不预。

（盖章）：中国国民党反共
救国军特别服务队

established in East Tsu An Pang off Edinburgh Road, O.O.L.

Made by D.S.I. Liao Chung-chien. Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

Under the auspices of the Special Service
Corps of the Chung kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and
National Salvation Army, a "Moral Endeavour Society"
was recently formed at No.81, East Tsu An Pang, off
Edinburgh Road, O.O.L. with Sung Sing Fu ( 沈心撫 ),
ex-Chairman of the Nantao Traders Association
(defunct), and a professional organization promoter,
as chairman.

The society claims that it has for its object
the promotion of morality among members but it is
understood that it has been formed for the sole
purpose of acting as a liaison body between the
Corps
Special Service of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-
Comintern & National Salvation Army and the middle
class Chinese in the Western District, O.O.L., such as
owners of small factories and shops situated in that
area.

It is reported that the society will also
make endeavours to mediate in labour disputes in the
extra-Settlement roads area in the Western District.

Liao Chung Chien
D. S. I.

在中国国民党反共救国军特别服务队的主持下，“励志社”最近在越界筑路区域爱丁堡路旁东诸安浜81号成立，由前南市商会主席（已解散）兼职业组织推广人沈心抚（Sung Sing Fu，音译）担任主席。

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COMMISSIONER 21-DEC-1939）

The Commissioner

Under the pretext of guarding factories in the extra-
Settlement roads area in the western District from acts
of extortion by undesirable elements, the special
service corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern
& National Salvation Army has established two "Factory
Registration Offices" at No. 66, Lane 110, Nyi Yuen Road
(倪園路), off Brenan Road, and No.1103 Connaught Road,
O.O.L., respectively, for the purpose of registering
factories in the enclaves. According to the regulations
of the two factory registration offices, all factories in
the enclaves are compelled to register with the offices
and are required to pay a registration fee of $6.00 each.
After registration, a certificate will be issued and the
holder will be assured of protection by the Special Corps
of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-comintern & National
Salvation Army.

It is reported that during the past few days, members
of the corps have been paying visits to the various
industrial concerns in the enclaves in turn, warning them
to apply to the two offices in question for registration.

R. W. Mac Adie.
D. S. I.

D. C. ( Special Branch ).

November 29, 1939. Morning Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News:

FACTORIES BEING FORCED TO REGISTER

Shortly after 10 a.m. yesterday, a reporter of
the Hsin Kwang News Agency (新光社) secured the following
information:-
A "Factory Owners' Registration Office" is
operating in Lane No.110 Ni Wei Road (倪家路) off Brenan
Road in the Western District. Its officials are armed.
On the night of November 27, they carried off certain
articles of furniture etc. from several shops in the
vicinity and took them to Lane No.110 Ni Wei Road for
their own use.
Upon learning this, the reporter made a personal
inspection at the place and his investigation confirmed
the above report.
At about 5 p.m. information was received from
foreign factories to the effect that a number of factories
in the vicinity of Kong Ka Kiao (康家桥) were being forced
to apply for registration certificates which would be
issued at $6 each. Should a factory owner refuse to
register, certain measures would be taken to deal with him.
It is learned that the honorary chief of the
office is one Chang (张), with one Vai (萬) as chief.

1939年11月29日。晨间翻译。

《中美日报》：

工厂被迫登记

昨天上午10点后不久，《新光社》记者获得如下消息：
西区白利南路旁倪家路（Ni Wei Road）110弄内有一家“工厂主登记处”正在运作。其官员携带武器。11月27日晚，他们从附近几家商店搬走了一些家具等物品，并将其带到倪家路110弄供自己使用。
得知此事后，记者亲自前往该地视察，调查结果证实了上述报道。
下午5点左右，收到外籍工厂方面的消息，称康家桥（Kong Ka Kiao）附近的一些工厂正被迫申请登记证，每张收费6美元。如果工厂主拒绝登记，将对其采取某些措施。
据悉，该处的名誉主任姓张（Chang），主任姓万（Vai）。

On November 9, at 7.35 p.m., an assassination took place in the Van Lee Restaurant (萬利酒樓), 514 Foochow Road, in which two male Chinese named YANG TSING HAI (楊進海) and LOO TSE PING (羅志斌) were shot and killed. The culprits made good their escape after the shooting.

YANG TSING HAI was a Section Commander of the 3rd Section of the "Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army," with offices at No.29 Sing Loh Tsung, Singapore Road, S.O.L.. He was also conductor of two gambling dens called Tsung Hsing (振興) and Lien Yih (聯益), at 23 Ching Kya Hong off Jessfield Road, and Yanping Road, S.O.L. respectively.

The second victim LOO TSE PING was formerly an interpreter attached to the Western District Japanese Military Police Headquarters, 94 Jessfield Road. He was subsequently appointed officer in charge of a branch of the "Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army," at 12 Yoong Loh Tsung, Jessfield Road. Special Branch
report dated
1/11/39.

With reference to the attached trans-
lation of an extract from the "Mainichi", dated
31/10/39 on the murder of a pro-Japanese Chinese
in Zuh Hwei Yao, off Ferry Road, O.O.L. on
October 29, discreet enquiries show that the
deceased was named Tsang Siao San Tse ( 張小三子 ),
and was a member of the 3rd Section of the Chung
Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salva-
tion Army recently established in a straw hut
in Zuh Hwei Yao, off Ferry Road.

It is said that he was shot dead by
Kuh Shu Sung ( 葛樹森 ), the commander of the
Section, for having raped a woman who is a lover
of another member of the Section, residing at
No.24 Zuh Hwei Yao, There is no truth in the
report contained in the "Mainichi" that the deceased
was killed by terrorists.

MURDER OF A PRO-JAPANESE CHINESE

At 7.50 a.m. October 29, shooting was heard
in House No.24, Zah Fai Yao, Western District. Hurrying
to the house, the neighbours found a Chinese occupant of

immediately reported the matter to the Police.
The victim was known as a pro-Japanese.

一名亲华中国人的谋杀案

Made by D.S.I. Ling Chung Chien Forwarded by

Under the auspices of T.J. Lee (李秋野) or U.
Akino, a Korean, who is a section chief of the Crime
Detective Corps in the Western District and concurrently
in charge of the Japanese Special Service Section in Lane
61, No.81, Ninner Road, a dinner party will be held
in the Lido Restaurant, 306 Redhurst Road, at 6 p.m.
October 27, 1939, when some 140 persons connected with
the Wang Ching Wei Clique, including a number of prominent
merchants in the Western District, will be present.

For San-sing (潘省三), the ex-collector of the
Asia Club, 65 Carlton Road, who is at present active in
a move out for the revival of all pre-war merchant bodies
in Shanghai, and Jui Sung Lin (朱顺林), a notorious
figure in the underworld fraternity of the Western
District, O.O.L., will assist T.J. Lee in officiating at
the party.

It is reported that a discussion will take place
on measures for the revival of the various pre-war public
bodies in Shanghai in support of the movement for the
inauguration of a new government under Wang Ching Wei.

Ling Chung Chien

Made by D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by C Clauson

It is reported that at 7 a.m. October 17, three
members of the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo
Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army,
each armed with a pistol, called at House 8, Tsung In
Sing Teung (中一新村), Edinburgh Road, C.C.L., the
home of one Wong Tsu Chuan (王祖權), and conducted
a search allegedly for firearms. Seeing that Wong was
absent and that nothing of an incriminating nature was
found, the three took down a photograph of Wong from
the wall, warned the family members to send Wong
immediately to their office at No. 20 Sing Loh Tsung
(新樂), Singapore Road, C.C.L., for interrogation
and then withdrew.

Wong Tsu Chuan, tenant of the house, is the
proprietor of Doong Chi Silk Weaving Factory, No. 20

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. I. REGISTRY No. S. B. D. 923 C Date October 9, 1939.）

Subject. Pro-Wang Ching Wei Clique - to secure dominance over various Chinese Circles in Shanghai.
Made by...D.S.I. Liao Chung-chien, Forwarded by... C Crawford.

It is reported that the Wang Ching Wei Clique is accelerating its efforts to secure dominance over various local Chinese circles in the hope that when the proposed government under Wang Ching Wei is inaugurated (the inauguration was originally scheduled for October 10 and is now said to have been postponed to November 1) it will have the support of these circles and will receive greetings from them. In connection with these movements, the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army has organized four sections namely:-

1. Labour Movement Section in charge of Chang Kuh Chong (張克昌), a committee member of the local Postal Workers Union.
2. Merchant Movement Section in charge of Pan San Sing (潘省三), ex-conductor of the Asia Club, 65 Gordon Road.
3. Student Movement Section in charge of Chen Chi Zung (陳濟成), ex-principal of the Shanghai Middle School, 460 Chengtu Road.
4. Woman Circles Section in charge of (1) Miss Kyung Kwang Mei (金光楣), ex-proctor of the Hwai Kiu Middle School for Girls and head of a rival clique among the faculty of the school engaged in a dispute over the appointment of a new principal in March 1939. She is at present the principal of the Chien Shu Middle School situated at No. 537 Weihaiwei Road.

（批：This Robertson (Sp. Br.)）
（印：CONFIDENTIAL To Sec d C.G）
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 18 OCT. 1939）

主题：亲汪精卫派系 - 企图控制上海各华人圈子。
由...特别课督察廖仲坚（Liao Chung-chien）撰写，由... C Crawford 转呈。

据报道，汪精卫派系正加紧努力，以求控制上海当地各华人圈子，希望当拟议中的汪精卫政府成立时（原定成立日期为10月10日，现称已推迟至11月1日），能获得这些圈子的支持并收到他们的贺电。与此类活动相关，中国国民党反共救国军特别服务队已组织了四个分部，即：-

1. 劳工运动部，由当地邮政工会委员张克昌（Chang Kuh Chong）负责。
2. 商人运动部，由前戈登路（Gordon Road）65号亚洲俱乐部干事潘省三（Pan San Sing）负责。
3. 学生运动部，由前成都路460号上海中学校长陈济成（Chen Chi Zung）负责。
4. 妇女界部，由 (1) 金光楣小姐（Miss Kyung Kwang Mei）负责，她是怀久女子中学的前舍监，也是该校教员中一个 rival clique 的头目，曾卷入1939年3月关于任命新校长的纠纷。她目前是威海卫路537号建树中学的校长。

Date September 17, 1939.
Subject Disarming of police constables in Western District, U.O.L.
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. MacAdie

On September 15, three Shanghai Municipal Police
constables were robbed of their service pistols
on Jessfield Road by a number of armed plain-clothes
men while on September 16 a further two constables
were similarly disarmed on Brenan Road.

It is learned that the robberies are the work
of members of the Special Service Corps of the Chung
Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation
Army attached to the branch office of the organization
at 1081 Jessfield Road, U.O.L., and were carried out
with a view to:-
1. embarrassing and obstructing the S.M.P. authorities.
2. convincing members of the Chinese Branch that the
S.M.P. is powerless in the extra-Settlement roads
area in the Western District, thereby undermining
the morale of the former.

It is reported that these attacks will continue
until definite measures have been laid down in settle-
ment of the dispute over the question of policing the
extra-Settlement roads area in the Western District.

R. W. Mac Adie
D. S. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

9月15日，三名上海公共租界工部局警务处巡捕在极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）遭数名武装便衣男子抢劫，服务配枪被夺；9月16日，另有两名巡捕在布伦南路（Brenan Road）遭遇类似缴械事件。

据悉，上述抢劫案系“中国国民党反共救国军”特别服务队成员所为，该组织分支机构位于越界筑路区极司菲尔路1081号。其行动旨在：
1. 使上海公共租界工部局警务处当局难堪并加以阻挠。
2. 使华籍警员相信，上海公共租界工部局警务处在西区越界筑路区域无力行使职权，从而打击前者的士气。

据报，此类袭击将持续进行，直至就西区越界筑路区域的警务管辖权争议制定出明确的解决措施为止。

9月5日上午，刑事侦探科第308号探员王震菲（Wong Tseng Fee）报告称，9月4日上午9时30分，他在极司菲尔路76号附近行走时，遇见其朋友陈全才（Chen Chung Zai），32岁，高邮（Kompo）人，目前受雇于“中国国民党反共救国军”特别服务队，担任驻守极司菲尔路76号的警卫分队长。该探员称，陈告知他，特别服务队的高级成员正密切关注特别情报科（S....I.）人员在西区越界筑路区域的活动。据称，他们收到报告称，刑事侦探科第308号探员是由刑事侦探科督察施世良（Sih Se Liang）指派去侦查亲汪组织的活动，因此已发出指令，一旦在越界筑路区（O.O.L.）西区发现刑事侦探科第308号探员王震菲或特别情报科的任何其他探员在执行任务，即予杀害。

On the afternoon of July 15, 1939, with the assistance of Police constables of the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau, members of the Special Service Corps, 7C Jessfield Road, of the "Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army" (中國國民黨反共救國軍), a pro-Japanese armed corps at No. 6 Lane 95, Edinburgh Road distributed in the Western District, O.O.L., pamphlets and coloured paper slips of an anti-communist and pro-Wang Ching Wei nature purporting to have emanated from the Three People's Principles Anti-Communist Youths' Corps (三民主義反共青年團). The pamphlets contain an epistle addressed to Chinese youths urging them to support Wang Ching Wei and his peace policy of national salvation, while on the paper slips anti-communist and pro-Wang Ching Wei slogans appear.

Copies of similar pamphlets were also found on the afternoon of July 15, at the corner of Yu Ya Ching and Nanking Roads.

Attached to this report is a specimen of the pamphlet and the coloured paper slips in question together with translation.

C. Crawford
D. I.
D.C. (Special Branch)

1939年7月15日下午，在上海市公安局巡捕的协助下，“中国国民党反共救国军”（親日武裝團體）特别服务队成员（该队位于爱丁堡路95弄6号及极司菲尔路7C号）在越界筑路区（O.O.L.）西区分发了具有反共和亲汪精卫性质的传单及彩色纸条，声称出自“三民主义反共青年团”。传单中包含一封致中国青年的信，敦促他们支持汪精卫及其“和平救国”政策，而彩色纸条上则印有反共和亲汪精卫的标语。

7月15日下午，在虞洽卿路与南京路转角处也发现了类似的传单副本。

AN EPISTLE TO THE YOUTHS OF THE WHOLE NATION

Dear youthful Comrades :

For the existence and independence of the nation,
we have been fighting a sacred war of resistance for the
past two years. When we look back into history, we
cannot but recollect that prior to the August 13 Incident
the communists in China were about to meet defeat and
that the Kuomintang had fulfilled its mission of unifying
China preparatory to reconstructing a new nation. Reali-
zing their own precarious position and in order to save
themselves, the communists played upon the patriotic
sentiments of the people and rallied them under their
banner in the name of a war of resistance against Japan.
When the July 7 Incident broke, the door of peaceful
settlement was blocked by the exaggerated propaganda of
the communists thus frustrating the policy of national
reconstruction. The Kuomintang was compelled to
embark upon a war of resistance as a last resort in saving
the party and the nation.

The lesson gained in the sanguinary war of two years
has amply proved that China is incapable of extinction, and
this is realized by Japan. We feel that the time has
arrived for China and Japan to commence peace negotiations
on condition that the two nations be placed on an equal
footing.

Since his advocation of peace in Chungking, Mr. Wang
Ching Wei has candidly stressed the following point :-

"The purpose of a state is to maintain its

1939年7月15日下午在越界筑路区（C.O.L.）西区以及虞洽卿路与南京路转角处发现的亲汪精卫及反共传单译文

致全国青年书

亲爱的青年同志们：

为了国家的生存与独立，我们在过去两年中一直进行着神圣的抗战。回顾历史，我们不禁想起，在“八一三”事变之前，中国的共产党人即将面临失败，而国民党已完成统一中国的使命，为重建新国家做好准备。共产党人意识到自身处境岌岌可危，为了自救，利用人民的爱国情绪，以抗日为名将其聚集在自己的旗帜下。当“七七”事变爆发时，共产党人的夸大宣传阻塞了和平解决的大门，从而挫败了国家重建的政策。国民党被迫作为挽救党国最后的手段，踏上抗战之路。

两年血腥战争的教训充分证明，中国是不会灭亡的，这一点日本也已认识到。我们认为，中日两国在平等基础上开始和平谈判的时机已经到来。

自从汪精卫先生在重庆倡导和平以来，他坦率地强调了以下几点：

“国家的目的在于维持其

pages.en:
(2)
existence and independence whether at war
or peace. We should not shrink from
war should war be inevitable, and we
should not refuse negotiation for peace
when peace is possible. When peace is
to be concluded it should depend on whether
it adversely affects the existence and
independence of China."
This is the unfailing truth, which should serve as
a guide to the continued existence of this nation.
But the communists are against peace; they would rather
see China continue in her suicidal path of war for an
indefinite period than have her abandon the resurrected
Red Army and its political dominance which they obtained
under the plea of a war of resistance.
We fully realize that the time is now ripe for
peace and that the "principles of rapprochement, joint
anti-comintern and economic cooperation" as advocated
by Mr. Wang Ching Wei should form the basis for Sino-
Japanese cooperation for the establishment of permanent
peace in the Orient.
We firmly support the policy of national salvation
through peace; we reaffirm our faith in the Three People's
Principles; and we assert that we will concentrate our
strength with the will of the Fascist spirit and endeavour
to bring about national salvation and national reconstruction.
Youthful Comrades! Unite!
Support the peace policy of national salvation as
stated by Mr. Wang!
Oppose the Government's policy of continuing the
war of resistance!
pages.zh:
(2)
生存与独立，无论战时还是平时。如果战争不可避免，我们不应畏战；如果和平有可能，我们不应拒绝和谈。缔结和约应取决于是否不利于中国的生存与独立。”
这是永恒的真理，应作为本民族继续生存的指南。但共产党人反对和平；他们宁愿看到中国在无限期的自杀式战争道路上继续走下去，也不愿放弃他们借抗战之名获得的复活的红军及其政治统治地位。
我们充分认识到，现在和平的时机已经成熟，汪精卫先生所倡导的“善邻、共同防共、经济合作”原则，应成为中日合作的基础，以建立东方的永久和平。
我们坚决支持和平救国政策；我们重申对三民主义的信仰；并宣称我们将集中力量，秉持法西斯精神意志，努力实现救国与建国。
青年同志们！团结起来！
支持汪先生所述的和平救国政策！
反对政府继续抗战的政策！

On June 24, 1939, a search party from
Bubbling Well Station arrested one Nyi Sieu Zien
(嚴秀泉) for being in possession of
unlicensed firearms. As a result of information
obtained the arrest of Wong Sao Ching (王少慶)
was effected on July 2, 1939.
As they were suspected of indulging in
political activities, on July 3, 1939, Wong was
interrogated at length by Special Branch detectives
at Headquarters in consequence of which a statement
was obtained wherein he admitted being a member of
an armed gang with political interests.
On July 4, 1939, Nyi was also questioned by
Special Branch detectives and made a statement
which agreed in detail with that of Wong, the two
statements are attached hereto.
The prisoners were returned to Bubbling Well
Station on 3rd and 4th of July respectively.

1939年6月24日，静安寺捕房（Bubbling Well Station）搜查队逮捕了一名严秀泉（Nyi Sieu Zien），因其持有无照枪支。根据获得的情报，于1939年7月2日实施了王少庆（Wong Sao Ching）的逮捕。
由于怀疑他们从事政治活动，1939年7月3日，特别情报科探员在总部对王进行了详细审讯，由此获得一份供词，其中他承认自己是具有政治利益的武装团伙成员。
1939年7月4日，特别情报科探员也对严进行了讯问，并作出了一份供词，其细节与王的供词一致，两份供词附后。
两名囚犯分别于7月3日和4日被送回静安寺捕房。

The following is the statement of Nyi Sieu Zien (嚴秀泉), alias Nyi Shing (嚴鑫).
native of Wusieh ........................................taken by me D.P.S. Roberts
D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien
at Police Hdqrs. on the July 4, 1939 .......and interpreted by ....................................

I was employed as a printer for approximately ten years
in various local printing presses, including the Commercial
Press and the Chung Hwa Book Company. At the outbreak of
the Sino-Japanese hostilities in August, 1937, I returned to
my native place at Wusieh and stayed there until February,
1939 when I again came to Shanghai and commenced work at
the Roosevelt Terminal as a foreman coolie. I obtained this
position through the recommendation of a relative of mine
named Zung Vung Zien (陳文泉) who is employed as an account-
ant by the Roosevelt Terminal.

At the beginning of April 1939, through a friend of
mine named Tsang Ding Sung (張挺生) I joined an organiza-
tion which was termed a "Special Squad" and I later found
it was sponsored by Wang Ching Wei's clique.

Two of the coolies employed by the Roosevelt Terminal
namely Tsang Tien Zai (張天在) and Wong Sao Ching (王少慶)
were persuaded by me to join this group, our pay being $30
each month.

At the beginning of May, 1939, Tsang Tien Zai and I
were instructed by Loh Yao Ling (陸耀令), who acted as an
intermediary between Lao Wang (老王), a senior member of
the Special Squad, and our small party, to live in No.2
Tseng Nyeu Li (貞元里), Rue Lieutenant Petiot, and Tsang
Ding Sung (張挺生) and Wong Sao Ching (王少慶) to reside
in House 61 Woo Huh Faung (和合坊), Ave. Joffre, the rent
being paid by Loh Yao Ling who I believe obtained the money
from the Squad's headquarters situated in House 6 in a lane

我曾在包括商务印书馆和中华书局在内的本地多家印刷厂担任排字工人，历时约十年。1937 年 8 月中日战事爆发时，我返回家乡吴县，并在那里逗留至 1939 年 2 月，随后再次来到上海，开始在罗斯福终点站（Roosevelt Terminal）担任苦力领班。我是通过我的亲戚陈文泉（Zung Vung Zien）的介绍获得该职位的，他在罗斯福终点站担任会计。

1939 年 4 月初，通过我的朋友张挺生（Tsang Ding Sung），我加入了一个称为“特别行动队”的组织，后来我发现该组织是由汪精卫派系资助的。

我劝说罗斯福终点站雇佣的两名苦力，即张天在（Tsang Tien Zai）和王少庆（Wong Sao Ching），加入了这个团体，我们每人的月薪为 30 元。

1939 年 5 月初，陆耀令（Loh Yao Ling）指示我和张天在住在贝当路（Rue Lieutenant Petiot）贞元里 2 号，张挺生和王少庆住在霞飞路（Ave. Joffre）和合坊 61 号。陆耀令充当特别行动队高级成员“老王”与我们这个小团体之间的中间人。房租由陆耀令支付，我相信他是从位于爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）某弄堂 6 号的行动队总部获取的资金。

off Edinburgh Road.
This Special Squad which we had joined is believed
to be divided into a number of sections each comprising
five persons. The section to which I was attached consisted
of the following five men:-
1. Loh Yao Ling (陸耀令), Chief.
2. Tsang Ding Sung (張挺生), Assistant Chief.
3. Nyi Sieu Zien (嚴秀泉), alias Nyi Shing (嚴鑫).
4. Tsang Tien Zai (張天在).
5. Wong Sao Ching (王少慶).
Loh Yao Ling visited us frequently at No.2 Tseng Nyeu
Li, Rue Lieutenant Petiot, where we, Tsang Ding Sung, Nyi Sieu
Zien, Tsang Tien Zai and Wong Sao Ching, had our meals together
daily.
At about 6 p.m. on June 8, 1939 Loh Yao Ling visited
No.2 Tseng Nyeu Li, Rue Lieutenant Petiot, and instructed
Tsang Ding Sung, Wong Sao Ching, Tsang Tien Zai and me to
keep observation in the vicinity of Hwa Mei Wan Pao offices
at 172 Ave. Edward VII and report the movements of a male
Chinese who would arrive at the newspaper offices about 9 a.m.
daily in a motor car, the last two numbers of the licence as
far as I can remember were --66.
I proceeded to the appointed place on the 9th June, 1939
with Wong Sao Ching and we kept observation for four or five
days, the other two members Tsang Ding Sung and Tsang Tien
Zai taking their turn when we rested.
During this observation I saw two male Chinese arrive

据信，我们加入的这个特别行动队分为若干个小组，每组由五人组成。我所在的小组由以下五人组成：
1. 陆耀令（Loh Yao Ling），组长。
2. 张挺生（Tsang Ding Sung），副组长。
3. 严秀泉（Nyi Sieu Zien），别名严鑫（Nyi Shing）。
4. 张天在（Tsang Tien Zai）。
5. 王少庆（Wong Sao Ching）。
陆耀令经常到贝当路贞元里 2 号看望我们，在那里，我们——张挺生、严秀泉、张天在和王少庆——每天一起吃饭。
1939 年 6 月 8 日下午 6 点左右，陆耀令来到贝当路贞元里 2 号，指示张挺生、王少庆、张天在和我在爱德华七世路（Ave. Edward VII）172 号《华美晚报》（Hwa Mei Wan Pao）报社附近进行监视，并报告一名每日上午 9 点左右乘汽车到达报社的中国男子的行踪。据我回忆，该车牌照的最后两位数字是 --66。
1939 年 6 月 9 日，我和王少庆前往指定地点，我们监视了四五天，另外两名成员张挺生和张天在在我们休息时轮流值班。
在监视期间，我看到两名中国男子乘车

at the offices in a motor car but I would not be able to
identify them as I was some distance away from the spot.
Loh Yao Ling called at No.2 Tseng Nyeu Li, Rue Lt.
Petiot, at 6 p.m. daily to hear reports from us regarding
the result of our observation.
On or about June 14, 1939 Loh gave further instructions
at No.2 Tseng Nyeu Li, Rue Lt. Petiot, that we would now
be required to carry out observation at a house in Rue
Ferguson near Rue Dupleix, the number of which I have now
forgotten.
This address I found out was the home of the person we
had been watching at 172 Ave. Edward VII. I kept watch on
this place between June 14 and June 17, 1939 and noticed
that the man left his home in a motor car at about 9 a.m.
every morning. I was accompanied by Tsang Tien Zai while
carrying out the observation.
In the evening of June 17, 1939, Lao Wang, the senior
member of the Special Squad, accompanied by Loh Yao Ling,
came to No.2 Tseng Nyeu Li, Rue Lt. Petiot, and instructed
that Tsang Tien Zai, Wong Sao Ching and I attend the office
of the Special Squad on the morning of June 18, 1939 to
undergo some training.
On the morning of June 18, 1939 at about 8 a.m. Lao
Wang came to Tseng Nyeu Li and escorted Tsang Tien Zai,
Wong Sao Ching and myself to House No.6, a two-storeyed
house, in an alleyway off Edinburgh Road. We travelled
on a No.2 bus from Ave. Foch. The house was guarded by a

陆耀令每天下午 6 点会到贝当路贞元里 2 号，听取我们要关于监视结果的汇报。
1939 年 6 月 14 日左右，陆在贝当路贞元里 2 号发出进一步指示，要求我们现在对杜美路（Rue Ferguson）靠近巨籁达路（Rue Dupleix）的一处房屋进行监视，具体门牌号我现在已忘记。
我后来得知，这个地址就是我们在爱德华七世路 172 号监视的那个人的家。1939 年 6 月 14 日至 6 月 17 日期间，我对此地进行了监视，注意到该男子每天早上 9 点左右乘车离开家。在执行监视任务时，由张天在陪同我。
1939 年 6 月 17 日晚，特别行动队的高级成员“老王”在陆耀令的陪同下，来到贝当路贞元里 2 号，并指示张天在、王少庆和我于 1939 年 6 月 18 日上午前往特别行动队办公室接受一些训练。
1939 年 6 月 18 日上午 8 点左右，“老王”来到贞元里，护送张天在、王少庆和我前往爱丁堡路一条弄堂内的 6 号房屋，这是一栋两层楼的建筑。我们从霞飞路乘坐 2 路公共汽车前往。该房屋由数名

- 4 -

number of male Chinese armed with pistols but these did not
stop us, apparently they had been informed of our coming.
We were conducted by Lao Wang to a room on the upper
floor above the kitchen which is occupied by a man named
Sung (沈 ) who is the chief and is directly in charge of the
different sections. In this room we were given instructions
how to use a pistol by a male Chinese, aged about 30,
height 5'4", dressed in blue jacket and pants, who gave
Tsang Tien Zai and I a Mauser pistol each and Wong Sao Ching
a smaller and different one. We practised aiming and loading
but without being given any bullets. After practising for a
while our instructor told us to return him the pistols where-
upon he loaded each one with a full magazine and put the
safety catch on. He informed us that when we wanted to fire
we should release the catch and pull the trigger.
Lao Wang who had been in attendance the whole time
told us that we would be required to kill the person whom
we had been watching and that the act would be carried out in
the vicinity of the residence in Rue Ferguson. He then told
me that the name of the person to be assassinated was Tsu
Tsoh Tung (朱作全) and remarked that Loh Yao Ling and Tsang
Ding Sung were already at the scene and would keep observation
on us.
At about 9.15 a.m. Tsang Tien Zai, Wong Sao Ching and
myself left the address in Edinburgh Road, all armed with
the pistols we had practised with, hidden under our gowns
and proceeded to Rue Ferguson on foot, arriving there about

手持手枪的中国男子把守，但他们没有阻拦我们，显然他们已被告知我们将到来。
“老王”将我们带到厨房楼上的一间房间，该房间由一名姓沈（Sung）的男子占用，他是负责人，直接管辖各个小组。在这个房间里，一名约 30 岁、身高 5 英尺 4 英寸、身穿蓝色夹克和裤子的中国男子指导我们如何使用手枪。他给了我和张天在每人一支毛瑟手枪，给王少庆一支较小且型号不同的手枪。我们练习了瞄准和装弹，但没有发给子弹。练习了一会儿后，教官让我们交还手枪，随后他为每支手枪装满弹匣并打开保险栓。他告诉我们，想射击时应释放保险栓并扣动扳机。
全程在场的“老王”告诉我们，我们需要杀死我们一直监视的那个人，行动将在杜美路住所附近进行。然后他告诉我，将被暗杀的人名叫朱作全（Tsu Tsoh Tung），并说陆耀令和张挺生已经在现场，并将监视我们的行动。
上午 9 点 15 分左右，张天在、王少庆和我离开爱丁堡路的地址，我们都带着练习过的手枪，藏在长袍下，步行前往杜美路，大约于

- 5 -

9.30 a.m.. June 18th was a Sunday and we understood that
the person to be assassinated would leave his home a little
later than usual.
On arrival at the place we saw Loh and Tsang standing
about 30 yards away. We recognized them but refrained from
speaking to them and proceeded to the house to inspect the
locality. We kept watch for approximately one hour but
the person did not leave his home although his motor car
was seen to be parked outside the house. I began to be
afraid and said so to Wong Sao Ching who was also not keen
on the project. Tsang Tien Zai, Wong Sao Ching and I all
showed an inclination to retreat. A little later several
Annamite police constables approached so we informed Loh
Yao Ling and Tsang Ding Sung that we thought the Police
knew of the plans and that we had better return to the
office. They agreed to our proposal and Tsang Tien Zai,
Wong Sao Ching and I returned to House No.6, Edinburgh Road,
the office of the Special Squad. On entering the premises
I saw a number of male Chinese armed with Mauser pistols.
We were allowed to pass as they were told we would return
some time later. In the office we were met by Lao Wong
and he told us to return the pistols which we did.
On June 20, 1939 Lao Wang called again at No.2 Tseng
Nyeu Li, Rue Lt. Petiot and asked me to accompany him to
the vicinity of Koo Ka Zah Park, Route Vallon where, after
waiting for about half an hour I saw a male Chinese dressed
in a long grey Chinese gown approach Lao Wang and hand him

- 5 -

上午 9 点 30 分到达。6 月 18 日是星期日，我们得知被暗杀者会比平时稍晚离开家。
到达该地后，我们看到陆和张站在大约 30 码外。我们认出了他们，但没有与他们交谈，而是前往那所房子勘察地形。我们监视了大约一个小时，但那人没有离开家，尽管看到他的汽车停在屋外。我开始感到害怕，并告诉了同样对该计划不热衷的王少庆。张天在、王少庆和我都表现出撤退的意向。过了一会儿，几名安南巡捕走近，于是我们告诉陆耀令和张挺生，我们认为警方已经知道了计划，我们最好返回办公室。他们同意了我们的提议，张天在、王少庆和我回到了爱丁堡路 6 号，即特别行动队的办公室。进入 premises 时，我看到许多手持毛瑟手枪的中国男子。由于他们被告知我们稍后会回来，因此允许我们通过。在办公室里，我们见到了“老王”，他让我们交还手枪，我们照办了。
1939 年 6 月 20 日，“老王”再次来到贝当路贞元里 2 号，让我陪他去法租界华龙路（Route Vallon）顾家宅公园（Koo Ka Zah Park）附近。在那里等了大约半小时后，我看到一名身穿灰色长衫的中国男子走近“老王”，递给他一

- 6 -

a basket of loquats ("Bee-ba" fruit) which Lao Wang accepted.
We returned to No.2 Tseng Nyeu Li, Rue Lt. Petiot and on
entering the room Lao Wang informed me that the basket contain-
ed two pistols which would be used to carry out the murder which
we failed to execute on June 18, 1939. Lao Wang departed but
left the basket of fruit.

Later Tsang Tien Zai, Wong Sao Ching and I discussed
this further plan at length and decided that the mission,
which could have serious consequences to us, be not carried
out, and that Lao Wang be informed that we thought the chauffeur
of the intended victim would be able to identify us. On
June 23, 1939, when Lao Wang visited us at No.2 Tseng Nyeu
Li, Rue Lt. Petiot we told him of our decision and he informed
us that we must wait for an answer.

On June 24, 1939, a note was left at No.2 Tseng Nyeu Li,
Rue Lt. Petiot, by Loh Yao Ling written by Lao Wang instructing
me to return the two pistols to Edinburgh Road. At about
8.40 p.m. Wong Sao Ching and I left Tseng Nyeu Li, Rue Lt.
Petiot and placed our pistols in our trouser belts, and from
the corner of Ave. Foch and Chengtu Road took a west bound
No.2 bus to Edinburgh Road.

About 50 yards east of Edinburgh Road, the bus suddenly
stopped and I saw a police party board the bus. I attempted to
discard my pistol but was discovered by the police and was
arrested. Wong Sao Ching was not arrested by the police so I
assumed that he had managed to discard his pistol and escape
during the confusion that followed the discovery of my pistol.
I was taken to Bubbling Well Station.
(Signed) Nyi Sieu Zien.

- 6 -

篮枇杷（“Bee-ba”果），“老王”收下了。
我们回到贝当路贞元里 2 号，进屋后，“老王”告诉我，篮子里装着两支手枪，将用于执行我们在 1939 年 6 月 18 日未能实施的谋杀。“老王”离开了，但留下了那篮水果。

后来，张天在、王少庆和我详细讨论了这个进一步的计划，决定不执行这项可能给我们带来严重后果的任务，并告知“老王”，我们认为预定受害者的司机能够认出我们。1939 年 6 月 23 日，当“老王”在贝当路贞元里 2 号拜访我们时，我们告诉了他我们的决定，他告诉我们必须等待答复。

1939 年 6 月 24 日，陆耀令在贝当路贞元里 2 号留下了一张由“老王”写的便条，指示我将两支手枪送回爱丁堡路。晚上 8 点 40 分左右，王少庆和我离开贝当路贞元里，将手枪放在裤腰带上，从霞飞路和成都路的拐角处乘坐向西行驶的 2 路公共汽车前往爱丁堡路。

在爱丁堡路以东约 50 码处，公共汽车突然停下，我看到一队警察登上公共汽车。我试图丢弃手枪，但被警察发现并被捕。王少庆未被警察逮捕，所以我推测他在发现我的手枪后的混乱中设法丢弃了手枪并逃脱。
我被带往静安寺捕房。
（签名）严秀泉。

The following is the statement of Wong Sao Ching (王少慶) alias Wong Pei Shing (王必兴)
native of Taichow, Kompo, taken by me D.P.S. Roberts
D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien
at Police Hdqrs. on the July 3, 1939 and interpreted by

My name is Wong Sao Ching alias Wong Pei Shing (王必兴),
aged 28, native of Taichow, Kompo, married, residing at 61
Woo Huh Faung (和合坊 ), Avenue Joffre.

At the age of 15, I came from my native home to Shanghai
and worked as a coolie on various wharfs in Nantao. After
the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities in Shanghai in
August, 1937, I left Nantao and joined the Roosevelt Terminal
as a coolie (No.395).

At the beginning of February, 1939, one Nien Shing
(嚴鑫 ) was appointed by the management of the Roosevelt
Terminal as a foreman coolie; he later left and joined some
organization.

In the middle of April 1939, Nien Shing told me while
I was working on the wharf that he could secure a far better
job for me and asked if I would accept it. On being question-
ed as to the nature of the employment, Nien stated that
"Central" (中央) (National Government) was recruiting
secret agents and should I join I would have a very hopeful
future. He also told me that the pay would be about $30.00
per mensem.

On May 6, 1939, Nien took me to the Van Saung Tea Shop
(萬商茶樓 ), junction of Fokien and Canton Roads, and Tsang
Tien Zai (張天在 ), another coolie of the Roosevelt Terminal
who also expressed his willingness to work as a secret agent,
accompanied us. There we met Loh Yao Ling (陸耀令 ) and
Tsang Ding Sung (張挺生 ) who, we were told, were members of
the secret service and would take charge of a section in which

以下为王少慶（Wong Sao Ching），又名王必兴（Wong Pei Shing），广东高州人，于1939年7月3日在警察总部由我，副督察罗伯茨（D.P.S. Roberts）及廖仲坚副督察（D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien）所取得的供词，并由……翻译。

我叫王少慶，又名王必兴，28岁，广东高州人，已婚，住霞飞路和合坊61号。

15岁时，我从家乡来到上海，在南市各码头做苦力。1937年8月上海中日战事爆发后，我离开南市，加入罗斯福码头（Roosevelt Terminal）做苦力（编号395）。

1939年2月初，严鑫（Nien Shing）被罗斯福码头管理层任命为苦力工头；他后来离职，加入了某个组织。

1939年4月中旬，严鑫在我在码头工作时告诉我，他可以为我谋得一份好得多的工作，并问我是否愿意接受。当问及工作性质时，严鑫称“中央”（国民政府）正在招募秘密特工，如果我加入，前途将很有希望。他还告诉我，月薪约为30元。

1939年5月6日，严鑫带我到福建路与广东路交界处的万商茶楼（Van Saung Tea Shop），罗斯福码头的另一名苦力张天在（Tsang Tien Zai）也表达了担任秘密特工的意愿，随同我们前往。在那里，我们见到了陆耀令（Loh Yao Ling）和张挺生（Tsang Ding Sung），据称他们是特务机关成员，将负责一个分部，我们将

The same evening the four of us, Tsang Ding Sung, Tsang
Tien Zai, Nien Shing and myself obtained a room in the
Sing Sung Yu Lodging House in the vicinity of Great World
Amusement Resort. Loh Yao Ling later visited us and paid
us $30.00, such this being our wages for the month of May.

On May 8, Tsang Ding Sung and I went to live in a
room on the second floor of House 61, Woo Huh Faung, Avenue

The four of us were instructed to attend various tea shops

1939年6月17日晚，老王（Lao Wang）——特务机关的一名高级职员，曾与陆耀令多次一同到访我们在霞飞路和合坊以及贝当路卤元里2号的住所——指示严鑫、张天在和我于次日上午前往特务机关分部办公室接受训练。第二天早上，即1939年6月18日，

at about 8.15 a.m. Lao Wang came to No.2 Tseng Nyeu Lee, Rue
Lieutenant Petiot where we were waiting and took us to the
office of the secret service section situated at House 6,
inside an alleyway off Edinburgh Road.

On arrival at the house, we were led inside and in
an upstairs room Lao Wang handed us over to a male Chinese
dressed in blue jacket and pants who gave us instructions
in the use of pistol. After we had had some practice at
aiming, loading and pulling the trigger, Tsang Tien Zai and
Nien Shing were each given a Mauser pistol and I a small one
of different type. The person in blue jacket and pants
then loaded the pistols for us placing one round of ammunition
in the breech and then put the safety catch in the safe
position. He told us that in case we wanted to fire, we
just had to release the safety catch and pull the trigger.
At this time Lao Wang told us that we were to kill the
person whom we had been watching and this was to be carried
out in the vicinity of his residence at 63 Rue Ferguson.
He remarked that Loh Yao Ling and Tsang Ding Sung were
already in the vicinity of the place to supervise us and
if it was successful, a reward would be forthcoming.
Tsang Tien Zai, Nien Shing and I left the office at about
9.15 a.m. and proceeded to 63 Rue Ferguson on foot, arriving
there at about 9.30 a.m.. June 18 was a Sunday and we
understood that the man would leave his home a little later
than usual.

On arriving at the place, we saw Loh Yao Ling and Tsang

上午8点15分左右，老王来到贝当路卤元里2号，我们正那里等候，随后他将我们带到位于爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）某弄堂内6号的特务机关分部办公室。

到达该房屋后，我们被带进屋内，在楼上的一间房间里，老王将我们移交给一名身穿蓝色夹克和裤子的中国男子，他向我们讲授手枪的使用方法。在进行了一些瞄准、装弹和扣动扳机的练习后，张天在和严鑫各获赠一支毛瑟手枪，我则获得一支不同类型的小手枪。那名穿蓝衣蓝裤的男子随后为我们装填手枪，在枪膛内放入一发子弹，然后将保险栓置于安全位置。他告诉我们，如果想射击，只需释放保险栓并扣动扳机即可。此时，老王告诉我们，我们要杀死我们一直监视的那个人，行动将在其位于费格森路63号的住所附近进行。他说陆耀令和张挺生已经在该地附近监督我们，如果行动成功，将会有奖赏。张天在、严鑫和我于上午9点15分左右离开办公室，步行前往费格森路63号，约在上午9点30分到达。6月18日是星期日，我们得知那人会比平时稍晚一些离家。

Ding Sung were already in the vicinity of House 63 Rue
Ferguson. The three of us realizing the seriousness of
the mission became afraid and took a half-hearted observation
yet we dared not disobey the order as it was common knowledge
that such action would meet with severe punishment from the
secret office. I, therefore, went near to the chauffeur
who was cleaning the motor car standing in front of the house
(No.63) and purposely showed him the pistol which I then had
in my hand, half covered by my sleeve. He immediately went
into the house and after a while an elderly amah came out,
walked to a street along Rue Ferguson and returned with three
Annamite police constables. On seeing the policemen approach,
we three, Tsang Tien Zai, Nien Shing and myself, went to
Loh Yao Ling and Tseng Ding Sung and told them that we would
not carry out the murder that day and thought it would be
better to postpone the business. They agreed and the three
of us returned to House 6, off Edinburgh Road. There we saw
a number of armed guards outside the house, but we were admit-
ted without being questioned as the guards had received
instructions from Lao Wang that we would be back in an hour
or two. In the office we met Lao Wang and reported what had
happened to him. He gave instructions that the work must be
done and we should try a few days later. During the time I
was in the house, I saw no less than 20 persons all of whom
were armed with Mauser pistols. Tsang Tien Zai, Nien Shing
and I later handed over our pistols to Lao Wong, left the
premises and returned to No.2 Tseng Nyeu Li, Rue Lieutenant

On June 20 or 21, 1939 Lao Wang called at no.2 Tseng Nyeu Li, Rue Lt. Petiot again and took Nien Shing away to a certain place not known to me and both later returned with two pistols which were concealed in a basket of loquats ("bee ba" fruit). Nien stated that the weapons were to be used to carry out our former mission.

After a lengthy discussion the three of us, Tsang Tien Zai, Nien Shing and myself, decided to tell Lao Wang that we could not execute his orders as it was possible that the chauffeur might be able to identify us. We told Lao Wang the following day when he called on us and he gave instructions that we should wait.

At 6 p.m. June 24, 1939, I went as usual to No.2 Tseng Nyeu Li, Rue Lt. Petiot for dinner and I was told by Nien that Loh Yao Ling had left a note at the house instructing that the two pistols should be returned to the office.

At about 8.40 p.m. Nien Shing and I, each placing a pistol in our trouser belts, left No.2 Tseng Nyeu Li, Rue Lieutenant Petiot and walked northward to Avenue Foch where we boarded a west bound No.2 bus for Edinburgh Road. As the bus passed Tifeng Road I stood up ready to alight at the next stop, Edinbrugh Road, but when the bus was about 50 yards to the east of Edinbrugh Road, it was stopped by a police search party. As I was standing at the time, I saw clearly the movements of the police and and immediately discarded my pistol on the floor of the bus. The police

1939年6月20日或21日，老王再次来到贝当路卤元里2号，将严鑫带到一个我不清楚的地方，后来两人带着两支藏在一篮枇杷（“bee ba” fruit）里的手枪回来。严鑫称这些武器将用于执行我们之前的任务。

经过长时间讨论，我们三人——张天在、严鑫和我——决定告诉老王，我们无法执行他的命令，因为司机可能会认出我们。第二天老王来看望我们时，我们告诉了他这一决定，他指示我们等待。

1939年6月24日下午6点，我像往常一样去贝当路卤元里2号吃晚饭，严鑫告诉我，陆耀令在屋里留了一张纸条，指示将两支手枪归还给办公室。

晚上8点40分左右，严鑫和我各自将一支手枪藏在裤腰带里，离开贝当路卤元里2号，向北走到霞飞路（Avenue Foch），在那里搭乘一辆向西行驶的2路电车前往爱丁堡路。当电车经过狄思威路（Tifeng Road）时，我站起来准备在下一站爱丁堡路下车，但当电车行驶至爱丁堡路以东约50码处时，被警方搜查队拦停。由于我当时站着，清楚地看到了警察的行动，并立即将手枪丢弃在电车地板上。警察

July 1, 1939
9236
7 31
Kidnapping of Secret Service Agents of the National
Government from the King Kong Restaurant, Rue Wagner

From a usually reliable source, it has been learned
that the two Chinese who were rumoured to have been kid-
napped by certain unknown persons from the King Kong
Restaurant, Rue Wagner, in the evening of June 22, 1939,
are actually two section chiefs of the secret intelligence
service of the Chungking Government operating in Shanghai.
One of the two persons kidnapped is reported to be named
Hsu Yien (許 燕) but the name of the other is not known.
After having been taken away from the restaurant, they
were said to have been sent to 76 Jessfield Road, O.O.L.
and were interviewed there by Ting Luh Tsung (丁默村),
formerly Chief of the Military Investigation Section of
Military Affairs Commission of the National Government
and at present Director of the "Special Service Corps
of the "Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National
Salvation Army" (中國國民黨剷共救國軍別動隊), a pro-
Japanese and pro-Wang Ching Wei organization with head-
quarters at House 10, Lane 95, Edinburgh Road, O.O.L..
They were warned by Ting to leave Shanghai as soon as
possible and were released separately the same evening.
Ting Luh Tsung is said to know the majority of the
senior secret service agents of the National Government
in Shanghai for most of them were under his control when
he was Chief of the Investigation Section of the Military
Affairs Commission. Ting is a staunch supporter of
Wang Ching Wei and, following the latter, changed his
allegiance from the National Government and is now work-
ing for the Japanese.
His arrival in Shanghai (about the end of April, 1939)
has been the cause of a general reorganization in the
secret service of the National Government operating in

关于瓦格纳路（Rue Wagner）金宫餐厅（King Kong Restaurant）国民政府特工被绑架案

据通常可靠的消息来源获悉，传闻于1939年6月22日晚在瓦格纳路金宫餐厅被某些不明身份者绑架的两名中国人，实际上是重庆政府在沪运作的秘密情报服务的两名科长。据报道，被绑两人中一人名为许燕（Hsu Yien），另一人姓名不详。据说他们被带离餐厅后，被送往极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）76号，并在那里接受了丁默村（Ting Luh Tsung）的问话。丁默村曾任国民政府军事委员会军事情报处处长，现任“中国国民党铲共救国军别动队”主任，该组织为亲日及亲汪精卫组织，总部设在爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）95弄10号。丁警告他们尽快离开上海，并于当晚将他们分别释放。据说丁默村认识国民政府在沪的大部分高级特工，因为在他担任军事委员会调查处处长期间，这些人大多受其控制。丁是汪精卫的坚定支持者，追随汪精卫改变了对国民政府的效忠，目前正为日本人工作。
他的抵达上海（约在1939年4月底）导致了国民政府在沪秘密情报服务的全面重组，

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. 9236
Section 1, Special Branch
REPORT
Date June 27, 1939.
Subject Tsang Vung Ziang (張文祥) and Zee Ching Hoong (徐金洪),
two criminal suspects.
Made by. D.S.I. Lino Chung Chien Forwarded by. C. Crawford D. I.

Reference to the two prisoners, Tsang Vung Ziang
and Zee Ching Hoong, who were arrested at 265 Rue
Ratard on 28/5/39 on suspicion of having connections
with the armed criminals arrested by detectives of
Bubbling Well Station (Vide Misc. 209/39 BW), Zee
Ching Hoong, the second named. has no record in the
Special Branch. The name Tsang Vung Ziang (張文祥),
however, appeared twice in Special Branch reports
as follows :-

"Tsang Vung Ziang, coolie, arrested by the
Municipal Police on 28/8/32 in the Tung Woo
Lodging House at 20 Nan Shiang Feng Loong
off Nanking Road, on suspicion of having
instigated the throwing of acid and sulphuric
bombs at buses; released by the S.S.D. Court,
there being insufficient evidence to sustain
a charge (Vide I.R. 29/8/32 and 13/9/32).

"Tsang Vung Ziang, Chief of the 1st sub-section
(60 men) of the Woosung-Shanghai Special
Section of the Guerilla Main Corps of the
Military Affairs Commission of the National
Government. His superior officer is one
Hsiung Chien Tung (熊劍東) (Vide Special
Branch report dated 3/2/39).

There is no connection, however, between the
Tsang Vung Ziang at present in custody at Bubbling
Well Station and Tsang Vung Ziang mentioned above
as having a Special Branch record.

主题 张文祥（Tsang Vung Ziang）和徐金洪（Zee Ching Hoong），两名刑事嫌疑人。
制作人. 侦探副督察林崇坚（Lino Chung Chien，音译） 转呈人. C. Crawford 侦探督察

关于两名囚犯张文祥和徐金洪，他们于1939年5月28日在拉塔德路（Rue Ratard）265号因涉嫌与静安寺捕房侦探逮捕的武装罪犯有关联而被捕（参见杂项档案 209/39 BW），其中排名第二的徐金洪在特务科无记录。然而，张文祥（Tsang Vung Ziang）的名字曾两次出现在特务科报告中，如下所示：

“张文祥，苦力，于1932年8月28日因涉嫌煽动向公共汽车投掷酸液和硫酸炸弹，在南京路附近的南翔丰隆20号同武旅馆被工部局警务处逮捕；因证据不足无法提起诉讼，由特别法庭释放（参见1932年8月29日和9月13日情报报告）。

“张文祥，国民政府军事委员会游击总队沪淞特别区第一分队（60人）队长。其上级军官为熊剑东（Hsiung Chien Tung）（参见1939年2月3日特务科报告）。

然而，目前关押在静安寺捕房的张文祥与上述有特务科记录的张文祥之间并无关联。

Regarding the two prisoners, discreet enquiries
have been made by members of this Branch and the
result substantiates the report of Bubbling Well
Station dated 20/6/39 - Misc. No.298/39, to the effect
that, just prior to their arrest, both Tsang Vung Zing
and Zee Ching Hoong were recruited by Chiu Siao Er Ts,
(戚小二子), now in custody at Bubbling Well Station
on a charge of armed extortion, and joined the secret
pro-Japanese organization at 10/95 Edinburgh Road,
O.C.L., which has now assumed the title "Special
Service Corps of the Chun-Tuo Kuomintang Anti-
Comintern and National Salvation Army" (中國國民黨共
救國軍別動隊), but they have no connection with the
gang of armed criminals who were responsible for
numerous armed outrages on outside roads in the
Western District and who formerly operated as members
of the "Chinese Youths' Anti-Japanese and Traitors
Extermination Iron and Blood Corps." (中國青年抗日鋤奸鐵血軍).

Liao Chung Chen.
D. S. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

SECRET
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S.1, Special Branch
REPORT
Date July 6, 1939
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
REGISTRY
File No. S. B. D. 7236
Station,
Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern
onal Salvation Army", 10/95 Edinburgh Road.
Chung Chien, Forwarded by C Crawford

It is reported that the members of the "Special
Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern
and National Salvation Army", 10/95 Edinburgh Road,
have been increased from 150 to 230 during the past
fortnight and the majority are now armed with Mauser
and other brands of pistols. Persons who wish to join
the organization are required first to secure the
recommendation of two members and should they be
admitted to membership, will receive $30 per mensem
as wages, minus $8.00 for food and another $8.00 for
uniform which is supplied to them by the organization.
A new member will be paid the sum of $140.00 should he
join in possession of a Mauser pistol and $60.00 for
any other kind of pistol.

Li Shih Chung (李士群), assistant director
of the corps removed on June 28, 1939, from his home
at 67 Great Western Road to 76 Jessfield Road, C.O.L.,
which premises are occupied by Ting Muh Tsung (丁默村).

At present the 230 members of the corps are
distributed as follows :-
House 10/95 Edinburgh Road ............ 130
House 76 Jessfield Road ............... 60
House 6/95 Edinburgh Road ............. 40

It is reported that beginning from June 26, 1939,
the members accommodated at 76 Jessfield Road will be
required to undergo a course of training which will
consist of physical exercise and the use of pistols.

据报道，“中国国民党铲共救国军别动队”（爱丁堡路95弄10号）的成员在过去两周内已从150人增加到230人，大多数人现在配备了毛瑟牌及其他品牌的手枪。希望加入该组织的人必须先获得两名成员的推荐，如果被接纳为成员，每月将获得30美元工资，扣除8美元伙食费和8美元由组织提供的制服费。如果新成员自带毛瑟手枪加入，将获得140.00美元，若携带其他种类手枪，则获得60.00美元。

该队副队长李士群（Li Shih Chung）于1939年6月28日从大西路67号的住所搬至极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）76号，该处由丁默村（Ting Muh Tsung）占用。

目前，该队230名成员的分布如下：
爱丁堡路95弄10号 ............ 130人
极司菲尔路76号 ............... 60人
爱丁堡路95弄6号 ............. 40人

据报道，从1939年6月26日开始，居住在极司菲尔路76号的成员将被要求接受包括体能训练和使用手枪在内的课程训练。

Section 1, Special Branch,
June 24, 1939.
Secret Pro-Japanese organization at House 10, Lane 95 Edinburgh Rd.
O. O. L.

The secret pro-Japanese organization which has an office at
House 10 Lane 95 Edinburgh Road, first came to the notice of the
Municipal Police on April 11, 1939, when a follower of Li Shih
Chung (李向群), Chief of the Office, was taken into custody by
the Municipal Police together with a pedestrian on Edinburgh Road
near Great Western Road while he was making an illegal attempt to
effect the arrest of the pedestrian whom he suspected of spying.

Subsequent enquiries revealed that the organization came into
existence about the beginning of March 1939, at 67 Great Western
Road, the home of Li Shih Chung with the sole object of promoting
an anti-Comintern and pro-peace movement, under the auspices of
the Japanese Military Authorities. It removed to its present
address, 10/95 Edinburgh Road, on March 27, 1939. When the organi-
zation was first formed, Li engaged himself in the recruiting of
members and announced that he would direct them in an extensive
anti-Comintern, Pro-Peace and National Salvation Movement.

Li Shih Chung, chief of the organization, was prior to the
outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities in August 1937, an
employee of the Bureau of Social Affairs of the Shanghai City
Government and concurrently was assigned by the Central Kuomi
to assist the Public Safety Bureau in the suppression of com
activities in Shanghai. Some time after the fall of Shang in
November 1937 —— a Dai Fok Steamboat Company (大福) at 998
North Soochow Road, operating three steamboats between Shanghai
and Wusieh under the supervision of the Japanese Inland Navigatio
Bureau, but the concern was dissolved in November 1938 following
the introduction by the Japanese authorities of certain new res-
trictive measures rendering the navigation in the inland waters
by steamboats of the company practically impossible. It is
reported to have a large circle of friends of Japanese nationality,
including Sergeant Major Shita of the Japanese Military Police,
94 Jessfield Road, O.O.L., and a large number of Officials of the
local Japanese Consulate-General. After the closing down of the
pages.zh:
第一科，特别支部，
1939年6月24日。
爱丁堡路95弄10号的秘密亲日组织。
O. O. L.

位于爱丁堡路95弄10号设有办事处的秘密亲日组织，于1939年4月11日首次引起工部局警务处的注意。当时，该办事处主任李向群（Li Shih Chung）的一名追随者，在爱丁堡路近大西路处试图非法逮捕一名他怀疑是间谍的行人时，与该行人一同被工部局警务处拘捕。

随后的调查表明，该组织约于1939年3月初在李向群的住所——大西路67号成立，其唯一目的是在日本军方的支持下，推动反共产国际及“和平”运动。该组织于1939年3月27日迁至现址，即爱丁堡路95弄10号。组织初建时，李致力于招募成员，并宣布将指导他们开展大规模的反共产国际、亲“和平”及救国运动。

该组织主任李向群，在1937年8月中日敌对行动爆发前，曾是上海市政府社会局的一名雇员，同时受国民党中央委派，协助公安局镇压上海的共产党活动。1937年11月上海沦陷后不久——他在北苏州路998号的大福轮船公司（Dai Fok Steamboat Company）任职，该公司在日本内河航运局的监管下，运营三艘往返于上海与吴淞（Wusieh）之间的轮船，但随着日本当局实施某些新的限制措施，使得该公司的轮船实际上无法在内河航行，该公司遂于1938年11月解散。据报他拥有广泛的日本籍朋友圈，包括住在极司菲尔路94号的日本宪兵曹长Shita（音译），O.O.L.，以及当地日本总领事馆的众多官员。随着

pages.en:
- 2 -

Dah Foh Steamboat Company, Li, it is reported, became a secret
intelligence agent of the Japanese Military and, to facilitate
his activities, he secured the cooperation of members of Wang
Ching Wei's clique. By his diligence and good service he is said
to have gained the confidence of the local Japanese authorities,
hence his appointment in charge of the organization.

Towards the end of April 1939, the Japanese authorities and
the Wang Ching Wei clique reached an agreement according to which
Ting Muh Tsung (丁默村), was appointed director of the organizatic
superseding Li Shih Chung in the office. Ting is a staunch sup-
porter of Wang Ching Wei and was formerly chief of the Investiga-
tion Section of the Military Affairs Commission of the National
Government. He is stated to be a man of the military type and
entertains a strong belief in the motto that "might is right".

Immediately after he became director of the organization, he
drew up a plan which provides for the following:-

1. The recruiting of men from the underworld fraternity as members
who are to be made instruments in combating communism - a
measure which was carried out with remarkable success by the
Kuomintang Party.

2. The pacification of guerillas and bandits by peaceful measures
instead of using force to suppress them. (Ting avers that
after securing an effective control over the guerillas and
bandits it would be an easy matter to eliminate them should
the situation warrant such action.)

3. The organization of all the members into semi-military units,
to arm and imbue them with anti-Comintern and pro-peace
principles.

The above plan was approved and the organization was subject
to a drastic change in May 1939. A large number of persons of the
loafer class were recruited through Chu Zung Ling (朱顺林), conduc-
tor of the Li Wai Lo (利匯廬) Amusement Society, a gambling den
situated behind the Hollywood Garden, 1204 Yu Yuen Road, and the
most influential figure in the underworld fraternity in the outs
roads area in the Western District. Later through these member
the office succeeded in establishing contact with the leaders
pages.zh:
- 2 -

大福轮船公司的关闭，据报李成为了日本军方的秘密情报人员，并为便利其活动，他取得了汪精卫派系成员的合作。据说凭借其勤勉和良好服务，他赢得了当地日本当局的信任，因此被任命负责该组织。

1939年4月底，日本当局与汪精卫派系达成协议，根据该协议，丁默村（Ting Muh Tsung）被任命为该组织主任，取代李向群的职务。丁是汪精卫的坚定支持者，曾任国民政府军事委员会调查统计局局长。据说他是军人类型的人，并坚信“强权即公理”的信条。

他就任该组织主任后，立即制定了一项计划，内容如下：

1. 从黑社会团伙中招募人员作为成员，使其成为对抗共产主义的工具——这是国民党曾取得显著成效的一项措施。

2. 通过和平手段安抚游击队和土匪，而非使用武力镇压。（丁声称，在有效控制游击队和土匪后，如果局势需要，消灭他们将是一件容易的事。）

3. 将所有成员编组为半军事化单位，武装他们并向其灌输反共产国际和亲“和平”的原则。

上述计划获得批准，该组织在1939年5月经历了剧烈变动。大量无业游民通过朱顺林（Chu Zung Ling）被招募进来，朱是利匯廬（Li Wai Lo）游乐社的经理，该社是一家位于西区愚园路1204号好莱坞花园后面的赌场，也是西区越界筑路地区黑社会团伙中最具影响力的人物。后来，通过这些成员，办事处成功建立了与

pages.en:
- 3 -

the "Chinese Youths' Anti-Japanese and Traitors' Extermination
Iron and Blood Corps" (中國青年抗日鋤奸铁血軍) named Sung Feng Keng
(孙风岗) and Lee Yih Fei (李一飛), the latter being shot and
wounded by the Municipal Police when participating in an armed
robbery at No. 5 Fah wah Sing Tsung off Rockhill Avenue. After
protracted negotiations between Li Shih Chung (李自群) and the
two leaders of the Chinese Youths' Anti-Japanese and Traitors'
Extermination Iron and Blood Corps, all the members of the corps,
some 75 in number, agreed to work under Li Shih Chung at a pay of
$30.00 per mensem. These persons, it will be recalled, were res-
ponsible for numerous armed outrages in the outside roads area in
the Western District, including the murder of Keng Shou Pao (耿寿
宝) on Connaught Road on 2-2-39, and the firing on a Municipal
Police van on 22-2-39 on Jessfield Road which resulted in the death
of C.D.C. 165 Liu Zang Hung.

At the beginning of June 1939, the secret organization at
10/95 Edinburgh Road began to use the title "Tsing Ih Suh" ("All
of one colour") Defence Corps", but on June 9, 1939, it was renam-
ed "Headquarters of the Western District Self Defence Corps (沪西
自衛团). By this time the corps declared that it was formed to
protect residents in the outside roads area from being embarrassed
by guerillas but would collect from the business concerns, gambling
dens and opium hongs in the area subsidies for its maintenance.
It subsequently started independent negotiations with the various
gambling dens, "Hwo-wei" dens and opium hongs on the issue and the
majority of them are said to be willing to make the payment. These
establishments are cognizant of the fact that the corps is in
possession of a band of armed men consisting of the most unscru-
pulous elements and that it enjoys the support of the Japanese
Military. To reject any demand from the corps, therefore, would
most probably invite serious consequences.

At present it is reported that the corps has a total of some
150 members accommodated in House 6 and 10 Lane 95 Edinburgh Road.
The following is a list of the personnel of the organization:-
Ting Muh Tsung (丁默村), Director.
