- 3 -

“中国青年抗日锄奸铁血军”领导人孙风岗（Sung Feng Keng）和李一飛（Lee Yih Fei）的联系，后者在洛克赫路（Rockhill Avenue）附近的法华兴宗5号参与武装抢劫时被工部局警务处枪击受伤。经过李自群（Li Shih Chung）与“中国青年抗日锄奸铁血军”两位领导人的长期谈判，该团所有成员（约75人）同意以每月30美元的薪金在李自群手下工作。回想起来，这些人曾在西区越界筑路地区犯下多起武装暴行，包括1939年2月2日在康纳脱路谋杀耿寿宝（Keng Shou Pao），以及1939年2月22日在极司菲尔路向一辆工部局警务处面包车开枪，导致第165号中国籍巡捕刘藏洪（Liu Zang Hung）死亡。

1939年6月初，位于爱丁堡路95弄10号的秘密组织开始使用“清一色”防卫团（"Tsing Ih Suh" ("All of one colour") Defence Corps）的名称，但在1939年6月9日，更名为“沪西自卫团总部”。此时，该团宣称其成立目的是保护越界筑路地区的居民免受游击队的困扰，但会向该地区的商行、赌场和鸦片烟馆收取维持费作为补贴。随后，该团就此事开始与各赌场、“花会”赌档和鸦片烟馆进行独立谈判，据说大多数都愿意付款。这些场所深知该团拥有一支由最肆无忌惮分子组成的武装队伍，并享有日本军方的支持。因此，拒绝该团的任何要求很可能会招致严重后果。

据报，目前该团共有约150名成员，居住在爱丁堡路95弄6号和10号。以下是该组织的人员名单：
丁默村（Ting Muh Tsung），主任。

pages.en:
- 4 -

Li Shih Chung (李白群), Assistant Director.
Bang Tso Ming (彭祖明), Secretary.
Zee Wen Oen (許文安), Chief of Staff.
Sung Tsong Mei (宋忠美), Chief of the Personnel Affairs Dept.

It is reported that some 60 of the 150 members of the corps are at present armed with mauser and other pistols, the majority of which were, it is reported, supplied by the Japanese Military. Fifteen of the armed members are reported to be at present stationed in 76 Jessfield Road, C.O.L., to protect Ting Muh Tsung, Director of the Corps, who is said to be now residing in that house.

Meantime preparations are being made by the corps to establish branches at the following places:
1. In the vicinity of Brenan Piece.
2. In the vicinity of Jessfield Park.
3. In the vicinity of Kong Kya Jao, off Jessfield Road.

It is reported that on June 8 the office of the corps at 10/95 Edinburgh Road, was raided by a party of Japanese Military Police and as a result six of the inmates were arrested and four Mauser pistols seized. However, through representations made by Li Shih Chung, the Japanese Military Police released all those arrested and returned their pistols, intimating that the raid has been carried out as a result of their having received some misleading information.

On the morning of June 22, 1939 a detective of the Shanghai Municipal Police while attempting to verify an address outside Lane 1423 Yu Yuen Road, was arrested by some twenty members of the corps who were armed with pistols, and was marched away to a Chinese style house in the Zau Ka Yi Village situated between Edinburgh Road and Great Western Road. He, however, was released the same day after a visit to 10/95 Edinburgh Road by police officers attached to Bubbling Well Station. Except that he was scared and accused of being a traitor, the detective was not injured in anyway. The police officers who visited the office of the corps, were received by the following:-
pages.zh:
- 4 -

李白群（Li Shih Chung），副主任。
彭祖明（Bang Tso Ming），秘书。
許文安（Zee Wen Oen），参谋长。
宋忠美（Sung Tsong Mei），人事处处长。

据报，该团150名成员中约有60人目前配备毛瑟枪及其他手枪，其中大多数据报由日本军方提供。据报，15名武装成员目前驻扎在极司菲尔路76号，C.O.L.，以保护据称现居住在该处的该团主任丁默村。

与此同时，该团正计划在以下地点设立分部：
1. 布伦南片（Brenan Piece）附近。
2. 极司菲尔公园附近。
3. 极司菲尔路附近的孔家角（Kong Kya Jao）。

据报，6月8日，日本宪兵队突袭了位于爱丁堡路95弄10号的该团办事处，结果逮捕了六名在场人员，并缴获四支毛瑟手枪。然而，经李向群交涉，日本宪兵队释放了所有被捕人员并归还了他们的手枪，暗示此次突袭是由于收到了某些误导性信息所致。

1939年6月22日上午，一名上海工部局警务处侦探在试图核实愚园路1423弄外的一处地址时，被该团约二十名持手枪的成员逮捕，并被押送至位于爱丁堡路和大西路之间的赵家义村（Zau Ka Yi Village）的一所中式房屋内。然而，在同一天静安寺分局的警官访问爱丁堡路95弄10号后，该侦探获释。除受到惊吓并被指控为汉奸外，该侦探未受任何伤害。访问该团办事处的警官受到了以下人员的接待：

pages.en:

1. Li Shih Chung (李自群), Assistant Director of the Corps.
2. Tung Tsoong Mei (孙忠美), Chief of the Personnel Affairs Dept.
3. Tee En Oen (徐文安), Chief of Staff.
4. Lee Yih Fei (李一飛), an ex-leader of the "Chinese Youths' Anti-Japanese and Traitors Extermination Iron and Blood Corps", who was shot and wounded by the Municipal Police when participating in an armed robbery in Pah Lah Sing Tsung off Rockhill Avenue, and later removed to Lane 95 House 10 Edinburgh Road in Li Shih Chung's motorcar.

Latest information to hand shows that on June 23, 1939 the organization changed its title again from that of "Headquarters of the Eastern District Self Defence Corps" to "Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army" (中國國民黨共救國軍特務隊) and that between 2 p.m. and 3p.m. daily lectures on anti-Comintern and anti-British subjects were given the members in the office of the corps at 10/96 Edinburgh Road.

 Dah Foh Steamboat Company, Li, it is reported, became a secret
 intelligence agent of the Japanese Military and, to facilitate
 his activities, he secured the cooperation of members of Wang
 Ching Wei's clique. By his diligence and good service he is said
 to have gained the confidence of the local Japanese authorities,
 hence his appointment in charge of the organization.

 Towards the end of April 1939, the Japanese authorities and
 the Wang Ching Wei clique reached an agreement according to which
 Ting Muh Tsung (丁默邨), was appointed director of the organization
 superseding Li Shih Chung in the office. Ting is a staunch sup-
 porter of Wang Ching Wei and was formerly chief of the Investiga-
 tion Section of the Military Affairs Commission of the National
 Government. He is stated to be a man of the military type and
 entertains a strong belief in the motto that "might is right".

 Immediately after he became director of the organization, he
 drew up a plan which provides for the following:-

 1. The recruiting of men from the underworld fraternity as members
 who are to be made instruments in combating communism - a
 measure which was carried out with remarkable success by the
 Kuomintang Party.

 2. The pacification of guerillas and bandits by peaceful measures
 instead of using force to suppress them. (Ting avers that
 after securing an effective control over the guerillas and
 bandits it would be an easy matter to eliminate them should
 the situation warrant such action.)

 3. The organization of all the members into semi-military units,
 to arm and imbue them with anti-Comintern and pro-peace
 principles.

 The above plan was approved and the organization was subject
 to a drastic change in May 1939. A large number of persons of the
 loafer class were recruited through Chu Zung Ling (朱顺林), conduc-
 tor of the Li Wai Lo (利匯廬) Amusement Society, a gambling den
 situated behind the Hollywood Garden, 1204 Yu Yuen Road, and the
 most influential figure in the underworld fraternity in the outside
 roads area in the Western District. Later through these members,
 the office succeeded in establishing contact with the leaders of

据报，大福轮船公司（Dah Foh Steamboat Company）的李氏成为日本军方的秘密情报人员，为便利其活动，他取得了汪精卫派系成员的合作。据说因其勤勉和良好服务，他赢得了当地日本当局的信任，因此被任命负责该组织。

1939年4月底，日本当局与汪精卫派系达成协议，根据该协议，丁默邨（Ting Muh Tsung）被任命为该组织主任，接替李士群（Li Shih Chung）的职务。丁是汪精卫的坚定支持者，曾任国民政府军事委员会调查统计局局长。据说他是军人类型的人，并坚信“强权即公理”的信条。

他就任该组织主任后，立即制定了一项计划，规定如下：

1. 从黑社会团伙中招募人员作为成员，使其成为反共的工具——这是国民党曾以显著成效实施的一项措施。

2. 通过和平手段安抚游击队和匪徒，而不是使用武力镇压他们。（丁声称，在有效控制游击队和匪徒后，如果局势需要，消灭他们将是一件容易的事。）

3. 将所有成员编组为准军事单位，武装他们并向其灌输反共产国际和拥护和平的原则。

上述计划获得批准，该组织于1939年5月经历了剧烈变动。通过朱顺林（Chu Zung Ling）招募了大量游手好闲之徒，朱是利汇庐（Li Wai Lo）娱乐社的经理，该社是一家位于愚园路1204号好莱坞花园后面的赌场，朱也是西区越界筑路地区黑社会团伙中最具影响力的人物。后来，通过这些成员，该办事处成功建立了与以下人员的联系：

the "Chinese Youths' Anti-Japanese and Traitors' Extermination
Iron and Blood Corps" (中國青年抗日鋤奸铁血軍) named Sung Feng Kong
(孙凤岗) and Lee Yih Pei (李一飞), the latter being shot and
wounded by the Municipal Police when participating in an armed
robbery at No. 5 Fah Wah Sing Tsang off Rockhill Avenue. After
protracted negotiations between Li Chih Chung (李志忠) and the
two leaders of the Chinese Youths' Anti-Japanese and Traitors'
Extermination Iron and Blood Corps, all the members of the corps,
some 75 in number, agreed to work under Li Chih Chung at a pay of
$30.00 per mensem. These persons, it will be recalled, were res-
ponsible for numerous armed outrages in the outside roads area in
the Western District, including the murder of Heng Chou Pao (耿寿
宝) on Connaught Road on 2-2-39, and the firing on a Municipal
Police van on 22-2-39 on Jessfield Road which resulted in the death
of S.M.C. 155 Liu Tang Hung.

At the beginning of June 1939, the secret organization at
10/95 Edinburgh Road began to use the title "Tsing Ih Suh" ("All
of one colour") Defence Corps", but on June 9, 1939, it was renam-
ed "Headquarters of the Western District Self Defence Corps (沪西
自衛團). By this time the corps declared that it was formed to
protect residents in the outside roads area from being embarrassed
by guerillas but would collect from the business concerns, gambling
dens and opium hongs in the area subsidies for its maintenance.
It subsequently started independent negotiations with the various
gambling dens, "Two-wei" dens and opium hongs on the issue and the
majority of them are said to be willing to make the payment. These
establishments are cognizant of the fact that the corps is in
possession of a band of armed men consisting of the most unscru-
pulous elements and that it enjoys the support of the Japanese
Military. To reject any demand from the corps, therefore, would
most probably invite serious consequences.

At present it is reported that the corps has a total of some
150 members accommodated in House 6 and 10 Lane 95 Edinburgh Road.
The following is a list of the personnel of the organization:-
Ting Muh Tsung (丁穆松), Director.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Logan

The secret pro-Japanese organization which has
an office at House 10, Lane 95, Edinburgh Road, first
came to the notice of the Municipal Police on April
11, 1939, when a follower of Li Shih Chung (李自群),
Chief of the office, was taken into custody by the
Municipal Police together with a pedestrian on
Edinburgh Road near Great Western Road while he was
making an illegal attempt to effect the arrest of the
pedestrian whom he suspected of spying.

Subsequent enquiries revealed that the
organization came into existence about the beginning
of March, 1939, at 67 Great Western Road, the home of
Li Shih Chung with the sole object of promoting an
anti-Comintern and pro-peace movement, under the
auspices of the Japanese Military Authorities. It removed
to its present address, 10/95 Edinburgh Road, on
March 27, 1939. When the organization was first
formed, Li engaged himself in the recruiting of members
and announced that he would direct them in an extensive
anti-Comintern, Pro-Peace and National Salvation
Movement.

Li Shih Chung, chief of the organization, was
prior to the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities
in August, 1937, an employee of the Bureau of Social
Affairs of the Shanghai City Government and
concurrently was assigned by the Central Kuomintang
to assist the Public Safety Bureau in the suppression
of communist activities in Shanghai. Some time

位于爱丁堡路95弄10号设有办事处的秘密亲日组织，首次引起工部局警务处注意是在1939年4月11日，当时该办事处主任李自群（Li Shih Chung）的一名追随者在大西路附近的愛丁堡路上试图非法逮捕一名他怀疑是间谍的行人时，与该行人一起被工部局警务处拘留。

后续调查显示，该组织于1939年3月初在李自群的住所大西路67号成立，唯一目的是在日本军政当局的支持下推动反共产国际和拥护和平运动。该组织于1939年3月27日迁至现址爱丁堡路95弄10号。组织成立之初，李致力于招募成员，并宣布他将指导他们开展广泛的反共产国际、拥护和平及救国运动。

该组织主任李士群在1937年8月中日敌对行动爆发前，曾是上海市政府社会局雇员，同时受国民党中央委派，协助公安局镇压上海的共产党活动。某段时间

should the situation warrant such action.)
3. The organization of all the members into semi-
military units, to arm and imbue them with anti-

2. 通过和平手段安抚游击队和匪徒，而不是使用武力镇压他们。（丁声称，在对游击队和匪徒实现有效控制后，如果局势需要，消灭他们将是一件容易的事。）
3. 将所有成员编组为半军事化单位，武装他们并向其灌输反共产国际和主张和平的原则。
上述计划获得批准，该组织于1939年5月进行了剧烈改组。大量无业游民类人员

Defence Corps", but on June 9, 1939, it was renamed
"Headquarters of the Western District Self Defence
Corps(沪西自卫团). By this time the corps
declared that it was formed to protect residents
in the outside roads area from being embarrassed by
guerillas but would collect from the business concerns,
gambling dens and opium hongs in the area subsidies
for its maintenance. It subsequently started
independent negotiations with the various gambling
dens, "Hwo-wei" dens and opium hongs on the issue
and the majority of them are said to be willing to
make the payment. These establishments are cognizant
of the fact that the corps is in possession of a band
of armed men consisting of the most unscrupulous
elements and that it enjoys the support of the
Japanese Military. To reject any demand from the
corps, therefore, would most probably invite
serious consequences.

At present it is reported that the corps has a
total of some 150 members accommodated in House 6
and 10, Lane 95, Edinburgh Road. The following is
a list of the personnel of the organization:-
Ting Muh Tsung (丁默村), Director.

Bang Tso Ming (彭祖明), Secretary.

“情一色”（Tsing Ih Suh）防卫团的名义，但在1939年6月9日，它更名为“沪西自卫团”。此时，该团宣称其成立目的是保护越界筑路地区的居民免受游击队的骚扰，但会向该地区的商行、赌博窝点和鸦片烟馆收取维持费作为补贴。随后，它就此事与各赌博窝点、“花会”窝点和鸦片烟馆开始了独立谈判，据说大多数都愿意付款。这些场所深知，该团拥有一支由最肆无忌惮分子组成的武装队伍，并享有日本军方的支持。因此，拒绝该团的任何要求很可能会招致严重后果。

据报，目前该团共有约150名成员，居住在爱丁堡路95弄6号和10号。以下是该组织的人员名单：-
丁默邨（Ting Muh Tsung），主任。

It is reported that some 60 of the 150 members
of the corps are at present armed with Mauser
and other pistols, the majority of which were, it is
reported, supplied by the Japanese Military. Fifteen
of the armed members are reported to be at present
stationed in 76 Jessfield Road, O.O.L., to protect
Ting Muh Tsung, Director of the Corps, who is said
to be now residing in that house.
Meantime preparations are being made by the
corps to establish branches at the following places:
1. In the vicinity of Brenan Piece.
2. In the vicinity of Jessfield Park.
3. In the vicinity of Kong Kya Jao, off Jessfield Rd.
It is reported that on June 8 the office of
the corps at 10/95 Edinburgh Road, was raided by a
party of Japanese Military Police and as a result six
of the inmates were arrested and four Mauser pistols
seized. However, through representations made by
Li Shih Chung, the Japanese Military Police released
all those arrested and returned their pistols,
intimating that the raid had been carried out as a
result of their having received some misleading
information.
On the morning of June 22, 1939, a detective
of the Shanghai Municipal Police while attempting

was arrested by some twenty members of the corps who

Subject "Tsing Ih Zuh" (All of One Colour) Defence Corps - renamed
Headquarters of the Western District Self-Defence Corps.
Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

A meeting of the members of the "Tsing Ih Zuh"
(All of One Colour) Defence corps of Lane 95, 10
Edinburgh Road, O.C.L., was held in the office on
the afternoon of June 9, 1939 and was presided over
by Li Shih Chung (李士群), Chief of the Corps. A
discussion took place and it was decided that the
corps be renamed the Headquarters of the Western
District Self-Defence corps (滬西自衛團),
their duties to comprise the protection of the sales
agents of Hwo Wei Lottery numbering about 170, the
various gambling dens, opium hongs and business
concerns generally. The headquarters are reported
to have removed to House 6, Lane 95, Edinburgh Road,
where the bodyguards of Li Shih Chung are quartered.
The Western District Self-Defence Corps has
at present a total of 90 members with one Sung Tsoong
Mei (沈忠美) in charge and one Pang Tso-ming (彭祖明)
as Secretary. The Chief-of-Staff of the Corps
is one Zee Wen Oen (徐文安), a follower of Chu
Zung Ling (朱順林), Chief of the now defunct
detective squad of the Opium Hong Guild and he is
actually responsible for the affairs of the corps.
The Headquarters of the Western District Self-
Defence Corps are making preparations for the
establishment of three branch corps at the following
places in the near future :-
(1) In the vicinity of Ng Kia Zang, Zau Ka Doo Area;
(2) In the vicinity of Jessfield Park;

Date June 8, 19 39.
Subject "Tsing Ih Suh" (All of One Colour) Defence Corps - office
raided by Japanese Military Police.
Made by                     Forwarded by

It is reported that at about 7 a.m. June 8,
1939, the office of the "Tsing Ih Suh" (All of One
Colour) Defence Corps, 10/95 Edinburgh Road, O.C.L.,
was raided by a party of Japanese Military Police.
Four Mauser pistols were seized and six of the inmates
taken into custody.
Li Shih Chung (李士群), Chief of the Corps,
who was absent from the office during the raid, later
made representations to the Western District Section
of the Japanese Military Police, 94 Jessfield Road,
C.O.L. and as a result, the arrested persons were
released and the pistols returned to them. It is
said that the Japanese Military Police had carried out
the raid as a result of having received misleading
information.
It will be recalled that the "Tsing Ih Suh"
Defence Corps was recently organized by Li Shih Chung,
residing at 67 Great Western Road, O.O.L. for the
purpose of affording protection to gambling dens and
opium hongs in the outside roads area in the Western
District.

M. C. Randley

该团团长李士群（Li Shih Chung），在搜查期间不在办事处，随后向位于越界筑路区极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）94号的日本宪兵西区分队提出交涉，结果被捕人员获释，手枪也被归还。据说日本宪兵是因收到误导性情报而进行此次搜查的。

The "Tsing Ih Suh (清一色)" or
"All of One Colour" Defence Corps, 10, Lane 95,
Edinburgh Road, O.O.L., which has not been formally
inaugurated, was recently organized by one Li Shih
Chung (李士羣), living at 67 Great Western
Road, O.O.L., for the purpose of affording protection
to gambling dens and opium hongs, etc. in the
Western District, O.O.L. The corps will live on
the subsidies paid by the gambling dens and opium
hongs, etc. and also on contributions collected from
shops in the Fah Hwa Village on the pretext that
the corps will prevent Chinese guerillas from
embarrassing them. Nothing definite can be learned
at present of the amount to be derived from these
subsidies from the gambling dens, but it is known
that the gambling dens are willing to make payment.
At present the corps has some thirty to
forty members and intends enlisting further members
from amongst the loafer fraternity through the
efforts of two loafers named Zee Wen Oen (徐文安)
and Sung Tscong Mei (沈忠美) who state that
those joining will receive pay in a sum from $30 to
$40 per month. In this connection, Chu Sung Ling
(朱顺林), Chief of the now defunct detective
squad of the Opium Hong Guild, is rendering
assistance to the Corps by introducing ex-guerilla
members. He is also working for one Li Tsien Yah
(李秋野), one of the principal assistants of

Subject Arrests by Bubbling Well Station of alleged followers of
Wang Ching-wei ( 汪精衛 ).

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

At 6.45p.m. on the 29th May, 1939 D.I.
Tabrum senior detective of Bubbling Well Station
telephoned the undersigned with the information
that they had taken into custody a gang of male
Chinese suspected of armed robbery and that
he had every reason to believe that some of them
were connected with the Wang Ching-wei clique.
He requested assistance in questioning them
on this point and arrangements were made for
the necessary assistance, the prisoner claiming
to be an executive being brought to Special
Branch at 7 p.m., May 29th, where a statement
was taken from him by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa. The
statement which is attached would tend to show
that the prisoner has been used to further the
ends of the gang who had other motives under
the pretence of belonging to the Wang Ching-wei
clique.

C. Crawford
D. I.

My name is Tsih Tseng Kwei alias Tsih Siao Er Tsz,
age 27, native of Funing, Kompo, married, and am residing
in an upstairs back room 265 Rue Ratard, French Concession.
I am uneducated and was a peasant in my native home
in Kompo until about Autumn of the 25th year of the Chinese
Republic (1936) when I came to Shanghai in company with my
brother-in-law Lee Tuh Shing (李德興) with a view to
obtaining employment. We resided at No. 97 Tang Ka Wan
(唐家灣), West Gate, Nantao, and, as we were unable to
secure any regular employment, we commenced earning our
livelihood by hawking salted eggs.
Following the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in 1937, we removed to an unnumbered hut in
Rue Amiral Bayle and continued hawking eggs in the Rue
Ratard Market.
In the 12th moon last year (January 1939) I went to
live at Su Ka Zeh (侯家宅) in Fah Hwa Village, Western
District. O.C.L. with a sweetheart named Tang Siao Mei
(唐小妹), occupying an upstairs room of the Kwang Loh
Koong (廣樂宮) Barber Shop. I had by that time ceased
hawking eggs owing to lack of business but my brother-in-law
continued to live in Rue Amiral Bayle.
While I was residing in Fah Hwa Village, an
acquaintance of mine named Tsang Sai Zah Ts (張三石子)
(who was concerned with Lee Ih Fai (李一飛) in a number
of armed robbery cases and was arrested by the S.M.P. on
the night of 18/4/39 in Fah Hwa Village and handed over to

以下为戚正貴（Tsih Tseng Kwei），别名戚小二子（Tsih Siao Er Tsz）的供词。戚系江苏高邮阜寧人，由我，警探 D. S. Pitts，于1939年5月29日在警察总局讯问，并由警探 Kuh Pao Hwa 担任翻译。

我叫戚正貴，别名戚小二子，现年27岁，江苏高邮阜寧人，已婚，现居住于法租界辣斐德路（Rue Ratard）265号楼上后间。我未受过教育，在民国二十五年（1936年）秋之前，我一直在高邮老家务农。那时我与姐夫李德興（Lee Tuh Shing）一同来到上海谋职。我们居住在南市西门唐家灣97号，由于找不到固定工作，便开始靠叫卖咸蛋为生。
1937年中日战事爆发后，我们搬至贝勒路（Rue Amiral Bayle）一处无门牌号的棚屋，并继续在辣斐德路市场叫卖鸡蛋。
去年农历十二月（1939年1月），我搬到西区法华村侯家宅（Su Ka Zeh），与一名叫唐小妹（Tang Siao Mei）的情妇同居，占据广乐宫（Kwang Loh Koong）理发店的楼上房间。当时因生意清淡，我已停止叫卖鸡蛋，但我姐夫仍住在贝勒路。
当我住在法华村时，我的一个熟人张三石子（Tsang Sai Zah Ts）（此人曾与李一飛（Lee Ih Fai）共同涉及多起武装抢劫案，并于1939年4月18日晚在法华村被上海公共租界警务处逮捕，随后于4月20日移交给

June 27, 1941

Dissolution of Labour Unions in Nantao

In compliance with an order issued on June 20,
1941, by the Social Affairs Bureau of the Shanghai Special
Municipal Government, all the labour unions, numbering more
than twenty, located at No. 85 Soong Sih Ka (松雪街),
Nantao, have now dissolved. Among the labour unions
dissolved, were the Shanghai Bath House Employees' Union,
the Shanghai Municipality Tailors Union, the Shanghai
Municipality Handcart Pullers Union, the Shanghai
Municipality Steamship Passengers' Baggage Transportation
Workers' Union, the Barbers' Union, the Shanghai District
Foundry Workers' Union and the Shanghai Ordure Coolies
Union.

It will be recalled that the Social Movement
Direction Committee of the Nanking Government formed the
"Shanghai Municipality Labour Unions Readjustment Committee",
Lane 247/5 Chung Hwa Road, Nantao, in February this year
in order to register and readjust the labour unions in
Shanghai. However, the labour unions at 85 Soong Sih Ka,
Nantao, failed to effect registration with the Committee
and their dissolution was therefore ordered.

Prior to the formation of the Labour Union
Readjustment Committee, the labour unions in Shanghai were
under the supervision of two different organs, namely, the
General Labour Union in Nantao and the General Labour Union
in the Western District, the former being patronized by
the Japanese Special Service in Shanghai and the latter
under the auspices of the Shanghai Branch, Social Movement
Direction Committee. All the labour unions at No. 85
Soong Sih Ka were under the General Labour Union in Nantao.
Being aware of the fact that it was improper to have two

南市工会解散

遵照上海特别市政府社会事务局于1941年6月20日发布的命令，位于南市松雪街85号的二十多个工会现已全部解散。在被解散的工会中，包括上海浴室职工工会、上海市裁缝工会、上海市人力车夫工会、上海市轮船乘客行李搬运工工会、理发师工会、上海地区翻砂工人工会和上海粪夫工会。

回顾今年二月，南京政府的社会运动指导委员会成立了“上海市工会整理委员会”，地址为南市中华路247弄5号，旨在对上海的工会进行登记和整理。然而，南市松雪街85号的工会未能向该委员会办理登记，因此被下令解散。

在工会整理委员会成立之前，上海的工会受两个不同机构的监管，即南市总工会和西区总工会，前者由上海日本特务机关支持，后者在上海社会运动指导委员会分会的主持下运作。松雪街85号的所有工会均隶属于南市总工会。鉴于在上海存在两个

The attached despatch bearing characters,
"Tseng Yen" ( 整函 ), No. 10, dated February
19, 1941, was received at Police Headquarters,
Foochow Road, on February 21, 1941. The despatch
bears the chop of the five Standing Committee
members of the Shanghai Municipality Labour Unions
Readjustment Committee at Lane 247/5 Chung Hwa
Road, Nantao. The names of these committee
members are given as :
1) Kun Yuen Ding ( 丁雲根 )
2) Woo Zao Ling ( 胡兆麟 )
3) Yuan Sz Shing ( 袁士星 )
4) Zah Chong Hsueh ( 查崇學 )
5) Tsu Zung Tung ( 諸永棟 )

The despatch reads that, acting on the
instructions of Mr. Ting Mun Tsung ( 丁默村 ),
Minister of Social Affairs of the Nanking Government,
the Readjustment Committee officially commenced
functioning on February 1, 1941, with offices at
the above-mentioned address. It requests S.M. Police
to render assistance to the committee from time
to time.

Information regarding this Readjustment
Committee are contained in Special Branch Reports
dated 13.2.41 and 18.2.41.

The Shanghai Municipality Labour Unions Readjustment
Committee has been re-organized temporarily for the sole
purpose of inducing the various local labour unions,
which have hitherto been independent or connected with
some other labour controlling organization, other than
the General Labour Union at Lane 95/10 Edinburgh Road,
C.O.L. which is sponsored by the Wang Ching Wei Government,
to register with the Shanghai Municipality Labour Unions
Readjustment Committee so that the committee can directly
exercise its control and supervision over them. It is
expected that the registration of the various labour unions
with the "committee" will be completed within three months
when the proposed "General Labour Union" will replace
the present Shanghai Municipality Labour Unions Readjustment
Committee.

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper) :-
SHANGHAI MUNICIPALITY LABOUR UNION TO BE ORGANIZED SOON

Following the dissolution of the Shanghai
Municipality General Labour Union and the Shanghai Special
District General Labour Union, the China Workers' Welfare
Association and other small labour organizations have ceased
functioning, and will be formed into a Shanghai Municipality
Labour Union.
It is learned that this union will be the
proper labour organ under the direction of the Labour
Movement Direction Committee of the Ministry of the Social
Affairs. The Labour Unions Readjustment Committee has summoned
the representatives of various labour organizations to attend
meetings which are being held twice a week and to discuss
the organization of the union which is expected to take two
to three months.

D. I. Pau pa-
Heng/2

102 1941年2月14日下午

《新顺报》（日资中文报纸）：-
上海市总工会即将组建

继上海市总工会和上海特别区总工会解散后，中国工人福利协会及其他小型劳工组织已停止运作，并将合并组建为上海市总工会。
据悉，该工会将成为在社会部劳工运动指导委员会指导下的正式劳工机构。工会整理委员会已召集各劳工组织代表参加每周举行两次的会议，讨论工会的组织事宜，预计耗时两至三个月。

D. I. Pau pa-
Heng/2

February 13, 1941. D. M

TAIRIKU SHIMPO :-

SHANGHAI LABOUR UNION ORGANIZED BY NANKING GOVERNMENT

The Nanking Government has decided
to organize a Shanghai Municipality Labour Union in
accordance with its new regulations. This Labour Union
will be formed by reorganizing and unifying the former
Shanghai Municipality General Labour Union, the Shanghai
Special Municipality General Labour Union, the Chinese
Welfare Association in Central China and various other
small organizations.
Meetings of the readjustment committee
for organizing the new Labour Union are being held twice a
week, at which representatives of various organizations
discuss concrete measures to be taken for the formation
of the new organ. The Labour Movement Committee has
its plan drawn up for it. It is expected that the formal
inauguration of the new Labour Union will be held after
two or three months.

D. I. Law L. P. Pan
Perry/2

1941年2月13日。 D. M

《大陆新报》：-

南京政府组建上海工会

南京政府决定根据其新法规组建上海市总工会。该总工会将由原上海市总工会、上海特别市总工会、华中中国福利协会及其他各种小型组织重组统一而成。
为新工会组建而设立的整理委员会会议每周举行两次，各组织代表在会上讨论组建新机构的具体措施。劳工运动委员会已为其制定计划。预计新工会的正式成立典礼将在两三个月后举行。

D. I. Law L. P. Pan

forthwith and to incorporate the two bodies in question
into one organization to be known as the "Shanghai

the incorporation could not be carried out until recently

established before the union in the Western District:

Municipality Labour Unions Readjustment Committee -

removed from 527 Range Rd. to Land 247/5 Chung Hwa Rd.,
Nantao.

Central China Daily News (4/2) :-

SHANGHAI MUNICIPALITY LABOUR UNIONS READJUSTMENT COMMITTEE
FORMED

With a view to unifying the labour movement
organizations and to improving the welfare of the labourers,
the Shanghai Branch of the Social Movement Direction Committee
last winter ordered the Shanghai Municipality Labour Union and
the Shanghai Special District Labour Union to cease functioning
after December 12. The Shanghai Municipality Labour Unions
Readjustment Committee was then formed and Yuan Shih-shing
(袁士興) and ten others were appointed as Committeemen to place
the local labour movement organizations into proper order.
At 10 a.m. yesterday an inaugurating meeting was held
by the Committeemen at the office of the Shanghai Branch of the
Social Movement Direction Committee. About 500 representatives
of local labour circles were present.
Chang (張), a representative of the Shanghai Branch of
the Social Movement Direction Committee, delivered an address, the
four main points of which were as follows :-
1) After the formation of the Labour Unions
Readjustment Committee, the Committee should assist labour unions
in completing their unfinished work.
2) At the present time, the Social Movement Direction
Committee is directing the public bodies. The work of organizing,
training, directing and supervising public bodies is being
undertaken by this Committee, on a system that is slightly
different from the pre-war system. The Committee must,
according to the revised Labour Unions Law, ascertain whether
the structure of the various labour unions is uniform and it
must readjust those that are not.
3) The labour unions in this city will assist the
Labour Unions Readjustment Committee in its mission.
4) During the period of readjustment, the labour unions
in this city should endeavour to organize a Shanghai Municipal
Labour Union.

《华中日报》（2月4日）：-

上海市工会整理委员会成立

为统一劳工运动组织并改善劳工福利，社会运动指导委员会上海分会于去年冬季下令，上海市工会和上海特别区工会于12月12日后停止运作。随后成立了上海市工会整理委员会，任命袁士興等十一人为委员，以整顿本地劳工运动组织。昨日上午10时，委员们在社会运动指导委员会上海分会办公室举行了成立大会。约500名本地劳工界代表出席。

社会运动指导委员会上海分会代表张氏发表讲话，其主要内容如下四点：-
1) 工会整理委员会成立后，应协助各工会完成其未竟之工作。
2) 目前，社会运动指导委员会正在指导公共团体。该委员会正按照与战前体制略有不同的制度，承担公共团体的组织、训练、指导和监督工作。委员会必须根据修订后的《工会法》，查明各工会的结构是否统一，并对不统一的工会进行整理。
3) 本市各工会将协助工会整理委员会履行其使命。
4) 在整理期间，本市各工会应努力组建上海市总工会。

General Labour Union and barbers' strike

（批：Commissioner of Police.
Sir:
Information 15/1.
[签名]
A. C. (SM Pol)）

At 4 p.m. January 14, Fang Siu Ngae (方秀岩),
Conductor of the Shanghai Tramways, who has been
a professional labour agitator, now working in the
General Labour Union, Lane 95, 10 Edinburgh Road, C.O.L.
telephoned D.I. Kao Yen Ken at Police Headquarters. He
stated that a number of barbers had been arrested in
front of the Sun Sun Barber Shop, Kweichow Road, and
detained in Louza Station and that delegates of the
employers were also in Louza Station and there was a
possibility that the employers would compel those
arrested to sign an agreement. He further mentioned
that the strikers were concentrating at the General
Labour Union Headquarters, Edinburgh Road where they
were some 1,000 barbers. They, intended, he went on to
say, to proceed to Louza Station and demand the release
of their colleagues and were prepared for trouble.
He was very abrupt and stated that D.I. Kao should have
the authority to release those arrested and suggested
that D. I. Kao will be held responsible for the release
of the two parties for negotiations to proceed outside.
At first he suggested that the Municipal Police should
carry out mediation, but retracted and stated that a
mediation meeting had already been arranged at the
Shanghai Branch, Social Movement Direction Committee,
527 Range Road, for January 14.

December 21, 1940.
Amalgamation of the General Labour Union, Nantao,
and the Chinese Labourers' Welfare Association with
the General Labour Union in the Western District.
Upon instructions from the Ministry of
Social Affairs of the Nanking Government, on 15th
December, 1940, the General Labour Union, No. 5, Lane
247, Chung Hwa Road, Nantao suspended operations.
It will now amalgamate with the Chinese Labourers'
Welfare Association and the Western District General
Labour Union and will be reorganized and this organ
will be known now as The Shanghai Municipality Labour
Movement Adjustment Committee which will be inaugurated
in the near future.
It is learned that this committee is directly
under the control of the Shanghai Office of the Social
Movement Direction Committee of the Ministry of Social
Affair of the Nanking Government which is situated at
527 Range Road. It will supervise all Labour Movement
in Shanghai and the whole area of Shanghai will be
divided into Southern, Northern, Western, Eastern and
Central districts (The French Concession and the Settle-
ment being the central district) and 15 committee
members will be appointed.
The Great Peoples' Society and the Chinese
Labourers' Welfare Association were organized by the
Asia Development Board and the Shanghai Japanese Special
Service Organ. During the period the Reformed Government
was functioning, branches of the Great Peoples' Society
were established in various shiens and municipalities
in Kiangsu, Chekiang, and Anhwei. On the inauguration
of the Nanking Government in March, this year, the
Ministry of Social Affairs was established, and Wang
Ching Wei strongly objected to the existence of these

December 22, 1940.
Morning Translation

Kuo Min Daily News, Bing Pao, Central China Daily News,
New China Daily News:

SOCIAL MOVEMENT DIRECTING COMMITTEE AND LABOUR
DISPUTES

With a view to centralizing the control of
affairs, the Shanghai branch of the Social Movement
Directing Committee yesterday gave instructions to its
subordinates to the effect that mediations of labour
disputes through private channels be strictly prohibited
and that any trouble among labourers in whatever trade be
reported to the branch to be dealt with, thereby putting
a stop to malpractices and avoiding misunderstandings.

December 19, 1940.
Morning Translation

Kuo Min Daily News, Central China Daily News, New China Daily
News, Bing Pao and Sin Shun Pao (Japanese-owned Chinese
language newspaper) :-

EFFECTIVE MEASURES ADOPTED BY THE AUTHORITIES TO
PREVENT SPREAD OF LABOUR DISPUTES

Of late, numerous disputes between Labour
and Capital have occurred, but in most of the cases the
workers have not asked official organs to mediate nor have
they dared to go on strike or to suspend work.
It is learned that the Shanghai Branch
of the Social Movement Direction Committee, the City
Government and the Bureau of Social Affairs will issue a
joint proclamation prohibiting such activities for they are
liable to obstruct the peace movement and affect peace and
order. The hope has been expressed that whenever a labour
dispute arises it will be referred to the authorities for
examination. During the period of mediation, no strike or
suspension of work should be allowed.

当局采取有效措施防止劳资纠纷蔓延

December 6, 1940.
Shanghai General Labour Unions - amalgamation proposed.

On November 22, 1940, the following advertisement was published in the Central China Daily News, by Messrs Sung Ming Chi (孫鳴岐) and Chang Kuh Chong (張克昌), Chief and Deputy Chief respectively of the Shanghai Branch of the Social Movement Direction Committee, of the Ministry of Police of the Wang Ching Wei Government, 75 Jessfield Road, O.O.L.:-

"This committee undertakes such duties as direction, supervision, organization and training in connection with social movements, and with this end in view, notice is hereby given that all public bodies are required to register with this committee before the end of this month, failing which they are to be disbanded and deprived of their legal status".

This action on the part of the Committee threatens the existence of the Shanghai General Labour Union, Lane 247/5 Chung Hwa Road, Nantao which is supported by the Japanese Special Service Department and which the Shanghai General Labour Union at Lane 95/10 Edinburgh Road, Western District, O.O.L. (sponsored by Wang Ching Wei) is endeavouring to incorporate.

1940年12月6日。
上海各总工会 - 拟议合并。

1940年11月22日，汪精卫政府警政部社会运动指导委员会上海分会主任孙鸣岐（Sung Ming Chi）和副主任张克昌（Chang Kuh Chong）在极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）75号于《华中日报》刊登了以下广告：-

“本委员会承担与社会运动有关的指导、监督、组织和培训等职责，为此目的，特此通知所有公共团体必须在本月底前向本委员会注册，否则将被解散并剥夺其合法地位”。

委员会的这一行动威胁到了位于南市中华路247弄5号、由日本特务部门支持的上海总工会的生存，而位于西区爱多亚路10号95弄、由汪精卫赞助的上海总工会正试图将其并入。

最近，西区总工会已派遣代理人，指示收买主要

pages.en:
- 2 -

figures of the various labour unions at present
connected with the General Labour Union in Nantao.
It is said, that any agent who succeeds in
effecting the buying over of any such person will
be given a reward of $100.00 while the latter will
be paid an allowance of $200.00, without obligation
but he is required to interview a responsible person
of the General Labour Union in the Western District and
openly express his loyalty to that union when called
upon to do so.

Apart from this new attempt, members of
the General Labour Union in the Western District
approached responsible persons of the General Labour
Union in Nantao, a short time ago with a request
for amalgamation of the two unions. The General
Labour Union in Nantao accordingly applied for
instructions from the Japanese Special Service
Department and the following points were decided
upon, which it is reported, have been passed to
and are under consideration by the General Labour
Union in the Western District:-

1. That this union (Nantao union) agrees to the
amalgamation proposed.

2. That the proposed amalgamated union be given
the title of "Shanghai Municipality Labour
Unions Reorganizing Committee"
( 上海市工会整理委员会 ).

3. That the membership of the executive committee of
the proposed amalgamated union be fixed at 15,
- 6 each from the two unions to be amalgamated,
2 from the Chinese Labourers' Welfare Association
and 1 from the Shanghai Branch of the Social
Movement Direction Committee.

目前与南市总工会有关联的各工会头面人物。据称，任何成功收买此类人员的特工将获得100.00美元的奖励，而被收买者将获得200.00美元的津贴，虽无其他义务，但须在被要求时会见西区总工会的负责人，并公开表示对该工会的忠诚。

除了这一新尝试外，西区总工会的成员不久前曾接触南市总工会的负责人，请求合并这两个工会。南市总工会随即向日本特务机关请示指示，并决定了以下几点，据报道，这些要点已转交西区总工会审议：-

1. 本工会（南市工会）同意所提议的合并。

2. 拟议的合并后工会命名为“上海市工会整理委员会”
( 上海市工会整理委员会 )。

3. 拟议的合并后工会执行委员会成员定为15人，
- 两个待合并的工会各出6人，
中国劳工福利协会出2人，
社会运动指导委员会上海分会出1人。

Subject Nanking Government's attitude towards labour disputes
in the International Settlement.
Made by D.I. Kao Yen Ken Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

The General Labour Union, situated at Lane 95,
10 Edinburgh Road, took a very active part in the
trouble which led the workers of the Shanghai
Tramways, the China General Omnibus Company and the
French Tramway Company to declare a strike and this
Union had every intention of using those strikers
to further the movement in other public utility
concerns with the ultimate object of causing a
general strike in Shanghai. On September 27,
delegates of the strikers of the three concerns
involved suddenly called on Mr. Yu Ya Ching and
requested his mediation for an early settlement.
On September 28, the strikers of the Shanghai
Tramways and China General Omnibus Company did not
persist in their demands and an agreement was reached
whereby a settlement of the disputes was made possible.
It is learned that on receiving reports on the
labour situation in Shanghai, the Ministry of Social
Affairs of the "National Government" (Nanking)
detailed a special official named Koo Chi-woo
(顧繼武) to Shanghai who conveyed written
instructions to Chang Kuh-chong (張克昌), who
is actually in charge of the Shanghai Branch,
Social Movement Direction Committee, 75 Jessfield
Road, O.O.L. that every effort was to be made to
stop the labour agitation and there should be no
further strikes.

D.I. Kao
Int. 26/9

Following the strikes in the Shanghai Electric Construction Company, the China General Omnibus Company and the French Tramway Company, the executives of the General Labour Union, Lane 95, 10 Edinburgh Road, are reported to have conceived a plan to paralize all local public utility services. Rumours were current on September 25, that the workers of the Shanghai Waterworks would join the strike, and a number of people took the precaution of storing a quantity of water for emergency use.

It has been learned that recently, one Chang Kwan (张坤), an ex-worker of the Shanghai Power Company, who owns the Woo Kwang (滬光) Water and Electric Supply Shop at 330 Chemulpo Road, approached his friends in the Shanghai Water Works and succeeded in inducing some 260 workers to join a union which has an office at 4 Loh An Fang, Jessfield Road, O.O.L. This union is alleged to be sponsored by the 4th District Kuomintang (pro-Wang Ching Wei). Most of these members are young men, the older ones refusing to join the movement. They (the young men) have an idea to engineer a strike to enforce a set of demands for better treatment, but owing to the opposition of the older workers, the young workers are withholding action for the time being. Situation is being closely watched.

内部传阅 9月26日

继上海电力建设公司、中国公共汽车公司及法商电车公司罢工之后，据报位于爱丁堡路95弄的总工会执行层已策划一项旨在瘫痪本地所有公用事业服务的计划。9月25日流传着谣言，称上海自来水厂工人将加入罢工，许多人采取预防措施，储存了一定数量的水以备急用。

据悉，上海电力公司前雇员张坤（Chang Kwan），拥有位于杰弥逊路（Chemulpo Road）330号的“滬光”水电供应行，最近接触了他在上海自来水厂的朋友，并成功诱使约260名工人加入一个在极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）罗安坊4号设有办事处的工会。据称该工会由国民党第四区党部（亲汪精卫派）资助。这些成员大多为年轻人，年长者拒绝加入该运动。他们（年轻人）企图策划罢工，以强制实现一系列改善待遇的要求，但由于遭到老工人的反对，年轻工人目前暂不采取行动。当局正密切监视事态发展。

Some twenty Chinese claiming to represent
various local labour unions held a meeting in the
office of the General Labour Union, Lane 95, 10
Edinburgh Road, between 3 p.m. and 6 p.m. September
27, and discussed the incident in which the French
Police opened fire in connection with the strike of
the French Tramway Company. The following
resolutions were discussed and passed :-
1. That a protest in the joint names of local
labour unions be lodged with the French Consul-
General in Shanghai against the "illegal action"
taken by the French Police.
2. That the Administrative Yuan, the Ministry of
Social Affairs and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
of the "National Government" (Nanking) be
requested to take up the matter with the French
authorities.
3. That demands be put forward for the issue of
compensation to the injured, and the French
authorities be required to tender an apology
and give an assurance that the incident will
not be repeated.
4. That a circular manifesto be issued announcing
to the world public. the "illegal" actions of the
French authorities.
5. That a "French Tramway Company Workers Tragedy
Support Committee" be formed.
6. That the Shanghai branch, Social Movement Direction

NEWS
AUG 2 . 1940

General Labour
Union Opened

New Body Formed Here
Under Auspices of City
Government Officials

Adding to the long list of Chinese public bodies which have sprung up under the protection of Chinese authorities in occupied districts and the Japanese since the hostilities, two new organizations have just been inaugurated. One of them is the "Shanghai Special District General Labour Union" which is trying to "centralize" labour movements in Shanghai and to increase the wages of workers.

The inaugural meeting of the new labour union was held on Monday in the former Chinese Chamber of Commerce building in North Soochow Road, according to the "Sin Shun Pao". In the presence of officials from the Shanghai Special Municipality, leaders of the union met and resolved upon a number of questions including a circular telegram.

Foreshadowing that the new union will control Shanghai workers, the telegram expresses regret that in the past labour movement leaders here have not done their best for the workers. More than 1,000 persons including representatives of many small labour unions, are said to have been present at the meeting.

Want Foreign Settlements

The resolutions passed at the meeting include a telegram to Nanking asking that the foreign settlements in China be taken over; a petition to Nanking for a purging movement against bandits and for centralizing labour control in Shanghai; reduction of prices of rice through official efforts; conclusion of hostilities by Japan; the increase of wages of workers through official efforts to be made by the Shanghai Special Municipality; and establishment of factories to relieve the unemployed.

The Korean Youths' Corps was also recently organized here, states the same paper. There are more than 7,000 Koreans in Shanghai and they are now said to have been closely united. The new corps will co-operate with the Shanghai Youths' Corps, a Chinese organization. A preparatory committee meeting was recently held and at this meeting methods of organizing the corps were discussed. The exact mission of the new corps is not mentioned but it is said that it will work for the "New Order" in East Asia.

1940年8月2日

总工会开幕

新机构在此成立
受市政府官员支持

自战事爆发以来，在中国占领区当局和日本人的庇护下涌现出的中国公共团体名单又增加了两个新组织。其中之一是“上海特别区总工会”，该会正试图“集中”上海的劳工运动并提高工人工资。

据《申报》报道，新工会的成立大会于周一在北苏州路原中国商会大楼举行。在上海特别市官员的出席下，工会领导人会面并就包括通电在内的一系列问题作出决议。

预示新工会将控制上海工人，该通电对过去这里的劳工运动领袖未能为工人尽力表示遗憾。据说包括许多小工会代表在内的1000多人出席了会议。

要求收回外国租界

会议通过的决议包括：致电南京，要求收回中国在外国租界；向南京请愿，开展肃清匪徒运动并在上海集中劳工控制权；通过官方努力降低米价；日本结束敌对行动；上海特别市通过官方努力提高工人工资；以及建立工厂以缓解失业问题。

该报还称，朝鲜青年团近期也在此成立。上海有7000多名朝鲜人，据说他们现在紧密团结在一起。新军团将与中国的上海青年团合作。近期召开了一次筹备委员会会议，讨论了组建军团的方法。新军团的确切使命未被提及，但据说它将为东亚的“新秩序”工作。

(From a Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper) :-
SHANGHAI GENERAL LABOUR UNION INAUGURATED
Under the supervision of deputies from the
Social and Police Bureaux, the inaugural meeting of the
Shanghai General Labour Union was held at 9 a.m. August 26
in the premises of the Shanghai General Labour Union. In all
about 1,000 persons were present, amongst whom were
representatives of labour unions.
During the proceedings, members of the Executive
and Supervisory Committees of the Shanghai General Labour Union
took over their seats. The following decisions were then
passed :-
(1) That the Nanking Government be requested
to promulgate the Labour Law immediately.
(2) That the Nanking Government be requested
to bring about the recovery of Foreign Settlements.
(3) That the Government be requested to
suppress undesirable elements.
(4) That the Government be requested to
improve the administrative organs and abolish superfluous
organs.
(5) That the Labour movement in Shanghai be
unified.
(6) That the Japanese Government be requested
to bring about the cessation of the Sino-Japanese war.
(7) That the Nanking Government be requested
to reduce the price of rice and to deal with the problems
relating to the livelihood of labourers.
(8) That the Shanghai City Government order
industrial employers to improve the treatment accorded to
their labourers.
(9) That the Shanghai City Government be
requested to establish factories and afford relief to
unemployed labourers.
The Union has also issued a manifesto stating
that the puppet Chungking regime, which is surrounded by
Communists, was continuing the war of resistance but fortunately
President Wang Ching-wei was endeavouring to save the country
by means of peace movement, regardless of personal danger.

上海市总工会成立
在社会局和警察局代表的监督下，上海市总工会成立大会于8月26日上午9时在上海市总工会会所举行。共有约1000人出席，其中包括各工会代表。
会议期间，上海市总工会执行委员会和监察委员会成员就职。随后通过了以下决定：
(1) 请求南京政府立即颁布劳动法。
(2) 请求南京政府促成收回外国租界。
(3) 请求政府镇压不良分子。
(4) 请求政府改善行政机构并裁撤冗余机构。
(5) 统一上海劳工运动。
(6) 请求日本政府促成中日战争停止。
(7) 请求南京政府降低米价并处理与劳工生计有关的问题。
(8) 要求上海市政府命令工业雇主改善对待劳工的方式。
(9) 请求上海市政府建立工厂并为失业劳工提供救济。
该工会还发表宣言称，被共产党包围的重庆傀儡政权仍在继续抗战，但幸运的是，汪精卫主席不顾个人安危，正致力于通过和平运动救国。

The Western Branch Office at 5 Nan Shan
Tsung, Lane 877 Robison Road, O.O.L., was established
recently, on July 12, 1940 and its coming into being
can only be regarded as a step towards gaining a
footing in the Western District O.O.L. with a view
to counteracting the activities of the "Shanghai
General Labour Union". This branch office is
now contemplating the formation of a "Stall Keepers'
Mutual Aid Association".

The Chinese Labourers' Welfare Association
was formed under the auspices of the Japanese
Military Special Service Department for the purpose
of ultimately securing complete control over all
workers in local industrial concerns and is, therefore,
running against the interests of the "Shanghai General
Labour Union" mentioned in the preceding paragraph
which is striving to attain the same end. This
situation prompts the question; why these organizations
are allowed to function at the same time and in the
same sphere, by the Japanese Authorities under
whose respective organization they came into being.

To explain this contradictory state of
affairs, it would be necessary to examine the
problem of 'politics' involving the different
Japanese advisors, attached to the different
Japanese sponsored organizations, including the
"New Central Government", who maintain official
relations either with the Japanese Navy or the
Japanese Military and who are adopting an independent
policy whilst discharging their duties without
apparently being able to maintain uniformity of
action in so far as a 'Central Policy' in respect
of administration by official or semi-official
organs in the Japanese occupied area is concerned,
thereby resulting in disaccord among the functions
of the local Japanese sponsored organizations.

Translation of a petition made by the Various Trade
Association situated at 85 Soong Sih Ka, Nantao.

Re a dispute over wages between the Hen Foong Silk Filature
and workers.

We have to state that the above Association was formerly
organised in September 1939, the object of which was to
support a constant peace and anti-communist movements. The sole
purpose of the said Association is to improve work condition and
get a welfare for labourers.

There were 10 workers employed by the Heng Foong Silk Filature
23 Haichow Road, came to the Association and petitioned that owing
to the high cost of living the all workers of the above filature
would request the management to grant an increase in wages.
They also stated that a rice allowance and an increase in wages
have already been carried out by other filatures and only the above
filature failed to do, and instead of this the management had
dismissed some workers without any cause. In view of this they
requested the said Association to detail some officials in contact
with the management of the Heng Foong Silk Filature and their
workers re increase in wages.

After the above information was obtained we (Association)
immediately detailed two officials to the Heng Foong Silk
Filature and on their arrival the manager of the filature refused
to have an interview with the officials. Being afraid that the
workers of the said filature would have a "Tai Kung" strike, we
would again send some men to interview the manager of the said
filature in an endeavour to talk over increase in wages, and
until such time we send our representatives to the said filature

位于南市宋家街85号的各同业公会请愿书译文。

关于恒丰丝厂与工人之间的工资纠纷。

兹陈述，上述协会前于1939年9月组建，其宗旨为支持持久和平及反共运动。该协会的唯一目的是改善工作条件并为劳工谋取福利。

海州路23号恒丰丝厂雇用的10名工人来到本协会请愿，称因生活成本高昂，该丝厂全体工人请求资方增加工资。他们还指出，其他丝厂已实施米贴及加薪，唯独该丝厂未予执行，反而无故解雇部分工人。有鉴于此，他们请求本协会派遣官员与恒丰丝厂管理层及其工人就加薪事宜进行联络。

在获悉上述情况后，我们（协会）立即派遣两名官员前往恒丰丝厂，但丝厂经理拒绝会见官员。因担心该丝厂工人举行“怠工”罢工，我们将再次派人会见该丝厂经理，试图商谈加薪事宜，在此期间我们派代表前往该丝厂

Translation of...Translation of precis of circular letter No. Tsung 1 3 from
"Shanghai General Labour Union", Lane 95/10, Edinburgh Road.

June 25, 1940.

With reference to the labour movement in this municipality after the cessation of hostilities, the "Shanghai Labour Movement Co-operative Association" was formed by various labour unions sometime in May last year as an advisory organ in a transitional stage. With the return of the "National Government" to the Capital and materialization of national unity by means of peace movement in sight, the workmen representatives meeting held on June 23 passed a resolution to the effect that the provisional organization be reorganized as the "Shanghai General Labour Union" in accordance with the regulations governing the organization of public bodies, promulgated by the central authorities and with the approval of the Shanghai Office of the Social Movement Advisory Committee of the Ministry of Social Affairs, when the following committees were selected:-

Executive Committee: Yu Yao Ch'iu & 20 other members.
Wang Yu Hsiang & 6 other candidate members.
Supervisory Committee: Mei Kuo Chen & 8 other members.
Chih Pai Hsiung & 2 other candidate members.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 30 JUNE 1940）

The Union commences to function forthwith, with an office at Lane 95/10, Edinburgh Road. Apart from parties concerned having been notified, the Police Department, Shanghai Municipal Council is requested to note accordingly.

(Seal of): "Shanghai General Labour Union".

S.K. Ho:

E. P. Ini, The change in organization
or title was fully reported on
June 25.

CONFIDENTIAL

China Labour Movement Association.

The China Labour Movement Association originated
from the Labour Movement Section of the Special Service
Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and
National Salvation Army, 76 Jessfield Road. This
section came into existence in October, 1939 for the
purposes of exercising control over local labour.

During the later part of November, 1939, the
Labour Movement Section was renamed the "China Labour
Movement Association" (中華工人協進會), and
formally established offices at Lane 95, 10 Edinbourgn
Road, O.O.L. The staff consists of some ten persons
with the following committee members :

(1) CHANG KUH CHONG    Native of Kiating, aged 36, formerly
    (張克昌)           a committee member of the Shanghai
                       Postal Workers' Union, and a follower
                       of TU YUEH SUNG. He turned over to
                       the Wang Ching Wei clique sometime
                       in August, 1939 and was appointed in
                       charge of the Labour Movement Section
                       of the Special Service Corps of the
                       Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern
                       and National Salvation Army. Following
                       the reorganization of the Labour
                       Movement Section, he was appointed
                       chief of the "China Labour Movement
                       Association," and became chief of
                       the Labour Department of the new
                       Central Government at the beginning
                       of April, 1940.
pages.zh:
机密

中国劳工运动协会。

中国劳工运动协会起源于位于极司菲尔路76号的“中国国民党反共救国军”特别服务队劳工运动科。该科成立于1939年10月，旨在对本地劳工实施控制。

1939年11月下旬，劳工运动科更名为“中国劳工运动协会”（中華工人協進會），并在老闸捕房辖区爱丁堡路10号95弄正式设立办事处。职员约十人，委员如下：

(1) 張克昌 (CHANG KUH CHONG)    嘉定人，36岁，原上海邮务工会
    (張克昌)           委员，杜月笙追随者。他于
                       1939年8月间投靠汪精卫集团，并被任命为
                       “中国国民党反共救国军”特别服务队
                       劳工运动科负责人。劳工运动科改组后，
                       他被任命为“中国劳工运动协会”主任，
                       并于1940年4月初成为新中央政府劳工部
                       部长。

REGISTRY

D. C. "B"
E.

After the arrest and execution of Zi Ah Mei (徐阿梅)
and Wang Ziang Sung (王祥生), Chairman and Vice Chairman
of the Shanghai Municipality Communications, Water and
Electricity Workers' Federation, by the Japanese Military
Authorities in December, 1939, the federation has been
practically inactive.

At 10 a.m. January 12, 1940, Van Ih Feng (范一峰),
the newly appointed Chairman of the organisation convened
a general meeting of the members at the new office at No.
10, Lane 95 Edinburgh Road with a view to discussing
measures in connection with the readjustment of the
affairs of the federation, when a total of some 200
persons consisting chiefly of workers of the China General
Omnibus Company and the French Tramway Company, attended.
Van Ih Feng presided and addressed the attendance stating
that all committee members should remain at their posts
and should do their best to assist him in readjusting
the affairs of the organisation. As a preliminary step
towards this object, he gave instructions that all
members sign a pledge form pledging observance to the
regulations of the federation and another pledging their
support to the peace movement. The meeting terminated
at 1 p.m. January 12, 1940.

After the meeting responsible members were given
copies of the pledge forms for distribution among the
members under them.

1940年1月12日上午10时，该组织新任主席范一峰 (Van Ih Feng) 在爱丁堡路10号95弄的新办事处召开全体会员大会，讨论调整联合会事务的相关措施。出席会议者约200人，主要为中国公共汽车公司和法商电车公司的工人。范一峰主持会议并发表讲话，称所有委员应留任，并尽力协助他调整组织事务。作为实现这一目标的初步步骤，他指示所有成员签署一份保证书，承诺遵守联合会规章，并签署另一份保证书，承诺支持和平运动。会议于1940年1月12日下午1时结束。

Made by D.S.I. Mac Adie Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

On December 29, 1939, Sung Feng Kong (孙凤岗),
a departmental chief of the Special Service Corps of
the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National
Salvation Army, who was before June the same year
leader of the "Chinese Youths' Anti-Japanese and
Traitors-Extermination Iron and Blood Corps"
(中國青年反日鋤奸铁血軍 ), was placed under
arrest by the Japanese Gendarmerie together with
a number of his followers, including Wang An Lyi
(王阿二 ), chief of a section of the Special
Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-
Comintern and National Salvation Army at 145 San
Wa Village, Zi An Mei (徐阿梅), Chairman of
the Shanghai Municipality Communications, Water &
Electricity Workers' Federation (上海市交通水電工人联合会),
and Meng Ziang Sung (孟祥生), ex-conductor 400 of
the China General Omnibus Company and Vice-Chairman
of the foregoing federation. On the following
day, Wang An Lyi, Zi An Mei, Meng Ziang Sung together
with several others were executed on Chung San Road
while Sung Feng Kong together with members of his
family are detained at 76 Jessfield Road, headquarters
of the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang
Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army. Detailed
antecedents of these four persons will appear at the
end of the report.

After the arrest and execution of Zi An Lei
(徐阿梅) and Wang Ziang Sung (王祥生), Chairman
and vice-Chairman of the Shanghai Municipality Com-
munications, Water & Electricity Workers' Federation,
on December 30, 1939, the federation was removed from
1103 Connaught Road to No.10, Lane 95, Edinburgh Road,
S.G.D., and Che Van In Boong (范一峰), an ex-Kuo-
mintang member, has been appointed in charge of the
organization.

agitating for a strike in local public utility concerns.
However, with the removal of the two principal leaders,
the scheme is likely to be suspended for some time to
come.

Translation of a letter addressed to C.D.I. Sih Tse Liang.

December 19, 1939.

Dear Mr. Tse Liang,
We have not seen you for a long time and hope
that you are in good health.
We have participated in the peace movement and
are directing labour affairs with the sole purpose of
preserving the good order of society and effecting
amicable settlements of labour disputes. Definitely
we are not inciting labour agitation prejudicial to
peace and good order.
However, we have just learned that certain
persons are causing trouble by using our names.
We presume that this might have caused the misunder-
standing on the part of the Settlement authorities.
Since you have been executing duties relating to
political affairs for a number of years and since you
well know about our doings in the past, we write this
letter to you to acquaint you with the truth. If you
can appoint a man to come to house No. 10, Lane 95 Edinburgh
Road so that arrangements can be made for an exchange of
opinions from time to time, it will be so much the better.

(signed) Yui Yao Jui (余耀球)

It is reported that dilligent efforts are being
made by the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo
Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army
to secure control over labour circles in Shanghai.

various local industrial concerns and later obtain
concessions from the management on behalf of the
workers in settlement of the disputes.
Yu Yao Jiu (余耀秋), who is in charge of the
"Federation of Associations of Shop Employees of
Various Trades" which was formed in November under
the guidance of the Special Service Corps of the Chung
Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation
Army, is said to be taking an active role in directing
the present labour movement. It is said that he is
responsible for the recent agitation in the Tung Yih
Cotton Mill, 26 Mokanshan Road, and is contemplating
the extension of such agitation to other cotton mills
in the Western District. In this connection, he
is assisted by one Li Yu Meng (李雨孟), one of his
followers, who is reported to be residing at No. 110
Tsau An Pang, off Ferry Road, O.O.L.. Li is
responsible for the organization of the "Shanghai
Municipality Bristle Workers' Union", situated at No. 3
Lane 484, Brenan Road, O.O.L., in whose name a letter
was addressed to the W. H. Bolton Bristle Company,

Date December 13. 1939.
Subject. Chungking Government's secret agents reported actively cultivating
anti-Japanese feeling among cotton mill workers in Shanghai.
Made by. D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by. D.I. Crawford

With reference to the attached translation of
an extract from the Mainichi, dated 8.12.39, alleging
that the Chungking Government has secretly despatched
agents to Shanghai to create anti-Japanese feeling
among cotton mill workers and that workers of the
Wing On Cotton Mill had formed a "Workers Association
of the War of Resistance," discreet enquiries from
different directions fail to confirm the report.

Regarding Li Dzu Deung (李绶堂) and Tung Yuen
Ying (董元英) (a female), the two persons mentioned
in the newspaper as representatives of the Chungking
Government and the Third International in Shanghai,
the former is known to this office. He was the
vice-chairman of a "Shanghai Cotton Mill Workers'
National Salvation Association" (上海市纱厂工友救亡协会),
which was formed in September 1937 at 24 Poh Shing
Tsung, Kiaochow Road, O.C.L., and which wound up its
affairs voluntarily at the end of October, 1937.
In common with numerous other national salvation
bodies then in existence, this organization only
engaged in conducting propaganda in favour of the
war against Japan and achieved nothing else. Tung
Yuen Ying, the other person mentioned in the newspaper,
is not known to this office. Diligent efforts to
trace the present whereabouts of both persons have
been without result.

Jno Robertson
D.C. (Sp. Br.)

9/10/37 and
24/11/37.

呈报人：副督察长 廖仲坚 (Liao Chung Chien) 转呈人：督察长 克劳福德 (Crawford)

关于附译的1939年12月8日《每日新闻》(Mainichi) 摘录，该报声称重庆政府已秘密派遣特工前往上海，在棉纺厂工人中制造反日情绪，并称永安纱厂工人已成立“抗战工人协会”，经从不同方向进行谨慎调查，未能证实该报道。

关于报纸中提及的作为重庆政府和第三国际在上海代表的李绶堂 (Li Dzu Deung) 和董元英 (Tung Yuen Ying)（女）二人，本处对前者有所了解。他曾是“上海市纱厂工友救亡协会”的副主席，该协会于1937年9月在胶州路24号（老闸捕房辖区）成立，并于1937年10月底自愿结束事务。与当时存在的众多救亡团体一样，该组织仅从事抗日宣传，未开展其他活动。报纸中提及的另一人董元英，本处并不知晓。经努力追查这两人的目前下落，均无结果。

约翰·罗伯逊 (Jno Robertson)
副督察长（特别科）

December 8, 1939.

MAINICHI

CHUNGKING GOVERNMENT'S SECRET AGENTS ACTIVELY
AGITATING ANTI-JAPANESE FEELING AMONG
COTTON MILL WORKERS

The Chungking Government has
secretly dispatched to Shanghai a man named Li Zai Daung,
member of the Kuomintang, and a woman named Tung Yuen
Ying, a member of the Chinese Third Internationale, to
create anti-Japanese feeling among cotton mill workers.
In the middle of October about 30
male and female workers of the Wing On Textile Manufactur-
ing Company held a meeting and organized a body known
as the "Workers Association of the War of Resistance".
About 1,400 workers of six cotton mills, including the
Wing On Cotton Mill, the Sinkow Cotton Mill, the Dah
Foong Cotton Mill, the Dong Shing Cotton Mill and the
Naigai Cotton Mill, are reported to have joined this
organization.
The activities of this organization
will be the following:-(1) to remove traitors, (2) to
secure members, (3) to set buildings on fire, (4) to
support the Chungking Government, (5) to encourage the
spirit of the war of resistance, (6) to raise money, (7)
to recover lost territory, (8) to collect secret informa-
tion.

（批：Sp Br）

Made by D.S.I. MacAdie Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

At 10 a.m. December 6, 1939, some 170 persons
claiming to be representatives of workers of the China
General Omnibus Company, the Shanghai Electric
Construction Company and the French Tramway Company,
held a meeting in No.3, Zung Ngoh Li, Kong Ka Jao, off
Connaught Road, O.O.L., the office of the "Shanghai
Municipality Communication, Water & Electricity Workers'
Federation", and formally inaugurated the organization.
Zi Ah Mei ( 徐阿梅 ), an ex-worker of the
French Tramway Co. and a notorious labour agitator,
presided and addressed the attendance stating that the
new body had for its object the promotion of co-
operation between capital and labour of the public
utility concerns and should not be regarded by any
means as an instrument for labour agitation. He also
urged the members to unite in order that their aims
could be successfully attained.
Discussions then took place and the following
resolutions were passed :-
1. That advertisements be inserted in the Shun Pao,
Sin Wan Pao and Central China Daily News announcing
the stand of the new organization.
2. That the official despatches be submitted to the
Police Authorities of the foreign Settlements
reporting the inauguration of the new organization.
3. That the following demands be submitted to the local
public utility concerns :-

Date November 28, 1939.
Subject. Shanghai Municipality Communication, Water and Electricity Workers'
Federation.
Made by D.S.I. MacAdie Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

E.

It is reported that on the morning of November
26, 1939 an informal meeting was held in the Shanghai
Municipality Communication, Water & Electricity
Workers' Federation, No. 3 Zung Ngoh Li, Long Ka Jao
off Jessfield Road, when Zi An Mei (徐阿梅),
chairman of the organization, Wong Ziang Sung (王祥生),
ex-conductor No. 400 of the C.G.O. Company and an
assistant of Zi, and several others were present. As
a result of discussions, it was decided that members
who are suspected of conducting counter-espionage in
the organization on behalf of the public utility
concerns, the S.M.P. or the Chungking Government be
kept under vigilant surveillance in order to prevent
leakage of information regarding the activities of
the Federation.

The premises of the Federation are at present
guarded by some 20 armed guards from 76 Jessfield Road.
They are under the command of Kuh Soo Sung (高树森),
the ex-Chief of the Special Service Section of the
Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National
Salvation Army, which was situated in Zah Hwei Yao off
Ferry Road, O.C.L. and which was dissolved on November
23, 1939.

In accordance with the instructions of the
Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National
Salvation Army, the Federation recently formed an
intelligence section which is in charge of an officer

据报，1939年11月26日上午，在位于极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）旁龙家角（Long Ka Jao）宗吾里（Zung Ngoh Li）3号的“上海市公用事业交通、水电工人联合会”举行了一次非正式会议，该组织主席徐阿梅（Zi An Mei）、前中国公共汽车公司（C.G.O. Company）400号售票员兼徐的助手王祥生（Wong Ziang Sung）以及其他数人出席了会议。经讨论决定，对涉嫌代表公用事业公司、上海公共租界工部局警务处或重庆政府在该组织内进行反间谍活动的成员保持严密监视，以防止有关联合会活动的情报泄露。

目前，联合会的会址由来自极司菲尔路76号的大约20名武装警卫把守。他们由高树森（Kuh Soo Sung）指挥，高曾任位于外摆渡路（Ferry Road）旁扎辉瑶（Zah Hwei Yao）的“中国国民党防共救国军”特别服务处处长，该部队已于1939年11月23日解散。

The Labour Movement Section of the Special
Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-
Comintern and National Salvation Army, which is
in charge of Tsang Kuh Chong (張固忠), a committee
member of the local Postal Workers' Union, has now
assumed the title "Chung Hwa Labour Movement
Association"(中華工運協進會) and will operate
under the direction of the new Kuomintang of Wang
Ching Wei in similar capacity to the now defunct
General Labour Union. Tsang Kuh Chong, the officer
in charge, is a native of Kiating, aged 35. He
was formerly a follower of Chu Hsueh Fan(朱學範),
an ex-prominent labour figure in Shanghai and was
appointed by the Special Service Corps of the Chung
Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation
Army to handle the formation of a labour organisation
in the form of a general labour union in August, 1939.
Under the direction of Tsang Kuh Chong, a
"Shanghai Municipality Communication, Water, and
Electricity Workers' Federation" and a "Federation
of associations of shop Employees of various Trades"
have been formed with Zi Ah Mei(徐阿美) and Yu Yao
Jiu(余耀球) respectively in charge. Zi Ah Mei
is a labour agitator in the French Tramway labour
disputes while Yu Yao Jiu is a committee member of
the Dried Goods Shop Employees' Union and an ex-staff
